title: Junior Technical Project Coordinator
description:
Junior Technical Project Coordinator
Cambridge, ON

Arriscraft Canada Brick, a General Shale Brick Inc. company, is recognized as a leading manufacturer and supplier within the brick and stone industry, with a strong reputation for product quality, technical expertise, customer service, and long-standing support of the architectural, construction, dealer, and masonry communities. As part of this organization, the Junior Technical Project Coordinator will play an important role in supporting the sales, technical, customer service, and operations teams by helping ensure project information is accurate, timely, and aligned with the expectations of our customers and internal stakeholders.

Position Summary

The Junior Technical Project Coordinator plays an important support role within the sales, customer service, technical, and operations teams. This position is responsible for assisting with project documentation, drafting, estimating, quotations, shop drawings, production tickets, purchase orders, and technical information updates. The role requires strong attention to detail, a willingness to learn, and the ability to coordinate effectively with internal teams, customers, suppliers, production scheduling, and third-party fabricators.

Key Responsibilities

  • Prepare and assist with technical drafting, estimating, shop drawings, production tickets, quotations, and related project documentation.
  • Review drawings, specifications, measurements, and customer requirements to support accurate estimates, take-offs, and order preparation.
  • Assist with preparing purchase orders and coordinating required information with suppliers, vendors, and third-party fabricators.
  • Work closely with the Production Coordinator / Scheduler to ensure technical documentation, tickets, and order details are complete, accurate, and aligned with production timelines.
  • Support Customer Service by providing timely information, clarifications, documentation, and responses required to serve customers effectively.
  • Collaborate with the Sales Team to support project opportunities, pricing requests, product recommendations, technical questions, and customer follow-up.
  • Maintain and update technical resources including hatching patterns, seamless textures, product data sheets, technical references, and related sales or customer-facing materials.
  • Coordinate with third-party fabricators to confirm scope, drawings, measurements, lead times, pricing details, and fabrication requirements.
  • Assist with the preparation, review, and organization of project files to ensure accuracy, consistency, and proper documentation control.
  • Identify potential errors, missing information, or conflicts in drawings, estimates, tickets, or order details and escalate them for resolution.
  • Support continuous improvement efforts by helping streamline technical support processes, templates, documentation, and communication between departments.
  • Perform other related duties as assigned to support sales, operations, customer service, and production needs.

Qualifications and Experience

  • Post-secondary education in architectural technology, drafting, construction technology, engineering technology, design, estimating, or a related field is preferred.
  • Previous experience in drafting, estimating, technical support, construction materials, manufacturing, fabrication, or building products is an asset.
  • Working knowledge of drawings, specifications, measurements, take-offs, and technical documentation.
  • Experience with CAD and BIM modellingdrafting software (such as AutoCAD and/or Revit), estimating tools, ERP systems, order entry platforms, or related technical software is considered an asset.
  • Strong computer skills, including Microsoft Office applications and the ability to learn internal systems quickly.
  • Ability to read, interpret, and organize technical information with a high degree of accuracy.
  • A valid driver’s licence and reliable vehicle are required, as the successful candidate will be expected to meet with vendors and fabricators as required.

Required Skills and Competencies

  • Excellent attention to detail and commitment to accuracy.
  • Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple requests and priorities.
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills in English (French would be an asset)
  • Customer-focused approach with a professional and responsive attitude.
  • Ability to work collaboratively across sales, customer service, scheduling, production, and external fabrication partners.
  • Strong problem-solving skills and willingness to ask questions when clarification is required.
  • Ability to work in a fast-paced environment while maintaining quality and consistency.
  • Positive attitude, accountability, and willingness to learn technical product knowledge and internal processes.

Key Working Relationships

  • Sales Team
  • Customer Service Team
  • Production Coordinator / Scheduler
  • Estimating and Technical Support
  • Operations and Production Teams
  • Third-Party Fabricators
  • Suppliers and Vendors
  • Customers, as required

Success Profile

The successful candidate will be detail-oriented, technically curious, dependable, and service-minded. They will contribute to accurate project execution by supporting the flow of information between sales, customer service, scheduling, production, and fabrication partners, while developing the technical knowledge required to grow within the organization.

What We Offer

  • Comprehensive health benefits after three months of employment.
  • Company RRSP matching program after one year of employment.
  • Opportunities for career growth and advancement.
  • Ongoing product knowledge and professional development training.
  • Support from a dedicated customer service team and experienced management staff
  • Equal opportunity employment and a commitment to fair pay practices.

title: Environmental Consultant – Senior Level (Hybrid)
description:
The role – what you’ll do

Barr is seeking a senior environmental consultant to join our Minneapolis, Minnesota, team. In this hybrid role, you will support Barr’s environmental review and natural resources management efforts, primarily across the Midwest, by leading and supporting environmental review, permitting, and compliance projects for a variety of clients. You will work closely with clients and multidisciplinary teams to identify opportunities, scope and execute projects, and provide strategic and technical guidance related to environmental permitting and compliance. This includes supporting environmental resource characterization, impact assessments, mitigation planning, and construction monitoring.

The ideal candidate is a strong technical leader who combines deep regulatory expertise with excellent client service, business development acumen, and the ability to lead teams in a fast-paced, client-driven environment.


Your impact – key responsibilities

  • Project leadership and delivery: lead environmental review, permitting, and compliance projects, including forming teams, coordinating work execution, managing budgets and schedules, and helping ensure quality outcomes.
  • Environmental permitting and regulatory strategy: provide technical expertise and interpretation of state and federal regulations, including Minnesota-specific programs, to support permitting strategies and successful approvals.
  • Wetland and natural resource expertise: conduct and oversee wetland delineations, functional assessments, impact assessments, mitigation planning, and construction monitoring activities.
  • Leadership and office support: contribute to leadership efforts in Barr’s Minnesota offices, including strategic planning, staff development, and recruiting initiatives.
  • Team mentorship and development: guide and support junior staff while fostering a collaborative, high-performing team environment.

About the opportunity

  • Hybrid: a hybrid work arrangement may be considered for this position. A hybrid work arrangement refers to splitting time worked between a Barr office and a home office. This position can be based out of Barr's Minneapolis, Minnesota, office.

About you – required core competencies

  • Education: bachelor’s or master’s degree in environmental science, ecology, natural resources management, biology, or a related field
  • Technical Experience: 15+ years of direct, relevant experience in environmental permitting, review, and compliance
    • Expertise in conducting and overseeing wetland delineations, impact assessments, and mitigation planning for a variety of project sizes and complexities, ranging from large industrial clients to small individual landowners
    • Applied knowledge of state and federal wetland, stream and endangered species programs
    • Experience managing projects (i.e., forming teams, overseeing work execution, monitoring and controlling cost and schedule, implementing quality assurance and quality control, and stakeholder communications)
  • Strong interpersonal, oral, and written communication skills and the ability to communicate effectively with project team members and clients
  • Demonstrated ability to prepare and implement business development strategies
  • Driver’s license: possession of a current, valid driver’s license and acceptable driving record
  • Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without the need for sponsorship by Barr, now or in the future

Helpful additional experience (not required)

  • Advanced degree or specialized expertise in ecology, natural resources, or related disciplines.
  • Experience with project contracting or construction oversight
  • Experience negotiating with regulatory agencies
  • Experience with stormwater management, permitting, and compliance
  • Experience with the NEPA environmental review process
  • Experience with lake management including water quality and invasive species management

title: Sr. Test Technician
description:
Application close date:

Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the requisition is closed.

At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight!

This role is part of Blue Origin Operations, which is comprised of Integrated Supply Chain, Test Operations, Safety, Quality, and Mission Assurance. This includes Manufacturing and Supply Chain support across all Blue Origin facilities.

This role is part of the Blue Origin TEAM, where our focus is the design, development, manufacturing, and testing of Cryogenic systems. Built for multiple uses, our family of next generation of rockets for commercial, civil, national security, and human spaceflight. Your contributions will help ensure test readiness, data quality, and system reliability - directly supporting safe human spaceflight and sustained lunar exploration.


We are seeking a Senior Test Technician with deep expertise in helium mass spectrometry leak detection to support the inspection and qualification of cryogenic and high-pressure systems. In this role, you will ensure the integrity of critical propulsion and fluid systems, directly contributing to safe and reliable flight hardware.


This position will directly impact the history of space exploration and will require your commitment and detailed attention towards safe and repeatable space flight. Join us in lowering the cost of access to space and enabling Blue Origin’s vision of millions of people living and working in space to benefit Earth.

Responsibilities

  • Perform and lead helium mass spectrometry leak detection on cryogenic and high-pressure components, assemblies, and integrated systems
  • Develop, refine, and validate leak test procedures, acceptance criteria, and work instructions
  • Operate, calibrate, and maintain helium mass spectrometer leak detectors and associated vacuum/pressurization equipment
  • Diagnose and troubleshoot leak paths in welds, joints, seals, and fittings; recommend corrective actions
  • Interpret leak rate data and document results in compliance with engineering specifications and quality requirements
  • Provide technical mentorship and training to junior technicians and engineers
  • Collaborate with design, manufacturing, and quality teams to improve leak-tightness of hardware
  • Ensure adherence to safety protocols when handling cryogenics, testing high-pressure gases, and vacuum systems
  • Support root cause investigations for leak-related nonconformances

Minimum Qualifications

  • 8+ years of hands-on experience with helium mass spectrometry leak detection (vacuum and pressure/sniffer methods)
  • 8+ years of hands-on experience with instrumentation and data acquisition systems, including configuration, calibration, and monitoring (such as pressure, temperature, strain, and environmental sensors)
  • Strong understanding of vacuum technology, gas flow, and leak rate fundamentals
  • Experience testing cryogenic and/or high-pressure fluid systems
  • Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, schematics, and specifications
  • Familiarity with leak test standards (e.g., ASTM E499, ASTM E498, ASME BPVC Section V)
  • Strong troubleshooting and problem-solving skills

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in aerospace, propulsion, or spaceflight hardware environments
  • ASNT Level II or III certification in Leak Testing (LT) or Blue Origin equivalent
  • Experience with test data acquisition systems and statistical analysis
  • Knowledge of cleanliness requirements for oxygen and propellant systems
  • Familiarity with AS9100 systems

Culture Statement

Don’t meet all desired requirements? Studies have shown that some people are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single desired qualification. At Blue Origin, we are dedicated to building an authentic workplace, so if you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every desired qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

  • Required for Certain Job Profiles: Drivers who operate Commercial Motor Vehicles with a Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW), Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) or combination of power unit and trailer that meets or exceeds 10,001 lbs. and/or transports placardable amounts of hazardous materials by ground in any vehicle on a public road while in commerce, may be subject to additional Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations including: Driver Qualification Files, Medical Certification (obtained before onboarding), Road Test, Hours of Service, Drug and Alcohol Testing, vehicle inspection requirements, CDL requirements (if applicable) and hazardous materials transportation/shipping training.
  • Required for certain Job Profiles: Ability to obtain and maintain Merchant Mariner Credential, which includes pre-employment and random drug testing as well as DOT physical

Benefits

  • Stock Options for all regular employees (working at least 20 hours/week)

Bonus amounts and eligibility are not guaranteed and subject to change and cancellation. Please check with your recruiter for more details.

title: The Director, Global Scientific & Value Content - Payor
description:
Job Description

Job Summary:


The Director, Global Scientific & Value Content (Dir GSVC), position resides in the Value & Implementation (V&I) organization, which includes Global Medical and Scientific Affairs as well as Outcomes Research.


The Dir GSVC is responsible for, but not limited to, the following GSVC core functions, which have a global scope and impact:


  • Actively engaging with key stakeholders in the creation and adaptation of the V&I Planning and Scientific Platform, which provides the framework for GSVC Annual Product and Disease State Plans.
  • Developing and adapting annual GSVC plans for one or more products and disease states aligned with the annual V&I Plans.
  • Engaging key stakeholders and incorporating medical insights into GSVC annual product plans
  • Leading the development, review, approval, and communication of individual GSVC content within V&I.
  • The Dir GSVC will also provide a high degree of mentoring within a designated key complex TA.
  • The Dir GSVC will report directly into the Sr Director, Payor Team Lead, GSVC.

Responsibilities and Primary Activities:


Scientific Platform and Development of Global V&I and GSVC Annual Plans:


  • Shapes and informs the creation and adaptation of the V&I Plans and Scientific Platform.
  • Creates, adapts and prioritizes annual GSVC Product Plan(s) aligned with V&I Plan/Scientific Platform and informed through insights and feedback from key internal stakeholders cross-functionally and worldwide.
  • Executes GSVC Plans that include, but are not limited to, medical information letters, frequently asked questions (FAQs), disease- and product-related slide decks, global congress medical booth materials, and digital/web-based medical content.

Global Scientific & Value Content Development:


  • Authors or delegates the development of GSVC content that aligns to annual GSVC plan(s) and V&I Plans and Scientific Platform.
  • Reviews GSVC materials to ensure they are relevant, scientifically accurate, and consistent with cited appropriate scientific literature, internal scientific information, and company values and standards.
  • Ensures appropriate stakeholders are engaged in the development, review and approval of GSVC materials. For the Payor team, this includes attending CRT prioritization meetings and managing the submission, review and approval of CRT reviewed content.
  • Communicates to key stakeholders (e.g., Medical Information, Global Medical and Scientific Affairs Payor & Health System ) of GSVC approved content.
  • Drives creation of materials that can be leveraged globally as a strategic content partner of the Outcomes Research (OR); obtains insights on the payer landscape from countries and translates requirements.

Leadership and Mentoring:


  • Is a key subject-matter expert in a product or disease area to lead product-related projects/initiatives that directly impact the V&I Plan product strategy and objectives to meet external customer needs. Drives the solution of complex problems through identification of innovative solutions and is a go-to person within the core GSVC team for colleagues across stakeholder departments. Mentors/empowers or leads GSVC P3/P4 staff to develop within their functional roles.

Medical Education and Training:


  • Leads training to internal stakeholders on key GSVC-developed disease and product content in alignment and coordination with Knowledge Management and V&I Global Medical and Value Capabilities (V&I GMVC) Global Scientific Training (GST) team/Field Medical organization.

Cross-Functional Collaborations/Initiatives:


  • Partners with GSVC Team Lead and other key stakeholders [e.g., Publications, Medical Directors, Payor & Health System Medical Affairs Directors (P&HS-MADs) for Oncology, Compliance, Product Development Team (PDT), Outcomes Research] across the globe to ensure team assets are available and aligned with V&I and GSVC plans and meet the needs of external customers and internal stakeholders.
  • Builds collaborative relationships across divisions and regions as a global scientific partner with key stakeholders to provide broad impact and provide scientific resources that inform patient-care, formulary and treatment decisions. Leads and executes complex cross-functional initiatives independently, which directly contribute to the strategy and objectives of GSVC and the vision of broader V&I stakeholders.
  • Directs a multitude of partnerships, both within and outside the department, by identifying gaps and leading in areas where there is value added, such as creation of V&I/GSVC processes/departmental initiatives, standard operating procedure (SOP) authoring/updates, and cross-functional activities that contribute to the GSVC vision.
  • May lead one or more GSVC organization or V&I GMVC cross-organization initiatives or is a core member of broader V&I project teams.

Global Input Meetings


  • Coordinates with Global Expert Management and Strategy Consulting & Medical Education (GEMS) to provide appropriate coverage for group input meetings (GIMs) relevant to TA.
  • Participates as medical writer for GIMs aligned to priorities and responsibilities.

Additional Key Leadership Responsibilities:


  • Has a deep understanding of payors and health systems, including disease-state management, emerging trends, budget impact and cost effectiveness models, and competitive landscape.
  • Assists the GSVC Team Lead in resolution of escalations of complex issues/challenges by providing strategic guidance to GSVC team. Aids in ensuring that the objectives of the team are achieved for the global core functions.
  • Partners with GSVC Team Lead to collaborate with other V&I colleagues and medical/legal review (our Research & Development Division) cross-functional teams and stakeholders [e.g., Publications, Scientific Affairs, Medical Directors, MSLs, Compliance, PDT, Outcomes Research] worldwide, to ensure implementation of strategic initiatives for the assigned franchises across deliverables of the GSVC Team.
  • Has a deep understanding of own therapeutic area including product knowledge, disease-state management, emerging therapies, and the competitive landscape. With extensive experience, applies developed depth and breadth of disease, product and process expertise and helps to solve unique and complex problems/inquiries specific to the brands within the team.
  • Anticipates internal/external business and information needs and regulatory/compliance issues; takes leadership role in decision-making with the GSVC Team Lead and develops cross-functional strategy and tangible solutions within functional, company and industry guidelines.
  • As needed, provides internal/external insights into other Global and V&I GMVC teams [e.g., GDMA, Global Medical Information (GMI), P&HS field team], as well as ensures that input is represented in the creation of the Scientific Platform. The Dir GSVC ensures consistent approach to use of GSVC within the team.
  • Assists GSVC Team Lead in conducting quantitative and qualitative analyses and reporting of insights.
  • Mentors newly hired V&I GMVC team members; leads onboarding and training of core functions for P3/P4 GSVC team members; and assists GSVC Team Lead in continued development of the team.
  • Helps lead departmental initiatives that have impact on GSVC process improvements and fosters innovation and cross-functional collaborations.
  • Endorses change to enable department to successfully adopt transitions that drive better individual and organizational performance and outcomes.

Required Qualifications, Skills and Experience:


Minimum:


  • MD/PharmD/PhD, plus minimum of five years of relevant Medical Affairs experience (e.g., medical communications, medical information, medical liaison, publications); OR MSN, BS degree in Pharmacy, MS degree in Life Sciences, plus minimum 10 years of relevant Medical Affairs experience; OR BS degree in Nursing, Life Sciences, plus minimum 15 years of relevant Medical Affairs experience.
  • Extensive knowledge of healthcare systems and payor process/environment
  • Relevant working experience in Medical Affairs or Outcomes Research in the pharmaceutical industry.
  • Exhibited leadership via initiatives, mentoring, process improvements, and innovation.
  • Strong scientific writing/verbal communication skills.
  • Proven ability to network, prioritize, and cross-functionally collaborate.
  • Organizational and prioritization skills.
  • Multi-tasking and problem-solving skills (solution-driven).

Preferred:


  • Advanced degree (MD, PharmD, PhD).
  • Exposure to Global health systems and payer organization subject matter expertise and knowledge of trends and new information impacting delivery of care and access globally.
  • Experience leading the development of multiple Global or Regional Medical/Scientific Affairs Plans.
  • Experience with promotional review or medical/legal review activities.
  • Ability to develop or deliver scientific content for purpose of scientific exchange with external customers.
  • Ability to negotiate with cross-functional teams.
  • Prior experience working across geographies with different regulation/compliance requirements.
  • Extensive knowledge across multiple related therapeutic areas.
  • Proven leadership and influence/negotiation skills for interaction with cross-functional teams.
  • Strong analytical skills and ability to translate strategy into action plans.
  • Strong track record of mentoring.
  • Ability to work in a complex organization and effectively operate in a global and team-oriented structure.

title: Data Scientist
description:
Data Scientist

The Opportunity:

As a data scientist, you’re excited at the prospect of unlocking the secrets held by a data set, and you’re fascinated by the possibilities presented by IoT, machine learning, and artificial intelligence. In an increasingly connected world, massive amounts of structured and unstructured data open new opportunities. As a data scientist at Booz Allen, you can help turn these complex data sets into useful information to solve global challenges. Across private and public sectors—from fraud detection to cancer research to national intelligence—we need you to help find the answers in the data.


On our team, you’ll use your analytical skills and data science knowledge to create real-world impact. You’ll work closely with your clients to understand their questions and needs, and then dig into their data-rich environments to find the pieces of their information puzzle. You’ll develop algorithms and systems and use the right combination of tools and frameworks to turn sets of disparate data points into objective answers to help clients make informed decisions. Ultimately, you’ll provide a deep understanding of the data, what it all means, and how it can be used.


Work with us as we use data science for good.


Join us. The world can’t wait.


You Have:

  • 2+ years of experience with data exploration, data cleaning, data analysis, data visualization, data engineering or data mining
  • 2+ years of experience with statistical and general-purpose programming languages for data analysis
  • Experience analyzing structured and unstructured data sources
  • Experience developing predictive data models, quantitative analyses and visualization of targeted data sources
  • Experience building robust and scalable data engineering pipelines with diverse datasets and data types
  • Experience working with LLMs including Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) and AI Agents
  • Knowledge of Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, or Natural Language Processing
  • Secret clearance
  • Bachelor’s degree in a STEM field

  • 2+ years of experience in the development of algorithms leveraging Python, R, Typescript or SQL and NoSQL
  • 2+ years of experience with Distributed data or computing tools, including MapReduce, Hadoop, Hive, EMR, Kafka, Spark, Gurobi, or MySQL
  • 2+ years of experience with Machine Learning, AI or NLP
  • Experience working with Maven Smart System (MSS)
  • Experience working with logistics optimization models leveraging discrete optimization algorithms and routing models
  • Experience working with geospatial datasets
  • Experience working with logistics or supply chain datasets
  • Experience with visualization packages, including matplotlib, Plotly, Seaborn, or ggplot2
  • TS/SCI clearance with a polygraph
  • Master’s degree in a STEM field

title: Graduate Cyber Security Analyst (Cyber Academy)
description:
McKesson is an impact-driven, Fortune 10 company that touches virtually every aspect of healthcare. We are known for delivering insights, products, and services that make quality care more accessible and affordable. Here, we focus on the health, happiness, and well-being of you and those we serve – we care.

What you do at McKesson matters. We foster a culture where you can grow, make an impact, and are empowered to bring new ideas. Together, we thrive as we shape the future of health for patients, our communities, and our people. If you want to be part of tomorrow’s health today, we want to hear from you.

Are you passionate about protecting digital assets and eager to launch your career in the world of cybersecurity? Join our team at McKesson, a leading organization in the healthcare industry, where cybersecurity plays a critical role in safeguarding sensitive information and ensuring operational resilience. As an Associate Cybersecurity Engineer, you will serve as a contributing member of McKesson's cybersecurity organization from your first day of employment. Through a structured 24-month rotational program, you will apply your technical skills to solve real business challenges, deliver meaningful cybersecurity outcomes, and gain experience across multiple cybersecurity disciplines.


Join us in our mission to fortify our digital landscape and protect our assets. Apply today to embark on an exciting journey in cybersecurity with McKesson through our Cyber Academy, where your career potential can truly flourish.


What You’ll Do:

• Analyze security events, vulnerabilities, and threat intelligence to assess risk and develop recommendations for mitigation and continuous improvement.

• Evaluate cybersecurity controls, policies, and procedures and contribute to initiatives that enhance enterprise security capabilities.

• Participate in incident investigations, root cause analysis, and post-incident reviews to strengthen organizational resilience.

• Design, develop, or enhance security automation solutions using scripting languages such as Python, Bash, or JavaScript.

• Collaborate with cybersecurity, infrastructure, cloud, and application teams to identify security risks and implement effective controls.

• Integrate security best practices throughout the Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) and support security tooling within CI/CD environments.

• Analyze identity and access management processes and contribute to the design and improvement of access governance and security controls.

• Participate in strategic projects across multiple cybersecurity domains, gaining exposure to enterprise security operations, engineering, governance, risk management, and emerging technologies.

• Own and deliver assigned cybersecurity objectives, work products, and recommendations with guidance from experienced cybersecurity professionals while demonstrating increasing independence throughout the program.


What We’re Looking For:

• A recent graduate within the last 12 months with a bachelor’s or master’s degree in Cybersecurity, Information Technology, Computer Science, or a related field.

• Demonstrated ability to analyze complex technical information, identify risks, and develop practical recommendations to address cybersecurity challenges.

• Ability to exercise sound judgment, manage multiple priorities, and work independently while collaborating effectively within cross-functional teams.

• Preferred certifications: CompTIA Security+ or equivalent.

• Proficiency in one or more scripting or programming languages such as Python, Bash, JavaScript, PowerShell, or similar technologies.

• Excellent communication skills and the ability to work effectively in a team environment.

• Strong analytical skills and attention to detail.

• Ability to work onsite 2–3 days per week at the assigned McKesson location.


Why Join the Cyber Academy?

• Engage in a program specifically designed for early career talent, providing a supportive environment for new college hires and interns.

• Contribute to enterprise-scale cybersecurity initiatives that protect critical healthcare systems, applications, and data.

• Benefit from comprehensive training resources and mentorship opportunities.

• Network with professionals and peers in the cybersecurity field.

• Experience a company culture that values diversity, innovation, and teamwork.

Job Summary

This position supports initiatives related to energy efficiency/demand response evaluation, measurement & verification (EMV), regulatory compliance and operational support for portfolio planning and regulatory reporting purposes. Responsibilities include the creation of analytics for product development and regulatory filing requirements emphasizing energy efficiency (EE) and demand response by providing project management and technical expertise on special projects requested of the Analytics department. Individuals in this role may help draft testimony, create filing exhibits for regulatory proceedings and compliance, and present EMV results to respective regulatory bodies.


Responsibilites

  • Assist in the development of Energy Efficiency / Demand Response / Direct Load Control strategy and programs.
  • Evaluate the value of and propose changes to enhance the value of energy efficiency and demand response programs.
  • Support the development of regulatory applications and filings concerning energy efficiency and demand response programs.
  • Support analysis and may help draft testimony on policy positions as well as analytical results as required relative to energy efficiency and demand response programs.
  • Track and evaluate federal, state, and local policies related to energy efficiency and demand response programs.
  • Routinely meet and communicate with internal project developers, program managers and stakeholders, as well as third party evaluators and consultants to stay abreast of market information.
  • Review and provide input into EMV plans and schedules.
  • Review EMV Impact and Evaluation reports and associated EMV deliverables for accuracy and compliance.
  • Communicate & present results from EMV reports and preliminary findings.
  • Help track EMV reports and recommendations, regulatory orders regarding EMV, and other EMV commitments.
  • Help prepare presentations for external stakeholders summarizing EMV results.
  • Support other areas of the company with advanced technical expertise (e.g., Strategic Planning, Asset Planning, Products & Services, Rates).
  • Work with internal customers to provide analytical support for program design and implementation. Provide expertise to project teams and other areas within the company.
  • Proactively seek opportunities to support internal and external customers.
  • Assist program managers with understanding the relationship of EMV with program objectives, insights, campaign results, and participation.
  • Educate and consult with retail EE program teams on EMV processes and application of EMV results.
  • Provide support for program managers offering new or revised versions of programs. Guide the program managers to provide the information necessary to evaluate the new or changed features of the measures/programs.

Basic/Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's Degree in Engineering, Market Research, Finance, Statistics, Business, or Economics
  • Minimum 3 years of related work experience
  • In Lieu of a Bachelor's Degree, and High School Diploma/GED and 7 years of related work experience

Preferred Qualifications

  • Knowledgeable in statistical methodologies, DSM cost-effectiveness analysis, financial analysis, and marketing effectiveness measurement
  • Ability to communicate clearly, both written and verbally
  • Ability to efficiently analyze data
  • Good interpersonal / team skills
  • Demonstrated effective work habits, e.g. displaying initiative and persistence in carrying out work assignments, seeking to continually improve knowledge and skills, knowledge and innovation in support of continuous improvement and enhanced productivity.
  • Experience in regulatory approval and review process
  • Experience in presenting and defending testimony
  • Highly organized, detail-oriented, and able to shift priorities based on evolving deadlines

The work we do every day allows us to discover key insights and break new ground to create some of the most meaningful technologies that have a lasting impact on companies, industries, and society. One of business segments is called Life Science Optics, the other Life Science Fluidics and we are looking to add more talent to the team.

IDEX HEALTH & SCIENCE, LLC:

IDEX Health & Science is the global leader in life science fluidics, microfluidics, and optics, offering a three-fold advantage to customers by bringing optofluidic paths to life with strategic partnerships, solutions, and expertise. As one of the few companies in the world with component, sub-system, and application-level experts, IDEX Health & Science helps instrument developers solve the most demanding fluidic and optical challenges in a wide array of applications. We work hard to maintain a culture where you can own your work; you are encouraged to try new ideas in a collaborative environment; and you can apply your skillset to enable our clients to gain a competitive advantage in their own market. At IDEX Health & Science, you have the opportunity to work with a great group of people, mentor others, and build a great future.

Operational Leadership

  • Work cross functionally on initiatives that improve efficiency, reduce waste, increase throughput, and enhance overall operational effectiveness.
  • Identify root causes of operational variances and implement sustainable corrective and preventive actions.
  • Champion operational change management efforts to ensure successful adoption of new systems, processes, and best practices.

Operational Excellence & Quality

  • Maintain compliance with ISO requirements and support all internal and external audits, corrective actions, and employee training initiatives.
  • Partner with Quality and lead Manufacturing Engineering teams to drive process capability, product quality, and regulatory compliance.
  • Lead preventive maintenance strategies that maximize equipment reliability, uptime, and manufacturing performance.

Safety & Environmental Leadership

  • Foster a culture where safety is a core organizational value.
  • Partner with EHS Leader to develop and implement proactive safety, ergonomic, and risk-reduction programs to prevent workplace injuries and incidents.
  • Ensure compliance with all applicable safety, environmental, and regulatory requirements.
  • Drive continuous improvement in safety performance through employee engagement, training, and accountability.

Supply Chain & Inventory Management

  • Partner with Supply Chain leadership to optimize sourcing strategies, inventory performance, supplier relationships, and material flow.
  • Implement effective inventory management practices that improve working capital performance while maintaining service levels.
  • Drive improvements in ERP utilization and system functionality to support operational efficiency and informed decision-making.

Financial & Strategic Management

  • Lead the development and execution of Annual Operating Plans, operating budgets, and strategic initiatives.
  • Assume overall accountability for manufacturing profitability, cost performance, productivity, and operational efficiency.
  • Evaluate and justify capital investments that support capacity expansion, process improvements, safety enhancements, and strategic growth.
  • Ensure facilities, equipment, and operational infrastructure support both current business requirements and future growth objectives.

Leadership & Talent Development

  • Serve as the Site Leader for the Middleboro, MA site including oversight and engagement of the IH&S and IDEX MPT (Materials Processing Technologies) teams. While this role has direct accountability for the IH&S Operations at the site, this leader will also indirectly oversee the MPT teams at the site and partner with the MPT Leadership team on site related needs and activities for that business.
  • Lead, coach, and develop direct and indirect team members to maximize engagement, performance, and career growth.
  • Build high-performing teams through effective recruitment, onboarding, training, succession planning, and talent development practices.
  • Maintain clear accountability and performance expectations across all operational functions.
  • Lead the site through all elements of the IDEX Operating Model, including Daily Management, Goal Deployment, Monthly Business Reviews, 80/20 Focus, and the Organization & Talent Cycle.
  • Collaborate effectively across functions to foster alignment, teamwork, and business success.

Education & Experience Required

  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Operations Management, Business, Supply Chain, or a related field.
  • 10+ years of progressive manufacturing operations leadership experience, including leadership of multiple operational functions.
  • Proven track record of driving operational improvements, productivity gains, quality enhancements, and cost reductions.

Preferred

  • Lean Certification, Six Sigma Certification, or equivalent continuous improvement credentials.
  • Experience within a highly regulated manufacturing environment.
  • Experience leading ERP optimization and business system improvement initiatives.

Knowledge, Skills & Competencies

  • Demonstrated success leading manufacturing operations with measurable and sustainable business results.
  • Strong expertise in Lean Manufacturing, Continuous Improvement, Operational Excellence, and Change Management.
  • Strategic thinker with the ability to translate business objectives into executable operational plans.
  • Proven ability to lead organizational transformation and drive adoption of new processes and systems.
  • Strong financial acumen with understanding of operational impact on growth, profitability, working capital, and cash flow. Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills.
  • Strong knowledge of ERP systems and manufacturing planning tools.
  • Ability to influence and collaborate effectively across departments and organizational levels.
  • Highly effective communicator with exceptional verbal, written, and presentation skills.
  • Results-oriented leader with a strong sense of accountability, urgency, and ownership.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage conflict, build relationships, and lead high-performing teams.

title: Supply Management Specialist

As a defense mission professional, you ask questions others don’t. You understand the nuances of complex situations. You use your skills to think bigger and push further, solving complex problems. We’re looking for an expert like you to create solutions for missions that keep our nation safe.


As the Supply Management Specialist, you are an expert in military food service and field feeding operations, your deep technical background enables you to shape modernization, enhance readiness, and strengthen operational feeding capabilities across the force. title: Network Engineer, Senior
description:
Network Engineer, Senior

The Opportunity:

A well-designed network is critical to move data and enable organizations to achieve their missions, but how can an organization make sure their network will fit their current and evolving needs? Crafting the right network, with the right equipment and software, requires a combination of technical skill and careful planning. That’s why we need you, a network engineer who knows how to develop the exact network the DoD needs.


As a Satellite Communications Network Engineer on our team, you will help develop, modernize, and sustain secure and resilient network capabilities that support critical defense operations. You’ll use your skills in network design, architecture, Layer 2/3 technologies, and system interoperability to improve reliability, availability, and performance across mission‑focused environments. You will also contribute to engineering efforts including implementation planning, technical reviews, test activities, and upgrades supporting enterprise‑wide modernization.


You’ll apply your knowledge in routing and switching, network design and architecture, IP engineering, network transport layers, updating network equipment, and performance monitoring as you join our team of problem-solvers to help the DoD evolve and deploy new capabilities and technologies. Your knowledge of network protocols, equipment, emerging technology, and configurations will come in handy as you help optimize client operations and modernization initiatives. Using your experience in Cisco, Juniper, and other COTS hardware and network performance management, and your technical curiosity and knowledge of industry standards, you’ll serve as a trusted advisor to clients on mission-critical projects and make an impact on national security missions.

Grow your career with us as we help the DoD field and sustain satellite communications capabilities to provide data and voice solutions to tactical and strategic users of worldwide network of SATCOM Gateways and Teleports.

Join us. The world can’t wait.

You Have:

  • 8+ years of experience with IP networking design and troubleshooting
  • 8+ years of experience architecting and designing complex network systems and leading the testing and deployment of systems or solutions
  • 8+ years of experience with Cisco switches, routers, and firewalls set up and configuration

description:
Chicago Metropolitan Fire Prevention
Full-Time | First Shift | Monday–Friday

The Alarm Technician II is an experienced field technician within our company's Alarm Division. This role is responsible for performing Alarm Systems Installation, Service, as well as making Corrective repairs with increasing independence. Alarm Technician II technicians are expected to identify deficiencies, complete approved repairs, and verify systems are restored to proper operation in accordance with NFPA codes, manufacturer requirements, and company standards.

  • Support and mentor Alarm Technician I team members through on-the-job guidance
  • Follow all safety procedures, company policies, and customer site requirements

  • High school diploma or GED
  • Minimum of 3 years of Alarm Installation, Inpection, Testing and Service experience (or equivalent progression from Alarm Technician I)
  • Working knowledge of Alarm Systems, devices, and basic circuitry
  • Ability to read and interpret inspection reports, device layouts, and system documentation
  • Comfortable working independently in the field while escalating complex issues as needed

Preferred Qualifications:

  • NICET Level I or Level II in Fire Alarm Systems or active pursuit of certification
  • Experience with common fire alarm panels and manufacturers
  • Familiarity with NFPA 72 and local AHJ requirements
  • Prior experience performing corrective repairs following inspections

  • Ability to lift and carry up to 50 pounds

title: V.I.E - Supply Chain Planner
description:
What is a VIE?


It’s an international graduate program for European citizens having graduated from a University School. This is an initiative created, designed, and supported by the French Government primarily to provide professional international work experience for European citizens aged between 18-28 recently graduated from University or Business School.

To apply for this V.I.E assignment you need to fulfil the following criteria:

  • International Graduates (European citizens) between 18 - 28 yo with an average of 12 months of professional experience
  • Higher education level (master’s degree)
  • Fluent in English
  • International profile (work experience or studies abroad)
  • Eager to continue your career abroad

This is a V.I.E position based in Stockholm, Sweden and lasts 12 months with possibility for extension of another 12 months. The position is not open to applicants already based in Stockholm, Sweden. For more information on the V.I.E program’s specificities please visit Mon Volontariat International : site officiel du V.I.E | V.I.A (businessfrance.fr).

ABOUT US


Pernod Ricard is a global leader in the spirits industry, with a portfolio of renowned brands including Absolut, Ricard, Ballantine’s, Chivas Regal, Jameson, Martell, Havana Club, Beefeater, Malibu, Mumm and Perrier-Jouët. In the Nordics, the Group combines its international expertise with strong local market knowledge to bring these brands to customers and consumers through tailored commercial and brand activations.


We aim to redefine the global spirits market by inspiring people from all backgrounds to connect, share ideas and enjoy our products responsibly. We are also committed to long-term sustainability, acting in the best interests of consumers, society, the environment and our employees.


We seek talented, bold individuals to join our team and drive innovation. After all, our brands are defined by lifestyle and mindset, but it is our people who define who we are. So, whether you are just starting your career or looking to take it to the next level, we offer a dynamic and supportive work environment that will help you grow.

ABOUT THE ROLE


Are you passionate about working for a global leader that brings iconic brands to consumers across the Nordics? Do you want to be part of an international and inclusive team that values collaboration, creativity and fun? Then look no further than Pernod Ricard Nordics, where conviviality is more than just a value – it's a way of life.


At the heart of our Swedish operations, this role helps keep products moving smoothly from forecast to delivery and, where relevant, supports other Nordic markets. Reporting to the Head of Supply Chain, the V.I.E Supply Chain Planner plays an active role across planning, inventory optimisation, logistics and performance analysis in an international FMCG environment. A key priority will be supporting the transition to a new third-party logistics provider while ensuring business continuity and service levels. To make this happen, you will work closely with Supply Chain, Sales, Marketing, Finance, Customer Service, Pernod Ricard production and supply entities, and logistics partners.


KEY TASKS & RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Help drive the monthly demand and supply planning process for Sweden and, where relevant, other Nordic markets.
  • Turn demand forecasts into clear supply requirements and coordinate replenishment with Pernod Ricard production and supply entities.
  • Keep a close eye on inventory, shortages, excess and slow-moving or obsolete stock, recommending actions that balance availability, working capital and stock coverage.
  • Bring meaningful analysis and reporting to the monthly S&OP process, highlighting risks and opportunities affecting availability and inventory.
  • Coordinate supply planning for new launches, limited editions and phase-in/phase-out, aligning quantities and timelines with Sales, Marketing and operational teams.
  • Play an active part in the transition to a new 3PL, supporting the operational setup, inventory transfer and reconciliation, risk mitigation, KPI tracking and post-go-live stabilisation.
  • Keep Sales, Marketing and Customer Service informed with timely updates on product availability.
  • Track key Supply Chain KPIs—including forecast accuracy, service level, inventory coverage, out-of-stock and slow-moving inventory—and turn insights into continuous improvement actions.

WHY JOIN US

We aspire to foster an authentic, open, challenging and innovative culture that supports your long-term professional development. And so, we have created a working environment at Pernod Ricard that allows you to thrive.

We champion inclusion and value different perspectives. We want our people to be their own authentic selves and we are committed to building a workplace that reflects our global consumer base. We are proud to be recognised among Forbes World's Best Employers and Equileap's top 100 Employers for Gender Equality. Conviviality is in our DNA and connects us beyond borders – you will always be welcomed for who you are and the strengths you bring.

This role could be for you if you:

  • Hold a Master’s degree in Supply Chain, Logistics, Engineering, Business or a related field.
  • Have initial experience in Supply Chain, Planning, Logistics or Operations.
  • Understand demand & supply planning, inventory management and Supply Chain KPIs.
  • Are comfortable with Excel and data analysis; knowledge of planning or ERP tools is a plus.
  • Are organised, proactive and solution-oriented, with strong attention to detail.
  • Enjoy working in a fast-paced, international environment and communicating in English (Swedish not required).

OUR OFFER

We want to help you through everyday challenges, encourage you to make healthy choices, take care of your well-being and enjoy work-life balance (we have a great canteen and a well-equipped gym in case you want to shake the day off!). We also provide you with opportunities for professional development and career progression that you’d expect from a global leader in the beverage industry.

Read more about us at Careers | The Absolut Group (theabsolutcompany.com)

APPLICATION

If this role sounds like it is for you, don’t hesitate to apply. As an international company, our working language is English, so please submit your application in English. All new employees are subject to a six-month probationary period and some positions may require a background check.

We look forward to hearing from you.

As a skills-based organisation, we ensure fair processes and equal opportunities. If you need extra support or accommodation during the recruitment process, please contact us. We are here to support you and welcome your application.

title: Defense Congressional Analyst, Mid

title: Software Development Engineer - Shopping Personalization AI, Amazon Stores
description:
Amazon's Personalization organization builds the AI systems behind how hundreds of millions of customers discover and shop. We extract and reason over customer signals in real time, power LLM-driven recommendation experiences, and build AI-native discovery surfaces that combine products, content, and contextual recommendations. Our work sits at the intersection of generative AI, large-scale distributed systems, and customer-facing products, delivered through high-performance web and mobile experiences at Amazon scale.

In this role you'll design and build features that shape how customers discover products - tailored to their preferences, helping them find exactly what they need, even before they know they need it. We're defining how LLMs integrate into real-time personalization, how noisy behavioral signals become durable customer understanding, and how AI-powered experiences ship reliably at scale. You'll work across multiple technical teams, ship iteratively, and see your work in the hands of customers quickly. This organization values experimentation, moves fast, and gives engineers real ownership over what they build.

We are looking for a Software Development Engineer with sound technical judgment and a bias for action who takes ownership of problems end to end, communicates clearly, and cares about operational excellence - not just launching features, but making sure they hold up at scale. Someone who naturally raises the bar for the team: mentoring junior developers, advocating engineering best practices, and thinking beyond the immediate sprint.

Key job responsibilities
- Design, build, test, and operate production AI features used by multiple teams and operating at Amazon scale
- Deliver end-to-end solutions with focus on maintainability, scalability, performance, and reliability
- Collaborate with Product and Science to define experiences, run experiments, and iterate based on data
- Build AI-powered experiences including personalized recommendations, relevance explanations, and knowledge-driven features using LLMs and generative AI
- Define and implement measurement strategies including analytics events and experiment configurations to track engagement and retention
- Navigate ambiguity and make sound technical decisions in a problem space where established patterns don't always apply

About the team
Our team is part of Amazon's Personalization organization, a high-performing group that leverages Amazon's expertise in machine learning, big data, distributed systems, and user experience design to deliver the best shopping experiences for our customers.

Our vision is to enhance customer shopping experience on Amazon by leveraging personalization techniques. We strive to save customers valuable time by tailoring their journey to their individual needs, interests, and preferences. Our goal involves identifying personalization opportunities to develop and optimize customer experiences, thereby improving the overall search and discovery process across Amazon.

description:

If you’ve been in the BAS world a while, you know the difference between a job that just keeps you busy and one that keeps you engaged, respected, and growing.

At Automated Logic, a Carrier Company, our Managers describe this as the place where they finally found both challenge and balance. A place that trusts your judgment, values your craftsmanship, and gives you the tools and autonomy to make an impact.

As a Field Service Supervisor, you’ll be the expert voice on-site — a professional with deep knowledge and highly developed technical expertise in Field Service work. You’ll be counted on to deliver the kind of precision work our customers remember.

Our long-tenured people put it simply:

“I finally found it. Not just a job. Not just a paycheck. A work home.”

If that sounds like what you’ve been looking for, we’d like to welcome you home too.

At Automated Logic, we believe in investing in our people. As a Supervisor, you’ll have access to:

● Professional Development: Training programs, certifications, and continuing education in BAS technologies and leadership.

● Career Pathways and Leadership Opportunities: Opportunities to advance into other roles as well as mentor junior staff and contribute to strategic initiatives that shape our service delivery.

● Recognition & Rewards: Recognition programs that celebrate your contributions.

What you’ll gain

● Health & wellness benefits (from day one), 401k, paid time off and competitive wages - along with fleet vehicle eligibility (with personal use allowance).

● Stability and respect. Many of our Managers have been here 10–20 years — because their work, time, and expertise are valued.

● Freedom to execute. You’ll own your projects, make field calls, and collaborate closely with engineers and PMs who trust your expertise.

● Continuous learning. Access to advanced training in WebCTRL®, networking, integration, and system analytics.

● Balance and culture. Leadership that respects family time, and a team that looks out for one another.


About this role

The Field Service Supervisor is a team leader of a selected number of Field Engineers (FE). Their primary responsibility is managing and training of their direct employees, and verification of their work. They will be responsible for the mentoring of new hires into new construction field operations, as well as current FE’s. They are responsible for working with the Project Management group in coordinating timely completion of all assigned projects. Ensure the field staff has the proper knowledge to perform that work and is executing their work at or under the project specific budget. Primarily responsible for coordinating all resources, internal and external, necessary for the execution of the new construction project their FE’s are assigned to in Cora PPM.

Key Responsibilities

COMMUNICATION AND DOCUMENTATION

· Provide necessary documentation and communication to all customer levels, sub-contractors (when necessary), and ALC Department Management as well as ensure that the appropriate members of the field operations department do so.

· Follow up on all daily log collection (Cora PPM) for the Field Engineers working for you and ensure timely delivery to New Construction Administration and Project Managers.

· Professionally represent Automated Logic in meetings and always be proactive in defending the company’s best interest. Always be prepared for meetings, have the answers to questions that you know will be asked, and have the appropriate back-up personnel in attendance when necessary.

· Lead, document, and participate in yearly and semi-yearly performance reviews for all of your employees

· Communicate with Engineering, Graphics developers and programmers to provide feedback on quality, accuracy and standards development.

BUDGET

· Thoroughly understand project budgets for negotiated projects that are executed by the Field Supervisor’s team.

· Continuously monitor work being performed by FE to ensure Quality Control. Provide continuous feedback to direct reports regarding performance, budgets and quality. Escalate any personnel concerns and proactively manage expectations of employees.

· Attend and actively participate in turnover meetings, Pre bid meetings and other meetings deemed important to the job.

PROJECT PLANNING AND SCHEDULING

· Collaborate with Project Manager in maximizing execution of projects by coordinating task assignment in Cora PPM

· Participate in monthly meetings with Project Managers and the Branch Operations Managers to collaborate in assigning resources for all projects

· Provide input to the Project Manager as to when resources will be needed on the project. This will include graphics, programming and technical checkout as required.

· Coordinate project schedule with electrical subcontractors and other trades to maintain schedule. Maintain continuous communications with FE’s, Project Managers, Customers and other trades to ensure consistent understanding of the project schedule. .

LEADERSHIP & TEAM PLAY

· Help develop and improve company standards.

· Develop Mentoring plans and continuously train new and current FE’s.

· Participate in peer reviews, turnover meetings, post mortem meetings and close out meetings as required.

· Assist in development of training and mentoring plans

PERSONAL DEVELOPMENT

Basic Qualifications

  • 3+ years of experience in the HVAC, Construction or building automation and controls industry

Preferred Qualifications

Other qualifications you may have that would be beneficial in this role include:

  • Bachelor’s Degree or 5+ years of relevant experience.

Provide a positive and seamless experience for guests by delivering excellent service.

Good understanding of business and financial concepts and demonstrated ability to lead the team to drive results.
Established time management, prioritization, and organizational skills.
Ability to communicate clearly and effectively with a positive attitude.
Proficiency with Word, Excel, PowerPoint.

Compensation for this role is $19 an hour.

#HarryPotterShop

Members:

title: Director, Integrated Process Team (IPT) Leader
description:
Job Description

Position Overview:


The Director, Operations position serves as the business unit manager for the cross-functional integrated process team (IPT) supporting a business area. This role provides leadership to the IPT and will also represent the business area on the Wilson Site Leadership Team.


Primary Activities:


Primary responsibilities for this position include providing tactical and strategic direction to the IPT. This includes ensuring that business objectives are met, a high standard for Quality and EHS compliance is maintained, and the IPT operates efficiently and within budget. The position will also be expected to promote continuous improvement within the IPT (aligned with lean manufacturing principles) and maintain an inclusive culture that supports positive employee relations. Additional activities, responsibilities, and competencies include but are not limited to the following:

Compliance:


  • Ensure that operations are executed in compliance with Safety, Environmental, Quality (cGMP), and Labor regulations.
  • Demonstrate leadership by maintaining a safe workplace and managing actions to prevent safety incidents.
  • Investigate, determine root cause, and implement robust CAPAs for any compliance discrepancies noted during activities, trend reviews, internal audits, or inspections.

Delivery:


  • Utilize a high degree of independent judgment and decision-making to direct production, packaging, and support personnel to ensure customer supply requirements are achieved.
  • Resolve and escalate issues impacting supply within the daily, weekly, and monthly IPT and site management processes.

Cost:


  • Develop budget for the IPT and ensure that activities are carried out in accordance with budget forecast.
  • Identify and execute capital projects needed to support the IPT short and long-term strategies.
  • Recognize and implement opportunities for efficiency and financial savings including elimination of waste.

People and Team:


  • Define and staff positions necessary to execute multi-shift operations at the Wilson site.
  • Provide leadership to the cross-functional team and direct Operations team providing coaching, development, and performance management where appropriate.
  • Ensure culture of inclusion and consistency is maintained supporting positive employee relations within the team and site.
  • Build effective relationships with other functional areas as well as stakeholders across our Company network.

Strategic Support and Continuous Improvement:


  • Help develop the strategy for the IPT as well as tactical plans to meet those goals.
  • Embed a culture of continuous improvement and MPS into the Operations team focused on standard work, making problems visible, minimizing waste, reducing process variability, and problem solving.
  • Identify and implement opportunities for process optimization and efficiency.
  • Provide site support and leadership to high-priority network strategies and initiatives.

Education Minimum Requirement:


  • B.A./ B.S. degree (preferably in Science or Engineering related field), Master’s Degree preferred

Required Experience and Skills:

  • Minimum 12 years relevant industry experience across multiple functions (Operations, Quality, Technical, Engineering, Supply Chain Management, etc.)
  • Concurrently, minimum 5 years Operations experience with some responsibility managing multi-layered organizations.
  • Strong leadership and influencing skills: ability to drive change, influence stakeholders, and motivate teams to achieve stretch goals.
  • Working knowledge of cGMP and regulatory requirements as they apply to the pharmaceutical industry
  • Strong communication skills: ability to effectively communicate with cross-functional teams, above-site stakeholders, and external authorities.
  • Willing to work irregular hours to support multi-shift operation on an as needed basis

Preferred Experience and Skills:


  • Experience leading a complex manufacturing or packaging operation within a plant site (Operations, Quality, or Technical role)
  • Experience licensing a new facility or start-up/scale-up of new capital installations for commercial supply
  • Experience in continuous improvement, lean manufacturing, problem solving, and/or right first time methodologies
  • Familiarity with change execution management and behavioral coaching / consequence management tools
  • Strong written and verbal communication including presentation skills and technical writing experience (investigations, change requests, standard operating procedures, protocols, etc.)
  • Project management skills: ability to prioritize tasks, manage timelines, and meet deadlines.
  • Experience supporting regulatory inspections (FDA, EMA, etc.)

Required Skills:

DP Operations, Leadership, Lean Manufacturing, Packaging, People Leadership, Plant Operations, Process Optimization, Production Scheduling, Safety Compliance, Sterile Manufacturing, Strategic Planning, Team Collaboration, Team Strategy

description:
Application close date:

At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight!

This role is part of Blue Origin corporate functions, providing centralized support across Blue Origin business unit teams, functions, and locations.

At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. Join our diverse team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight.


This role is part of Blue Origin Corporate Functions on the Finance AI & BI team and will be on-site in Renton, Washington with relocation provided.


We are seeking a Senior Business Intelligence Analyst to own the strategy and roadmap for the suite of BI tools supporting Finance and Accounting, including capital, labor, and inventory/production reporting today, with the expectation that this portfolio will grow. This is a senior, high-autonomy role: you will set direction for how existing tools evolve, lead build-vs-integrate decisions with Enterprise Technology (ET) and other cross-functional partners, and identify where new BI tools should be built to close reporting or controls gaps as the business scales. You will also mentor other analysts and represent Finance and Accounting BI needs in broader enterprise data and systems discussions.


Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

  • Own the execution of Finance and Accounting's BI tool portfolio, currently including Capital Management and In-Servicing, Labor Reporting, and Production web application with expansion to new tools as reporting or controls needs are identified
  • Partner with ET to determine what logic belongs in business intelligence vs. source systems and lead automation of inventory reconciliations and costing sheet rate monitoring
  • Lead the design of automated logic, using transaction detail and accounting guidance to flag and correct transactions, and drive upstream error-prevention to reduce reliance on manual corrections
  • Identify gaps in existing Finance and Accounting reporting and lead the design and build of new BI tools to address them
  • Set priorities for the BI roadmap with Finance, Accounting, and ET leadership, and represent Finance and Accounting BI needs in enterprise data governance discussions
  • Mentor and provide technical guidance to other BI analysts and supporting their development

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Business or Data Analytics, Data Science, Information Systems, or related field
  • 8+ years in business intelligence or systems analysis, ideally supporting a Finance or Accounting function
  • Demonstrated experience owning BI tool strategy and roadmap with full autonomy, including building new tools or reporting solutions from the ground up
  • Advanced proficiency in Power BI, Tableau, or equivalent, and advanced SQL knowledge
  • Working knowledge of cost accounting concepts (e.g., capital projects, labor allocation, or inventory costing), with the ability to quickly learn Blue Origin-specific policies and processes
  • Track record of leading cross-functional initiatives, influencing senior stakeholders, and mentoring other analysts

Preferred Qualifications

  • Strong working knowledge of cost accounting concepts, particularly capital project accounting or manufacturing cost accounting
  • Familiarity with ERP/cloud data platforms (Microsoft Dynamics 365, OneStream, Databricks, etc) and proficiency with Python or R for automation/advanced analytics
  • Experience with data warehousing, ETL workflow design, or applying AI/ML to automate error detection at scale
  • Experience driving enterprise-wide data governance or standardization initiatives

title: Evening Waste Collector
description:
Join our dynamic team at Community Concierge Services in Mooresville, NC zip code: 28117, and discover a rewarding part time evening job as a Trash Collector (Porter). This onsite position offers a unique truck needed opportunity to earn extra income while contributing to a cleaner community. With flexible evening hours, this role makes for an ideal side hustle for anyone looking to supplement their income while enjoying a high-performance work culture.

Plus, you'll earn $50 daily on average , making it a valuable option for those wanting to turn their evenings into productive and profitable times. As a Part Time Trash Collector (Porter) at Community Concierge Services, you will take on an active role that involves going up and down stairs to collect trash and recycling from residents' doors at your assigned apartment community. After collecting the trash, you will load it into your truck and transport it to the onsite compactor or trash bins.

Does this sound like you?

To excel as a Part Time Trash Collector (Porter) with Community Concierge Services, several key skills and tools are essential. First and foremost, you must have access to a reliable pickup truck capable of transporting collected trash to onsite compactor or bins. A smartphone with a data plan is also necessary for effective communication and navigation. Physical fitness is important, as you will need the ability to carry up to 50lbs at a time without assistance, ensuring efficient collection from residents' doors.

Knowledge and skills required for the position are:

  • ability to show up on time
  • smart phone with data plan
  • ability to carry up to 50lbs at a time without assistance
  • Evening availability to complete shifts on a set schedule each week
