title: Data Engineer
description:
Job Description

At SkyCity, we're building a modern, AI-enabled data platform that powers better decisions, unforgettable customer experiences, and the next generation of intelligent solutions. We're looking for a passionate Data Engineer to help shape and deliver the trusted data foundations that support reporting, analytics, and AI across the business.

As a Data Engineer, you'll design, build and maintain scalable data pipelines and reusable data assets that enable business insights and AI innovation. Working within our Data Platform Engineering team, you'll leverage technologies including Azure Data Factory, Snowflake and dbt to deliver reliable, production-grade data solutions.

This is an opportunity to work in a team embracing modern, AI-native ways of working, where tools such as Claude Code and other AI-assisted engineering technologies are part of daily development. You'll play a key role in ensuring data is high quality, well-governed, and ready to support emerging AI capabilities including Snowflake Cortex and Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) solutions.

  • Designing, building and maintaining data pipelines and data products across Azure Data Factory, Snowflake and dbt.
  • Developing reusable, well-documented data assets that support analytics, reporting and AI use cases.
  • Ensuring data quality, lineage, governance and security standards are maintained.
  • Working collaboratively with Data Governance, AI Enablement teams and business stakeholders.
  • Applying CI/CD and source control best practices across the data platform.
  • Identifying opportunities to automate and optimise data processes.
  • Contributing to the evolution of SkyCity's AI and data engineering capability
  • 3+ years' experience delivering data engineering solutions within cloud-based data platforms.
  • Strong hands‑on experience with Azure Data Factory, Snowflake, or comparable cloud data technologies.
  • Strong SQL skills and experience with data modelling approaches such as Kimball, Data Vault or Medallion Architecture.
  • Experience using dbt or similar transformation frameworks.
  • Working knowledge of CI/CD, Git, GitHub or Azure Repos.
  • Understanding of data governance, lineage, privacy and data quality principles.
  • A proactive mindset with the ability to take ownership from design through to production support.
  • Enthusiasm for leveraging AI-assisted development tools to improve speed, quality and innovation.

At SkyCity, our people are at the heart of everything we do. We celebrate diversity, collaborate openly, bring energy to our work, and continuously look for ways to improve. You'll join a team that's investing heavily in modern data capabilities and AI innovation while supporting some of New Zealand's most recognisable entertainment and hospitality brands.

  • A supportive, diverse company culture
  • Work with a fun and hardworking team
  • Fully laundered uniform before each shift
  • $2.50 cooked meals in our staff cafeteria (there's some healthy salads as well)
  • Heavily discounted staff car parking
  • Discounts at our outlets
  • Free trips for you and plus one as many times as you like up the Sky Tower

You'll get to be a key part of our fun team who work hard for ourguests. As an employer, we actively encourage your career development and expect our leaders to play a big part in developing their teams.

At SkyCity, our career opportunities are as diverse as our workforce. We don't just embrace differences; we value and support them. Our hiring is centred on capability and performance, regardless of gender, gender identity, race, origin, age, educational background, disability, or religious beliefs. We're here to empower you to shine. Our willingness to adapt ensures you can chart your path with us! Join us at SkyCity and be extraordinary by being you.

SkyCity takes its commitment to Host Responsibility seriously. Every member of our team, no matter their role, contributes towards SkyCity's culture of customer care.

title: POS Specialist
description:
POS Specialist

Department: IT – Point of Sale Systems

Reports To: POS Manager

Pay: $55,000 - $60,000

Position Summary

The POS Specialist is responsible for the administration, support, and ongoing reliability of the company’s Point‑of‑Sale (POS) systems and related retail technologies. This role supports traditional POS registers, mobile POS solutions, and self‑checkout systems across multiple store locations and serves as a technical subject matter expert for POS platforms and transaction workflows.

The POS Specialist works closely with Store Operations, vendors, and internal IT teams to ensure stable day‑to‑day operations and successful execution of POS upgrades, enhancements, and new store initiatives. This position participates in change windows, on‑call rotations, and off‑hours support as required.

Key Responsibilities

  • Support and maintain enterprise POS systems across traditional, mobile, and self‑checkout environments
  • Serve as an escalation point for hardware, software, and application issues
  • Support POS software deployments, patches, configuration changes, and version upgrades
  • Perform and document regression testing to validate POS functionality before and after system changes
  • Validate end‑to‑end transaction workflows, peripherals, and integrations during upgrade testing
  • Monitor POS system health and respond to outages or performance degradation
  • Perform root cause analysis and implement corrective actions for recurring POS issues
  • Maintain clear documentation for POS configurations, procedures, and testing activities
  • Coordinate with POS vendors, payment processors, and third‑party support providers
  • Support store openings, remodels, lane expansions, and technology refreshes
  • Responsible for on-call and after‑hours support for planned maintenance and critical incidents

Required Skills & Knowledge

  • Experience supporting POS systems in a multi‑store retail environment
  • Working knowledge of traditional fixed registers, mobile POS devices, and self‑checkout systems
  • Experience supporting POS peripherals (scanners, printers, pin pads, cash drawers, scanner‑scales, displays)
  • Comprehension of POS transaction processes (sales, returns, tenders, exceptions)
  • Familiarity with store networking concepts and POS connectivity
  • Strong troubleshooting, analytical, and documentation skills
  • Ability to work independently and collaborate across technical and non‑technical teams
  • Available to support nights, weekends, holidays, and change windows as required

Education & Experience

  • Associate’s degree in information technology, Computer Science, or equivalent practical experience
  • 1 year supporting POS systems or retail technology environments
  • Help desk and IT customer service experience
  • Prior experience working in, or supporting, a grocery and retail environment

Time / Travel Requirements

  • Availability for after‑hours maintenance, testing, and critical incidents
  • Occasional travel to store locations to support deployments, upgrades, and testing activities

title: Conversion Engineer
description:
At Materialise Medical, we believe that better healthcare starts with solutions designed around the individual patient. If you’re passionate about bringing personalized care to every patient, you’ll love being a part of this team. Through the technology we develop, researchers, engineers, and clinicians are revolutionizing personalized treatment — helping improve and save lives daily.


As a Conversion Engineer, you’ll perform all operational steps of the medical case. In the Segmentation and Pre-Planning step, the conversion engineer converts DICOM MRI or CT images into 3D models of the femur and tibia bones and creates landmarking to visualize axes and cuts for further surgical planning. According to the approved planning report from the surgeon, the conversion engineer creates the guide design and bone models (if requested). The main goal is to use Materialise software to add value to people’s lives by performing accurate 3D virtual surgical planning and customizing surgical guides for orthopaedic surgery worldwide.


Responsibilities:


Use Materialise software to convert 2D medical images; (radiology/CT/MRI) to 3D bone models;

​​ Perform pre-surgical planning on the 3D bone models;

Adjust automated surgical guides (such as knee surgery guides) to be used by the orthopaedic surgeon during the actual surgery.


Requirements:


Technical background is required;

English: at least pre-intermediate;

Good communication skills;

A successful candidate should be an open-minded, positive-thinking, and communicative person.

Will be a plus:


MS/BS degree in biomedical engineering or medicine;

Knowledge in 3D CAD/medical imaging or anatomy.


What’s waiting for you

Work that matters
The technology we build at Materialise pushes the boundaries. You’ll find pride in building something that matters, whether you designed it, printed it, or shipped it. No matter your role, we unlock new possibilities to build a better and healthier world every day.

At Materialise, we expect you to think about the customer, not just the task. You push for better solutions and care about the difference your work makes.

A people-centered space
When you join Materialise, you join a group of colleagues invested in you, not just your work. From your own team to a department across the world, you’ll find a sense of belonging with people who help without being asked, challenge you, and have your back.

At the same time, we expect you to invest in the people around you — not just your own work — to make the group stronger than the sum of its parts.

An environment of trust
As a company of innovators, we know how crucial autonomy is in your work. When we hire you, we trust in your expertise, giving you space to organize your tasks, work flexibly, and make your own calls.

At Materialise, we expect you to deliver on that trust and keep your commitments.

A career ready to build
When you see opportunities for your career to grow at Materialise, we encourage you to go for them. People shape a fulfilling career at their own pace here.

At Materialise, we expect you to take initiative in your own development. Don’t wait for someone else to plan your career. Step into the space and make it count.


Make a difference together with the Medical team.

What if your next security design helped protect the systems that save lives? Do you want to have a real impact on the cyber resilience of a global biopharmaceutical leader?

Senior Cyber Security Engineer

In our IT Risk Management & Security division, we don’t do dull routine – we protect the critical infrastructure that enables the development of future medicines. Right now, we are looking for an experienced partner to join us and take our identity security and PAM (Privileged Access Management) capabilities to the next level. title: Vice President US Private Placements
description:
Excited to grow your career?

BBVA is a global company with more than 160 years of history that operates in more than 25 countries where we serve more than 80 million customers. We are more than 121,000 professionals working in multidisciplinary teams with profiles as diverse as financiers, legal experts, data scientists, developers, engineers and designers.

About the job:

Position Overview

BBVA is seeking an experienced Vice President to join its US Private Placement team. The successful candidate will play a central role in originating, structuring and executing USPP transactions for corporate and project finance clients, working across industries and global jurisdictions. The position requires strong technical credit skills, disciplined transaction management and the ability to coordinate seamlessly with relationship bankers, capital markets professionals, legal counsel, operations teams, investors and clients.


The role is intended for an execution professional with recent, directly relevant USPP transaction experience, including activity involving data centers, commercial real estate and project finance. The candidate must be comfortable moving from detailed financial analysis and documentation to senior level client and investor dialogue, while maintaining high standards of accuracy, judgment and execution discipline.


Key Responsibilities

  • Lead and support the end to end execution of US Private Placement transactions, from initial opportunity assessment and mandate through structuring, investor engagement, due diligence, documentation, closing and post closing coordination.
  • Partner closely with BBVA relationship bankers and sector teams to identify financing opportunities, develop transaction strategies and position USPP solutions within broader client coverage plans.
  • Prepare and review detailed credit analysis, financial models, debt capacity assessments, cash flow forecasts, covenant analyses and downside/sensitivity cases for corporate and project finance transactions.
  • Develop financing structures that appropriately reflect borrower objectives, investor requirements, credit considerations, tenor, amortization, covenant packages, security and other transaction specific features.
  • Create high quality client and investor materials, including pitch books, market updates, financing alternatives, transaction summaries, information memoranda, management presentation materials and internal approval documentation.
  • Coordinate execution across internal stakeholders, including Capital Markets, Relationship Management, Credit/Risk, Legal, Compliance and Operations, ensuring clear ownership, timely escalation and disciplined follow through.
  • Manage external workstreams with clients, investors, external counsel, technical advisers, rating agencies and other transaction parties, as applicable.
  • Maintain active dialogue with institutional investors in the USPP market and contribute to investor targeting, market intelligence, feedback collection and distribution strategy.
  • Provide current market perspectives on pricing, structures, investor appetite, sector trends and comparable transactions to internal teams and clients.
  • Ensure transaction processes are executed in accordance with applicable BBVA policies, regulatory requirements and internal governance standards.
  • Support senior team members in business development and client coverage while independently managing substantial portions of live transactions and selected client/investor interactions.
  • Contribute to the development of junior team members through modeling review, transaction guidance, quality control and knowledge sharing.

Required Experience and Qualifications

  • Minimum 5+ years of relevant experience at a major banking institution, institutional capital markets platform or comparable financial institution.
  • Demonstrated execution experience in both corporate finance and project finance transactions, with direct exposure to the US Private Placement market.
  • Recent transaction and execution experience involving data centers, commercial real estate and project finance USPP activity.
  • Strong background in credit analysis, including assessment of business risk, financial risk, leverage, liquidity, debt service capacity, covenant protection and structural considerations.
  • Advanced financial modeling capabilities, including integrated financial statements, cash flow forecasting, debt sizing, scenario analysis, sensitivity analysis and transaction specific project finance models.
  • Established relationships and multiple contacts across the institutional investor universe, with an understanding of investor preferences, decision processes and documentation expectations.
  • Experience reviewing and negotiating key financing terms and working with legal counsel on transaction documentation and closing processes.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate complex financing concepts clearly to senior internal stakeholders, clients and investors across multiple countries and industries.
  • Ability to manage multiple concurrent workstreams under tight deadlines while maintaining strong attention to detail and execution quality.
  • Current FINRA Series 7, Series 63 and Series 79 licenses.

Technical and Execution Capabilities

Credit & Underwriting

Ability to independently assess credit quality, identify key risks and mitigants, evaluate capital structures and translate analysis into clear financing recommendations.


Financial Modeling

High proficiency in Excel based modeling, including complex debt schedules, cash flow waterfalls, sensitivities and project finance analytics.


USPP Execution

Working knowledge of the USPP transaction lifecycle, investor process, term negotiation, due diligence, documentation and closing mechanics.


Sector Relevance

Recent familiarity with financing considerations applicable to data centers, commercial real estate and infrastructure/project finance assets.


Materials & Productivity

High proficiency with Microsoft PowerPoint, Word and Excel, as well as Google Workspace products, with strong standards for presentation quality and analytical accuracy.


Leadership and Collaboration Expectations

  • Act as a trusted execution partner to relationship bankers and senior capital markets professionals, bringing sound judgment, responsiveness and accountability to client situations.
  • Build credibility with clients and investors through well supported analysis, command of transaction details and clear, concise communication.
  • Operate effectively in a cross border environment, coordinating stakeholders across time zones, legal jurisdictions and industry sectors.
  • Demonstrate a strong control mindset, including careful review of materials, documentation, approvals, data and closing requirements.
  • Take ownership of deliverables and deadlines, anticipate execution issues and escalate material risks or decisions promptly.
  • Contribute positively to a collaborative team culture and support the development of colleagues through constructive review and coaching.

Profile of the Ideal Candidate

The ideal candidate combines technical depth with commercial judgment and strong interpersonal skills. They will have a demonstrated record of executing complex financings, the confidence to engage institutional investors and senior client stakeholders, and the discipline to manage detailed analytical and documentation work. Success in the role will require intellectual curiosity, strong organization, a collaborative mindset and the ability to perform consistently in a fast paced, global environment.


Core Competencies

• US Private Placement execution

• Corporate and project finance

• Credit analysis and underwriting

• Advanced financial modeling

• Data center and commercial real estate financing

• Investor relationships and market intelligence

• Client communication and presentation

•Transaction documentation and closing

• Cross functional and cross border coordination

• Execution discipline and attention to detail

Job Purpose:

The Virtual Banker is responsible for providing comprehensive relationship and portfolio management for an assigned group of business customers. This role serves as the primary point of contact for existing client relationships and is accountable for portfolio health, credit quality, client experience, and revenue growth. The position balances proactive portfolio administration—including loan and deposit oversight, renewals, and risk management—with defined sales expectations focused on expanding existing relationships, identifying new opportunities, and delivering value-added financial solutions through a predominantly virtual engagement model.

Job Duties:

  • Directly manage an assigned portfolio of business customers, including business term loans, commercial real estate loans, lines of credit, and business deposit relationships.
  • Proactively manage portfolio performance through delinquency monitoring, outbound client contact, and coordination with Credit Administration and internal partners.
  • Manage loan maturities to ensure timely renewals, extensions, and required documentation in accordance with bank policy.
  • Facilitate loan modifications and portfolio adjustments within approved credit guidelines.
  • Oversee depository overdraft management for assigned accounts.
  • Conduct regular portfolio reviews to minimize risk, reduce delinquency, and ensure compliance with bank and regulatory standards.
  • Maintain current and accurate borrower financial information, including business and personal financial statements and tax returns.
  • Generate incremental loan, deposit, and fee revenue by expanding existing client relationships and meeting established individual sales goals.

description:
Job Description

At our company, we aspire to be the premier research-intensive biopharmaceutical company. We're at the forefront of research to deliver innovative health solutions that advance the prevention and treatment of diseases in people and animals.


Our Global Engineering Solutions (GES) executes a wide variety of capital and expense projects to ensure that our company has the capabilities and facilities to meet our goal to provide World Class Supply of Medicines and promote our Company's goal. The Global Engineering Solutions (GES) group is seeking an Senior Specialist of Engineering to manage large capital projects independently or a series of smaller projects within a portfolio in the manufacturing, laboratory and infrastructure lines of business.


Our GES Engineers support internal and external manufacturing operations to remain operational, continuously improving and innovative. With our extensive range of facilities and environments, our Engineers have opportunities across many varied areas including Biological, Chemical, Automation, Capital Projects, Maintenance, Safety, Process Development, Technical Services, Utilities and Validation.


Responsibilities

  • Manage an integrated project team to deliver critical assets on time and within a prescribed budget.
  • Manage a portfolio of low or medium segment capital projects or a single high segment capital project from initial evaluation, scope development, and execution to completion within time, budget, SHE, and quality constraints.
  • Obtain input and coordinate with design leaders and external FEL partners on equipment or facility design, material selection, and installation proposals that meet operating requirements to satisfy the development of FEL packages and detailed design packages.
  • Assist/participate in equipment reviews and installation including FAT and SAT.
  • Manage various meetings and drive project goals.
  • Ensure project designs are safe, efficient, and incorporate best engineering and compliance practices, meeting GES safety standards and local standards requirements.
  • Prepare and implement appropriate SHE plans during project scoping and manage the implementation of the plans during execution, including the use of peer reviews, accident investigation, contractor safety management, and implementing areas for improvement.
  • Lead the development of project execution plans.
  • Verify that project scopes provide an effective business solution.
  • Navigate through business requirements and goals and impact to company financial objectives.
  • Manage projects process through effective design strategies.
  • Develop and implement suitable procurement strategies.
  • Understand and manage project cost budgeting and control.
  • Manage schedule development and control; understand scheduling principles and coordinate project requirements to have others develop detailed schedules.
  • Provide construction management oversight.
  • Implement change management and control.
  • Manage communications requirements with effective reporting and distribution of information.
  • Plan and mitigate risk management.
  • Proactively prepare and communicate project status reports for management review, identifying areas of concern with proposed corrective actions.
  • Manage/implement commissioning, qualification, contract administration, and project close-out.
  • Develop good relationships with cross-functional areas consisting of all aspects of the business including Operations, Quality, Technology, Maintenance, and Safety.
  • Assemble and manage multiple internal and/or external resources to develop scope and execute projects.

The first assignment will be in Rahway, NJ. Future assignments may be in West Point, PA / Rahway, NJ / Wilmington, DE. Successful candidates must be able to work at any of these locations. Preferred

title: Data Scientist
description:
Data Scientist

The Opportunity:

As a data scientist, you’re excited at the prospect of unlocking the secrets held by a data set, and you’re fascinated by the possibilities presented by IoT, machine learning, and artificial intelligence. In an increasingly connected world, massive amounts of structured and unstructured data open new opportunities. As a data scientist at Booz Allen, you can help turn these complex data sets into useful information to solve global challenges. Across private and public sectors—from fraud detection to cancer research to national intelligence—we need you to help find the answers in the data.


On our team, you’ll use your analytical skills and data science knowledge to create real-world impact. You’ll work closely with your clients to understand their questions and needs, and then dig into their data-rich environments to find the pieces of their information puzzle. You’ll develop algorithms and systems and use the right combination of tools and frameworks to turn sets of disparate data points into objective answers to help clients make informed decisions. Ultimately, you’ll provide a deep understanding of the data, what it all means, and how it can be used.


Work with us as we use data science for good.


Join us. The world can’t wait.


You Have:

  • 2+ years of experience with data exploration, data cleaning, data analysis, data visualization, data engineering or data mining
  • 2+ years of experience with statistical and general-purpose programming languages for data analysis
  • Experience analyzing structured and unstructured data sources
  • Experience developing predictive data models, quantitative analyses and visualization of targeted data sources
  • Experience building robust and scalable data engineering pipelines with varied datasets and data types
  • Experience working with Maven Smart System (MSS)
  • Experience working with LLMs including Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) and AI Agents
  • Knowledge of Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, or Natural Language Processing
  • Secret clearance
  • Bachelor’s degree in a STEM field

  • 2+ years of experience in the development of algorithms leveraging Python, R, Typescript or SQL and NoSQL
  • 2+ years of experience with Distributed data or computing tools, including MapReduce, Hadoop, Hive, EMR, Kafka, Spark, Gurobi, or MySQL
  • 2+ years of experience with Machine Learning, AI or NLP
  • Experience working with logistics optimization models leveraging discrete optimization algorithms and routing models
  • Experience working with geospatial datasets
  • Experience working with logistics or supply chain datasets
  • Experience with visualization packages, including matplotlib, Plotly, Seaborn, or ggplot2

title: Associate Director, Business Partnerships, Teamship
description:
Associate Director, Teamship Business Partnerships

College Board - GST

Location:

  • This is a remote role. Candidates who live near CB offices have the option of being fully remote or hybrid (Tuesday and Wednesday in office). All CB employees are required to occasionally travel to meet in person for business purposes.

Role Type:

  • This is a full-time position

About College Board

College Board is a mission-driven, not-for-profit organization that aims to clear a path for all students to own their futures. We focus on expanding access to higher education and helping students develop the skills they need for college and career readiness. We serve 7 million students annually– a reach unparalleled in a fragmented sector.


At a moment when AI is transforming education and work, College Board is investing in work-based learning as a critical pathway for students to build durable skills — collaboration, communication, and problem solving — that technology cannot replace.


College Board acquired District C and its flagship program, Teamship, its first programmatic acquisition in over 20 years (learn more here). This acquisition reflects College Board’s commitment to exploring bold ideas that bridge K–12, higher education, and career, complementing time-tested programs like AP and SAT.


We are building a team to scale the Teamship program so more students have access to high-quality work-based learning.


About Teamship

Teamship is a work-based learning program where teams of students solve real problems for real businesses. Teamship provides a high-impact reimagined internship experience that builds the durable skills students need, employers value, and that power today's economy. Key offerings of the program:

  • Hands-on learning with employers and experiences that build the skills technology can’t replace
  • World-class professional learning to support educators
  • Employer partnership model that makes it simpler to engage with high schools
  • Better access for more students with program delivery through schools

To learn more, listen to an interview with the Co-founder and Teamship team leader, Dan Gonzalez, on The Education Equation podcast with College Board President, Jeremy Singer (recorded before the acquisition).


About the Opportunity

As we grow, we are building a dynamic and mission-aligned team to help us expand our network of business partners, the amazing companies and individuals who volunteer five hours to provide valuable work-based learning experiences to students and pose a real business problem for them to solve.

We’re looking for an Associate Director, Business Partnerships to join our growing team. You’ll own the end-to-end process of recruiting, engaging, and supporting business partners and ensuring 100% match rate and delivery of this program, while evolving the systems that will drive quality and efficiency at scale.


In this role, you will:

Build and convert a strong business partner pipeline (40%)

  • Build and manage a pipeline of prospective business partners aligned to Teamship’s program needs
  • Recruit and convert partners from initial outreach through confirmed participation using clear, compelling messaging
  • Build trust and excitement with diverse business leaders so partners are motivated, prepared, and eager to participate
  • Drive timely, professional communication that keeps momentum high and reduces friction throughout the process

Deliver high-quality matches between businesses and programs (50%)

  • Create strong matches between business partners and Teamship programs that result in high-quality experiences for students and ensures every spot is filled prior to program launch
  • Ensure partners are onboarded, scheduled, and supported to enable smooth program delivery and a positive experience for all stakeholders
  • Work with businesses to scope challenges for student teams, ensuring clarity and authenticity
  • Maintain accurate systems, tools, and workflows to keep matching organized, efficient, and scalable as volume grows

Strengthen operations and support the program’s scalability (10%)

  • Support improvements to systems, workflows, and resources that increase efficiency and impact
  • Surface insights from partner engagement that help improve outreach and stakeholder experiences
  • Contribute as a reliable, proactive teammate in a fast-moving environment, stepping in where needed to support iterations and strong program delivery

About You

We’re looking for someone who takes ownership, moves work forward with urgency, and enjoys figuring things out. This role is a good fit if you love working with people, thrive on staying organized amid ambiguity, and take real satisfaction in seeing things through to completion.


How You Operate

  • You have a get-it-done mindset and strong sense of ownership; when something needs to happen, you take responsibility for driving it forward from start to finish.
  • You bring a bias toward action, urgency, and results, with the ability to stay calm and focused when outcomes depend on factors outside your direct control.
  • You enjoy fast-paced, ambiguous environments and can flexibly reprioritize to adjust as needs evolve.
  • You have strong organizational and project management skills, including follow-through, clear communication, and proactive coordination.
  • You get satisfaction from checking items off the list.

How You Communicate

  • You have a natural ability to connect with people and move them into action, engaging a wide range of audiences from small businesses to senior leaders to educators.
  • You build trust quickly, communicate clearly, and know how to tailor your message to the audience in real time.
  • You’re confident talking to new people and energized by external outreach, with excitement about serving as an ambassador for Teamship and its mission.

How You Problem Solve

  • You bring a creative, solutions-oriented approach to problem solving and enjoy finding another path when the obvious one is blocked.
  • You’re intrinsically motivated by solving the puzzle, making the right match, and seeing meaningful outcomes through, even when the work gets complex or barriers pop up.
  • You can think strategically about what needs to happen next while also executing at the task level, rolling up your sleeves and pitching in when needed.

How You Like to Work

  • You have a deep belief in young people, a strong connection to student impact, and genuine excitement about work that expands educational access and opportunity.
  • You enjoy being in a supportive environment that celebrates wins and values genuine collaboration.
  • You work well in a remote (or hybrid) environment, and you’re willing to travel on behalf of College Board three to five times per year.

All roles at College Board require:

  • A passion for expanding educational and career opportunities and mission-driven work
  • Curiosity and enthusiasm for emerging technologies, with a willingness to experiment with and adopt new AI-driven solutions and comfort with learning and applying new digital tools independently and proactively.

title: Patrol Deputy
description:
Do you want to be a part of an energetic team with opportunities such as SWAT, drug task force, boat and water patrol, ATV and snowmobile patrol, drone operator, or K9 handler? Do you want to live and work in a community that supports our Law Enforcement? Do you want to work for an agency that collaborates with and works alongside other agencies? Apply to work for Freeborn County. We provide our employees with quality training and equipment so they can provide our citizens with their best.

Patrol Deputy duties include: protecting and assisting the public by responding to a variety of citizen complaints; responding to emergencies such as accidents, fires, domestics, fights, burglaries and alarms; performing routine traffic patrol and ensuring business and village security; assisting Detectives by performing investigative groundwork for illegal activity; performing a variety of routine paperwork and reports related to investigations, emergencies, accidents and arrests; providing court security, performing civil process, and transporting prisoners; and working with and assisting other agencies, emergency services and social services.

Freeborn County offers a robust benefits package including: vacation / sick, life insurance, dental, vision, short term and long-term disability, AFLAC, PERA, Nationwide Retirement, flex spending, medical with generous VEBA contributions, and a free clinic for employees and their family members who are covered under the county insurance.

Qualifications: High School graduate, Associates Degree in Criminal Justice, Law Enforcement or relevant field. Must have a valid Minnesota driver’s license and must be Minnesota P.O.S.T. licensed or eligible to be licensed at time of employment.

Wage range $36.62/hr. - $49.13/hr., annual COLA and step increases to top wage.

Job Details

The Patrol Deputy is responsible for patrolling County roads, city roads, State Highways, Interstates, conducting snowmobile and boat patrol, enforcing state and local laws. This position responds to citizen complaints and emergencies and investigation of illegal activity. Under direction of the Sheriff and supervisors, this position performs general law enforcement work to protect life and property and enforce local laws and ordinances throughout Freeborn County. Duties include: protecting and assisting the public by responding to a variety of calls or citizen complaints; responding to emergencies such as crashes, fires, domestic assaults, fights, burglaries, and alarms; assisting detectives by investigative groundwork for illegal activity; performing a variety of court duties, and paperwork; resolving conflict and mitigating civil disagreement. This position must maintain good relationships and assist other departments and other law enforcement agencies, emergency services and social services.

Duties and Responsibilities
- Patrol Freeborn County to protect and respond to the public while preserving law and order and prevent or discover crimes. Patrol all areas within Freeborn County, including U.S. Highways, State Highways, County Roads and Township Roads. Patrol areas may also include cities within the County that are with or without their own police department.
- Assist local police departments within Freeborn County, other state and local agencies, whenever possible and practical, with situations including but not limited to crashes, domestic assaults, fights, burglaries, thefts, special events or other instances that require assistance.
- Performs routine patrol that includes traffic enforcement in cities and county parks.
- Investigation of vehicle crashes, various crimes, and deaths including collection and preservation of evidence and statements. Makes arrests as needed.
- Prepare reports documenting actions/incidents during the call for service in a timely manner and serve civil and legal paperwork, including but not limited to Summons and Complaints, Court Orders, Foreclosure Notices, Orders for Protection, Harassment Orders and Subpoenas.
- Testifies in court and participates in preparation of court cases.
- Drafts and execute search documents, property, and evidence pertaining to a crime.
- Prioritizes calls for service on severity basis and responds to most severe first.
- Responds to critical incidents that require the SWAT Team.
- Investigate missing persons cases, including but not limited to children and vulnerable adults as necessary and required by law. - Conduct search and rescue in instances of lost persons, such as hunters, bikers, hikers, cavers, swimmers, boaters and tubers. This may also include downed aircraft and stranded snowmobilers.
- Provide security/transports of prisoners. - Respond and assists in medical emergencies, fires, and natural disaster situations.
- Works with other departments/ agencies (Fire, other law enforcement agencies, social services and court services).
- Trains, maintains, and recertifies in accordance with FAA regulations to operate a drone.
- Prepares and instructs course work, files, and maintains paperwork associated with Field Training/Firearms/Use of Force/Taser trainings.


Additional Duties and Responsibilities
- Acquire and maintain current knowledge of federal, state, county, and local laws and ordinances.
- Keep up to date with legislative updates, law changes and court decisions relevant to the performance of duties.
- Attend training as required by the Sheriff and/or POST Board.
- Maintain proficiency in use and maintenance of all office owned and issued equipment.
- Acquire and maintain current knowledge of streets, highways, and geography of Freeborn County.
- Maintain tactical and technical proficiency with job responsibilities.

While these are the primary focus of the position, we believe strongly in teamwork and employees will be called upon to perform a variety of duties as part of their role with the County.

Position Requirements

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities
- Working knowledge of laws, ordinances, rules and policies effective in Freeborn County.
- Knowledge of modern police practices and methods.
- Knowledge of First Aid methods and techniques.
- Skill in operation and maintenance of equipment and weapons used in activities.
- Effective communication skills, both oral and written.
- Ability to effectively use a computer and various software programs.
- Ability to interpret a variety of instructions furnished in written, oral, diagram, or schedule form.
- Work complexity includes complex and significant variables, which requires analytical ability and inductive thinking in adapting policies, procedures, and methods to fit unusual or complex situations.
- Ability to handle a variety of typical assignments and problems under moderate supervision within standard operating procedures.
- Ability to apply considerable analytical skills to select, evaluate, and interpret data from several sources.
- Effective communication skills to provide regular contact with office, outside agencies and the public.

Education and Experience
- Two-year Associates degree in Law Enforcement or equivalent as approved by the Minnesota POST Board.

Licenses/Certifications
This position will require the acquisition and maintenance of the following additional certificates/licenses:
- MN Peace Officer License
- Emergency Vehicle Operation Course - Firearms/Use of Force/Taser
- Class D Driver’s License or equivalent
- AED/First Aid and CPR


Equipment and Tools Responsibilities
- Frequently operates squad car, radar, recording equipment, computer, cameras, PBT, and office equipment. Intermittently must operate drone, boat, snowmobile, ATV, hand held Lidar, night vision, medical supplies and other County vehicles.
- Intermittently use fire extinguisher and AED.
- Continuously carries firearm, taser, baton and less lethal equipment.


Physical and Mental Requirements
Positions in this job typically require: sitting, walking, running, stooping, bending, feeling, manual dexterity, grasping, talking, hearing, typing, and seeing. This position encounters unexpected and prolonged workdays and stress and pressure from dealing with emotional issues, conflicts and physical altercations. This position is generally light-duty and may require the exertion up to 60 pounds of force on occasion and the ability to lift, carry, push, pull and move objects, including persons. This position is exposed to threats, trauma, offensive language, and deadly assault. This position occasionally performs under tight deadlines and attention to detail. The physical demands described here are representative to those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of the job. Reasonable accommodations can be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Working Conditions
Most work is performed in a field environment involving working inside and outside of vehicles, buildings, roads, water bodies, and outdoors. Seasonal conditions can include excessive heat or cold. Potential for exposure to dangerous situations and angry or violent individuals. The work environment characteristics described here are representative to those an employee encounters while performing essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations can be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.


Competencies Common to All County Positions
- Develop, maintain a thorough working knowledge of, and comply with all office and applicable County policies and procedures
- Demonstration by personal example the spirit of service, excellence, and integrity expected from all staff.
- Develop respectful and cooperative working relationships with co-workers, including willing assistance to newer staff so job responsibilities can be performed with confidence as quickly as possible.
- Confer regularly with and keep immediate supervisor informed of all-important matters which pertain to the applicable job functions and responsibilities.
- Represent Freeborn County in a professional manner to the public, outside contacts and constituencies.

*****Starting salary $36.62 - $49.13 per hour. *****

title: Compliance Examiner Business Lead
description:
At Freddie Mac, our mission of Making Home Possible is what motivates us, and it’s at the core of everything we do. Since our charter in 1970, we have made home possible for more than 90 million families across the country. Join an organization where your work contributes to a greater purpose.

Position Overview:


The Compliance Examiner Business Lead is an experienced risk management professional engaged in infrastructure support, planning, scoping, execution, closeout, and issue remediation processes involved in mortgage industry examinations and reviews conducted by the Counterparty Operational Risk Evaluation (CORE) department. Key characteristics include effective leadership skills, clear communication, and a collaborative spirit in both team and cross-departmental settings. A demonstrated proactive approach, ingenuity, and adaptability are essential traits in this position to effectuate operational excellence and a positive organizational culture. Incumbents in this role are committed to fostering professional growth—both personal and among colleagues—while championing transparency, knowledge sharing, and relationship building across business units and internal CORE pods. The position reports to the CORE Manager or Senior Manager and does not include direct staff management.



Our Impact:

As an Compliance Examiner Business Lead, you will:

  • Support management and/or Counterparty Review Leads in ensuring high-quality, timely completion of all functions associated with CORE pod assigned deliverables and adherence to CORE pod timeline standards related to individual Counterparty examinations.
  • Apply a robust monitoring framework to challenge and review risk practices.
  • Aggregate and communicate independent, data-driven views of risk with a forward-looking perspective.
  • Build influential relationships with business partners, becoming a trusted advisor and stakeholder in risk management activities.



Your Impact:

  • Serve as the primary point of contact for area of focus related matters, ensuring effective communication and collaboration between CORE teams and business unit stakeholders.
  • Act as the communication link spanning the CORE pod operational structure, facilitating the inflow and outflow of information and supporting coordinated efforts across the pods and teams.
  • Assist management in reviewing documentation and providing L1/L2 approval support (i.e., Planning Memo, Section Workpapers, Final Report and Letter, etc.), contributing to the quality and consistency of documentation and supporting overall Counterparty review processes.
  • Foster positive relationships with stakeholders, actively participating in risk discussions and supporting effective challenges to drive actionable outcomes.
  • Identify process redundancies, propose enhancements, troubleshoot issues, and implement effective solutions to improve examination workflow across the pod structure.
  • Bringing a focus upon internal process re-engineering, with a view to making recommendations and enhancements to existing Risk processes where opportunities arise.
  • Champion knowledge sharing, support cross-team initiatives, and maintain a collaborative, transparent work environment.



Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s Degree (or equivalent work experience) and 10+ years of overall relevant experience with 5+ years in operational or compliance risk management, preferred.
  • Proven ability to influence at all organizational levels, including executives, and unite teams toward common goals.
  • Experience in process design and control assessment.
  • Preferred experience in the mortgage market, mortgage lending, or mortgage default.
  • Highly driven, results-oriented, and recognized as a “value partner” who proactively builds and leverages relationships internally and externally.
  • Exceptional problem-solving skills and ability to articulate complex concepts clearly.



Keys to Success in this Role:

  • Deliver thoughtful, fact-based challenges to divisions using a clear, concise, and risk-based approach.
  • Strong team player and ability to communicate clearly and concisely to senior leadership.
  • Strong influencing skills and ability to lead change and deliver results; Ability to multi-task and prioritize.
  • Apply data-driven insights to advise on risk perspectives, demonstrating intellectual agility and interpersonal flexibility.
  • Exhibit strong situational analysis and decision-making abilities.
  • Communicate effectively—both written and verbal—across all levels of the organization, including through impactful visualizations.
  • Embraces new technologies and actively explores opportunities to apply AI and automation to enhance workflows, solve problems and create greater impact.

title: Software Engineer III
description:
Job Description

It’s about creating solutions that help people.


Do others often ask you for technology advice and assistance? Are you always looking for innovative ways to help people? Do you like having the autonomy to build new solutions from the ground up? If so, being a Software Engineer III at Frost could be the job for you.


At Frost, it’s about more than a job. It’s about having a flourishing career where you can thrive, both in and out of work. At Frost, we’re committed to fostering an environment that reflects our values and encourages team members to be the best they can be. In joining our adaptable, integrity-driven team, you’ll become part of Frost’s over 150-year legacy of providing unparalleled banking services.


Who you are:

As a Software Engineer III at Frost, you are our code guru, not only writing code but understanding the "why" behind it. Our software engineers believe in collaboration, ingenuity, and truly want to drive design and change in the IT realm. In this role, you will be responsible for designing, writing, testing, implementing, supporting, and documenting solutions for assigned programs and applications across the organization. You welcome a challenge and want to provide next level experiences to every individual that uses our systems.


What you’ll do:

  • Design, write, test, implement, and document solutions for assigned program modules.
  • Collaborate with and provide technical advice to Product Owners, Business Analysts, and lines of business to estimate level-of-effort, timing, and feasibility, to design new systems based on business requirements, and to optimize system and program functionality.
  • Review coding for a group of software engineers to ensure alignment with business needs, change control procedures, and Frost development standards.
  • Take action using Integrity, Caring, and Excellence to achieve all-win outcomes.

What you’ll need:

  • 4 years of experience in commonly-used concepts, practices, and procedures associated with programming.
  • 4 years of experience in building and interfacing with Restful API(s) and in using JSON and XML formats.
  • 4 years experience in application development using Java, Spring Boot, Angular, Bootstrap, HTML, and CSS.
  • 4 years of experience in core Java concepts, including object-oriented programming, generics, collections, multithreading, memory management, and data structures and algorithms.
  • 4 years of experience in Spring Boot ecosystem, including building RESTful APIs, SOAP Services, implementing microservices architectures with domain driven design, configuring dependency injection, and managing application properties, profiles, and lifecycle hooks.
  • 4 years of experience in test-driven development (using JUnit, Mockito), version control with Git, and use of design patterns like Singleton, Factory, and Strategy to ensure code maintainability and scalability.
  • 4 years of experience in building robust CI/CD pipelines, containerization using Docker, and orchestration via Kubernetes, Openshift.
  • 4 years of experience in integration with databases (using Spring Data JPA), messaging systems (Kafka), and security configurations (with Spring Security and OAuth2).
  • 4 years of experience in Agile environments.
  • 4 years of experience in working with relational databases including Microsoft SQL Server and PostgreSQL.
  • 4 years of experience in object relational mapping using tools including Hibernate.

Our Benefits:

At Frost, we care about your health, your family, and your future and strive to have our benefits reflect that. This includes:

  • Medical, dental, vision, long-term disability, and life insurance
  • 401(k) matching
  • Generous holiday and paid time off schedule
  • Tuition reimbursement
  • Extensive health and wellness programs, including our Employee Assistance Program
  • Referral bonus program + more!

Since 1868, Frost has dedicated their expertise to provide exceptional banking, investment, and insurance services to businesses and individuals throughout Texas. Frost is one of the 50 largest U.S. banks by asset size and is a leader in banking customer satisfaction. At Frost, it’s about being part of something bigger. If this sounds like you, we encourage you to apply and see what’s possible at Frost.


Experience may be gained concurrently. Employer will accept any suitable combination of education, training or experience.

Telecommute Position. Must reside within Texas and within commuting distance of a Frost bank branch. Various unanticipated locations throughout the state of Texas. Up to 10% domestic travel required.

description:
About Carrier

Carrier Global Corporation, global leader in intelligent climate and energy solutions, is committed to creating innovations that bring comfort, safety and sustainability to life. Through cutting-edge advancements in climate solutions such as temperature control, air quality and transportation, we improve lives, empower critical industries and ensure safe transport of food, lifesaving medicines and more. Since inventing modern air conditioning in 1902, we lead with purpose: enhancing the lives we live and the world we share. We continue to lead because of our world-class, inclusive workforce that puts the customer at the center of everything we do. For more information, visit corporate.carrier.com or follow on Carrier social media at @Carrier.

About the role

If you’ve been in the BAS world a while, you know the difference between a job that just keeps you busy and one that keeps you engaged, respected, and growing.


At Automated Logic, a Carrier Company, our Managers describe this as the place where they finally found both challenge and balance. A place that trusts your judgment, values your craftsmanship, and gives you the tools and autonomy to make an impact.


As a Mission Critical Field Service Supervisor, you’ll be the expert voice on-site — a professional with deep knowledge and highly developed technical expertise in Field Service work. You’ll be counted on to deliver the kind of precision work our customers remember.

Our long-tenured people put it simply:

“I finally found it. Not just a job. Not just a paycheck. A work home.”

If that sounds like what you’ve been looking for, we’d like to welcome you home too.

At Automated Logic, we believe in investing in our people. As a Supervisor, you’ll have access to:

● Professional Development: Training programs, certifications, and continuing education in BAS technologies and leadership.

● Career Pathways and Leadership Opportunities: Opportunities to advance into other roles as well as mentor junior staff and contribute to strategic initiatives that shape our service delivery.

● Recognition & Rewards: Recognition programs that celebrate your contributions.

What you’ll gain

● Health & wellness benefits (from day one), 401k, paid time off and competitive wages - along with fleet vehicle eligibility (with personal use allowance).

● Stability and respect. Many of our Managers have been here 10–20 years — because their work, time, and expertise are valued.

● Freedom to execute. You’ll own your projects, make field calls, and collaborate closely with engineers and PMs who trust your expertise.

● Continuous learning. Access to advanced training in WebCTRL®, networking, integration, and system analytics.

● Balance and culture. Leadership that respects family time, and a team that looks out for one another.


About this role

As Automated Logic continues to expand across Virginia's rapidly growing data center market, this role will play a critical part in supporting some of the most complex and demanding mission critical facilities in the world. From hyperscale cloud campuses to high-availability computing environments, you'll lead teams delivering building automation systems where uptime, reliability, and precision execution are essential. This is an opportunity to work at the forefront of data center technology while developing the next generation of field engineering talent.

Mission Critical Experience. Direct involvement supporting large-scale data center and mission critical facilities where building automation systems are integral to operational reliability, energy optimization, and continuous uptime.

Join a team supporting some of the largest and fastest-growing data center and mission critical facilities in North America.

As a Mission Critical Field Service Supervisor, you will lead and develop a team of Field Engineers responsible for delivering high-quality building automation solutions within data centers and other critical environments where uptime, reliability, and operational continuity are essential. You will partner with Project Managers, customers, and trade partners to safely execute projects, coordinate resources, maintain schedules, and ensure technical excellence across all phases of project delivery.

  • Lead, mentor, and develop a team of Field Engineers.
  • Coordinate field execution for mission critical and data center projects.
  • Support project planning, scheduling, staffing, commissioning, and technical checkout activities.
  • Ensure compliance with customer change management, safety, and operational readiness requirements.
  • Partner with Project Managers to manage resources, budgets, quality, and customer expectations.
  • Provide technical leadership and troubleshooting support for BAS installations, integrations, and commissioning activities.

  • High School Diploma or GED
  • 3+ years of experience in the HVAC, Construction or building automation and controls industry
  • 1+ years of experience with the Microsoft Office Suite, proficient in Microsoft Excel.
  • Clean and valid driver’s license
  • Capable of climbing ladders or using other lift equipment in excess of 8 feet above grade, and capable of lifting items up to 50lbs.
  • Ability to travel regionally with an occasional overnight stay.

Preferred Qualifications

Other qualifications you may have that would be beneficial in this role include:

  • Bachelor’s Degree or 5+ years of relevant experience.
  • Experience interacting with a large and diverse number of simultaneous challenges, requiring knowledge of multiple disciplines.
  • Building automation and controls experience with Automated Logic or similar BAS platforms.
  • Experience supporting data centers, healthcare, pharmaceutical, manufacturing, or other high-availability facilities.
  • Knowledge of chilled water systems, critical cooling applications, and facility operations.
  • Experience working under formal change management and outage planning processes.
  • Strong leadership, communication, and team development skills.

At Automated Logic, you’ll find the kind of work that challenges your mind, respects your time, and rewards your mastery — in a place that feels like home.

title: Photographer
description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

Scope of work:

  • The service provider will go through 3 rounds of feedback from the IRC team before submitting final photo selection.
  • Photography will take place at locations within Lebanon, as identified and agreed with the IRC team.
  • Gather community-based photographs at relevant project locations, capturing interactions, services, and surrounding context.
  • Capture a range of wide, medium and close up short.
  • Capture portraits and natural candid moments of clients, community members, staff, and other relevant subjects in line with IRC safeguarding and consent.
  • Capture contextual photographs of centers, project sites, facilities, and surrounding environment.
  • Take wide shots of crowds or group activities, where relevant.
  • Capture over-the-shoulder and from-behind shots were appropriate
  • Ensure a diverse selection of photographs that adequately represent the activities, people, environment, and outcomes of the project.
  • Provide a selection of high-resolution, professionally edited photographs to the IRC.
  • Apply basic color correction, exposure adjustment, cropping, and other necessary photo post-production while maintaining a natural and authentic representation of the subjects.
  • Execute IRC’s, as well as its relevant donor’s, branding, communications and visibility guidelines.
  • Submit a draft selection of photographs for feedback, followed by the final edited photographs in the agreed formats and resolution.

    • High-resolution JPEG files
    • Suitable for both digital and print use
    • Original/high-resolution files should be provided where requested by IRC
  • Guidelines will be provided.
  • Abide by the IRC’s child safeguarding policy and code of conduct.

Deliverables:

  • To deliver 30 to 40 edited high-resolution photos documenting PepsiCo activities, interactions and positive impact on children and families.
  • A selection including contextual, activity, candid, portrait, group, interactions, detail shots that collectively tell a coherent visual story.
  • Photos to demonstrate participation, engagement, positive experience and outcomes, i.e. sessions, medical counselling, etc.
  • The objective is to develop a coherent visual narrative through photography that documents the project’s activities, interactions, and impact on children and families, while creating a diverse and high-quality photo library that PepsiCo and IRC can use for media, communications, reporting, advocacy, donor visibility, publications, and other relevant materials.
  • The photographer will edit the photos, submit drafts and final versions to the IRC, along with all photos captured during the visit (unedited). The IRC reserves the unrestricted right to use the material for its own and third parties’ channels (including but not limited to media, social media, websites, and print) and may also offer the produced content free of charge to media outlets.
  • Meet with the IRC Health team and Communication Team for a brief on the project, planning, and the expected output.

Boeing Distribution Inc (BDI) has an opening for Entry Wheel and Brake Overhaul Technician. title: Scientist, Analytical Development
description:
The Role

In this role, you will develop mechanism-driven bioassays for early-stage mRNA-based vaccines and therapeutics within Analytical Development. You will work closely with Research from the earliest stages of product development to translate product biology, mechanism of action, and exploratory Research assays into scientifically relevant, robust, and phase-appropriate analytical methods. Success in this role requires strong hands-on expertise in cell biology and bioassay development, scientific curiosity, and effective collaboration across Research and Technical Development. You will own defined assay-development workstreams, generate proof-of-concept data, improve assay performance and reproducibility, and help mature promising assays toward future CMC and Quality Control applications.


Here’s What You’ll Do

  • Partner closely with Research scientists early in the program lifecycle to understand target biology, product mechanism of action, therapeutic hypotheses, and available assays, reagents, and experimental models.
  • Design, develop, optimize, and execute cell-based potency and biological activity assays supporting emerging mRNA-based vaccines, therapeutics, and new modalities.
  • Translate exploratory Research assays into robust, reproducible, CMC-amenable methods by evaluating biological relevance, assay format, sensitivity, dynamic range, precision, robustness, throughput, and suitability for continued development and eventual QC transfer.
  • Generate proof-of-concept data with relevant drug product and other representative materials to demonstrate biological activity and establish the relationship between assay response and intended mechanism of action.
  • Plan and execute experiments to understand assay performance, sources of variability, and potential failure modes; analyze data, formulate hypotheses, troubleshoot technical issues, and recommend experimental next steps.
  • Collaborate with Research and Development partners to identify, engineer, characterize, and maintain appropriate cell systems and critical biological reagents needed for sustainable bioassay development.
  • Apply complementary analytical approaches such as protein-expression assays, ligand-binding methods, flow cytometry, molecular biology techniques, and other orthogonal technologies to strengthen mechanistic understanding and assay relevance.
  • Partner with Analytical Product Leads (APLs), Process Development, Research, AS&T, QC, Applied Technologies, Quality, and other functions to align assay-development activities with program priorities and downstream analytical requirements.
  • Advance assays from proof-of-concept through method development and pre-qualification, including preparation of methods, protocols, reports, development summaries, and supporting documentation; contribute to downstream qualification, transfer, and lifecycle activities as appropriate.
  • Identify opportunities to leverage platform or semi-platform bioassay approaches across related products and modalities, and evaluate new technologies or automation approaches that improve assay robustness, biological relevance, throughput, or development speed.
  • Communicate experimental results, scientific conclusions, risks, and recommendations clearly to technical and cross-functional stakeholders while maintaining high standards for laboratory safety, data integrity, and documentation.

Here’s What You’ll Need (Basic Qualifications)

  • Ph.D. in Cell Biology, Molecular Biology, Immunology, Biochemistry, Bioengineering, Pharmaceutical Sciences, or a related field with 0-2 years of relevant experience; or M.S. with 8+ years; or B.S./B.A. with 10+ years of relevant industry experience. Hands-on experience with mammalian cell culture and development or optimization of cell-based assays is required.

Here’s What You’ll Bring to the Table (Preferred Qualifications)

  • Hands-on experience in immunology and/or oncology research, including multiparameter flow cytometry and in vivo/ex vivo assays to evaluate immune function, mechanism of action, and/or anti-tumor activity
  • Strong foundation in cell biology and demonstrated ability to translate biological mechanisms into meaningful functional assay designs.
  • Experience developing cell-based potency, biological activity, reporter-gene, target-binding, or other mechanism-of-action-related bioassays.
  • Experience working at the interface between Research/Discovery and Development, including adapting exploratory assays into more robust and reproducible analytical methods.
  • Hands-on experience with relevant technologies such as reporter assays, flow cytometry, ELISA/MSD, ligand-binding assays, qPCR/ddPCR, protein-expression assays, imaging, or other cellular and molecular biology techniques.
  • Experience with mammalian cell-line engineering, cell banking, or characterization and management of assay-critical cell systems and biological reagents is highly desirable.
  • Ability to assess key assay performance characteristics including specificity, sensitivity, dynamic range, precision, variability, robustness, and fitness for intended use.
  • Familiarity with quantitative analysis of bioassay data, including dose-response relationships, curve fitting, relative activity or potency measurements, and assessment of assay variability.
  • Experience with mRNA, nucleic-acid therapeutics, lipid nanoparticles, vaccines, oncology, immunology, or other advanced therapeutic modalities is preferred.
  • Understanding of phase-appropriate analytical method development and how methods progress from early Research through analytical development, pre-qualification, transfer, and eventual use in a regulated testing environment.
  • Familiarity with critical quality attribute concepts, analytical control strategies, and regulatory expectations for biological activity or potency assays is a plus.
  • Strong scientific curiosity, problem-solving ability, written and verbal communication skills, and demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively across multidisciplinary teams.
  • Self-motivated and organized, with the ability to manage multiple experimental priorities while maintaining scientific rigor and high-quality documentation, and a desire to make an impact as part of a high-growth, transformational company that is Bold, Relentless, Curious, and Collaborative.

Our Working Model

Otis is looking for a Packaging Engineer who is passionate about creating smarter, safer, and more sustainable packaging solutions. In this role, you’ll develop and improve packaging systems that protect our products, enhance transportation efficiency, support safe operations, reduce environmental impact, and optimize costs across the supply chain.

The Packaging Engineer partners closely with Manufacturing Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, Operations, Sourcing, Logistics, Suppliers, and Product Engineering teams to develop robust packaging solutions that prevent damage, improve material flow, reduce waste, and support field installation efficiency.



On a typical day you will:


  • Design, develop, validate, and implement packaging solutions for components, assemblies, controllers, and elevator systems to ensure product protection during storage, handling, and transportation.
  • Lead packaging improvement projects focused on reducing damage, improving pack density, minimizing waste, and lowering total packaging cost.
  • Support New Product Introduction (NPI) activities by developing packaging specifications, packaging validation plans, and transportation testing requirements.
  • Perform packaging root-cause investigations related to transit damage, field incidents, quality escapes, and customer complaints utilizing 8D, 5-Why, and Fishbone methodologies.
  • Develop and maintain packaging standards, work instructions, packaging drawings, specifications, bills of materials, and labeling requirements.
  • Collaborate with suppliers and logistics providers to implement standardized packaging solutions and ensure compliance with Otis packaging requirements.
  • Identify and execute sustainability initiatives including recyclable materials, packaging reduction, reusable packaging systems, and waste elimination projects.

  • Accurately summarize recorded documents affecting title, including deeds, mortgages, deeds of trust, liens, judgments, and contracts.
  • Prepare title commitments using the appropriate title codes and established company procedures.
  • Provide underwriting interpretation and support within established guidelines.
  • Coordinate national title services while effectively managing competing priorities and deadlines.
  • Monitor and prioritize assigned work to maintain a high level of individual productivity and accuracy.
  • Leverage modern title production procedures and technology to support efficient and accurate title operations.
  • Adapt quickly to changing priorities in a fast-paced, high-volume environment.
  • Work independently while collaborating effectively with team members and business partners.

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to work independently.
  • Ability to accurately review, interpret, and summarize recorded documents affecting title.
  • Strong organizational skills and the ability to prioritize multiple assignments in a high-volume environment.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
  • Strong interpersonal and teamwork skills.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively and make timely, sound decisions.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Outlook.
  • Demonstrated commitment to professionalism and exceptional customer service.

PREFERRED EXPERIENCE

  • Experience with commercial title transactions.
  • Experience with new construction transactions.
  • Experience coordinating national title services.
  • Familiarity with modern title production technology, electronic title plants, and title production procedures.
  • Experience supporting specialty title products and processes is a plus.

Over the course of the two-year journey, CLDP participants will complete three eight-month rotations aligned to enterprise priorities and individual development goals, with opportunities across marketing, marketing operations, sales operations, market access, launch excellence, and other critical commercial functions. description:

Job Overview

Who We Are

Our AI‑powered, cloud platform, RelativityOne, transforms massive volumes of complex information into actionable insights for litigation, investigations, regulatory inquiries, data breach responses, and other high‑stakes legal work where accuracy and trust are crucial.

The world’s largest law firms, corporations and government agencies rely on Relativity’s legal AI software to securely surface and manage the most relevant and impactful information in their matters. They shape how industries uncover critical insights, ensure compliance, advance access to justice and continuously evolve our platform using the latest technologies, including cloud-native architectures, AI capabilities, and modern developer tooling. Our AI powers privacy programs, identifies confidential information, and detects language indicating misconduct. We’re reimagining how legal professionals uncover truth at scale, and engineering is at the heart of that transformation.

Required
