title: Senior Materials Analyst
description:
About Us

We are a global climate technologies company engineered for sustainability. We create sustainable and efficient residential, commercial and industrial spaces through HVACR technologies. We protect temperature-sensitive goods throughout the cold chain. And we bring comfort to people globally. Best-in-class engineering, design and manufacturing combined with category-leading brands in compression, controls, software and monitoring solutions result in next-generation climate technology that is built for the needs of the world ahead.

Whether you are a professional looking for a career change, an undergraduate student exploring your first opportunity, or recent graduate with an advanced degree, we have opportunities that will allow you to innovate, be challenged and make an impact. Join our team and start your journey today!

If you are a Materials professional looking for an opportunity to grow, Copeland has an exciting role for you! Based out of our Rushville, IN location, you will coordinate and expedite purchases, inventory levels, flow of materials, parts, and assemblies from suppliers, between sections or departments, by performing the following duties.


AS A SENIOR MATERIALS ANALYST, YOU WILL:

  • Manage and develop process improvement projects for kanban pull systems to meet production and inventory targets
  • Manage MRP to ensure timely receipt of materials to meet production schedules.
  • Track the progress of materials and expedite, as required.
  • Analyze data and help develop analysis tools to improve efficiencies across the materials department. Develop and maintain autonomous reporting dashboard for “clear to build” window to prevent production interruptions
  • Manage inventory levels to meet both inventory and production goals.
  • Identify and resolve issues that impact on time deliveries.
  • Organize and set up daily transportation on critical timeframes to ensure timely receipt of products.
  • Work through new product development at the plant with part set ups, lead times, BOM changes, etc.
  • Utilize lean tools to improve supplier delivery to the plant
  • Meet customer requirements, including LTL, FTL, and expedites.
  • Work in conjunction with production, customer service, sales, suppliers, and procurement to meet customer requirements, including short LT and expedite requests.
  • Be cross trained in other positions in the/other department(s).
  • All other duties as assigned.


REQUIRED EDUCATION, EXPERIENCE & SKILLS:

  • Bachelor's degree plus 3-5 years of relevant materials experience. An equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered.
  • Working knowledge of Microsoft Office suite, proficient in Excel (Pivot Tables), Power-BI
  • Working experience with ERP and MRP use, Oracle
  • Capable of utilizing Lean tools, such as Kanban pull systems, demand-driven supply chain, and perfect execution strategies
  • Ability to travel up to 5% of the time
  • Legal authorization to work in the United States - Sponsorship will not be provided for this role.


PREFERRED EDUCATION, EXPERIENCE, & SKILLS:

  • Degree in Supply Chain/Operations or related degree
  • Knowledge of manufacturing operations, MRP systems, shop floor controls, supply chain methodology and lean practices



Schedule

Assembly operates on a 4-day, 10-hour work-shift schedule. Salaried employees who are not front-line supervisors work five days to support this arrangement. They can choose between working extended hours from Monday to Thursday with a half day on Friday, or they can opt for full eight-hour workdays from Monday to Friday.



Why Work in the Rushville, IN

Our facility is located in Rushville, IN, which is less than an hour from Indianapolis. Rushville is also a short drive from larger communities such as Shelbyville, Greenfield, and Greensburg. Downtown Rushville offers shopping, local eateries, a seasonal farmer and artisan market, and a host of community activities at the Riverside Park Amphitheater. We manufacture new semi-hermetic compressors and take the worn-out, failed compressors out of the field and remanufacture them to “like new” status, as well as manufacture crank shafts. Approximately 200 employees work in Rushville and are an integral part of our organization. A 2-building campus allows for learning and growth opportunities for all our team.

Together, we have the opportunity – and the power – to continue to revolutionize the technology behind air conditioning, heating and refrigeration, and cultivate a better future. Learn more about us and how you can join our team!

title: Cyber Security Director
description:
This role partners closely with IT, executive leadership, legal, compliance, operations, and external security partners to reduce cyber risk, strengthen business resilience, and ensure the organization is prepared to prevent, detect, respond to, and recover from cybersecurity threats.

What You’ll Do

  • Develop and maintain Flexsteel’s enterprise cybersecurity strategy, roadmap, policies, standards, and procedures aligned with business objectives, cyber insurance expectations, and recognized frameworks such as NIST and CIS Controls.
  • Lead cybersecurity governance, including risk reviews, executive reporting, metrics, maturity assessments, and continuous improvement plans.
  • Identify, assess, prioritize, and communicate cybersecurity risks across enterprise applications, cloud platforms, infrastructure, manufacturing environments, third parties, and business processes.
  • Oversee security operations, including threat monitoring, endpoint protection, email security, identity security, vulnerability management, cloud security, and managed detection and response services.
  • Lead vulnerability remediation planning in partnership with infrastructure, applications, data, and business system owners.
  • Develop, maintain, and test the Cybersecurity Incident Response Plan, including escalation procedures, communication plans, forensic coordination, ransomware response, and post-incident improvement actions.
  • Strengthen cyber recovery readiness through backup integrity, recovery testing, privileged access controls, disaster recovery alignment, and business continuity coordination.
  • Lead identity and access management strategy, including multifactor authentication, conditional access, privileged access, user lifecycle processes, and periodic access reviews.
  • Oversee data protection practices, including data classification, secure file sharing, encryption, data loss prevention, retention, monitoring, and controls for sensitive information used in analytics and AI tools.
  • Assess vendor and third-party cybersecurity posture, data protection practices, recovery capabilities, and contractual security requirements.
  • Consult with IT and business teams to ensure security requirements are incorporated into technology evaluation, design, selection, implementation, and ongoing operations.
  • Manage cybersecurity vendors, consultants, auditors, managed security service providers, cyber insurance partners, and incident response firms.
  • Develop cybersecurity awareness programs, phishing simulations, executive education, and targeted training for high-risk user groups.
  • Prepare and manage cybersecurity budgets, resource plans, business cases, and investment recommendations.
  • Serve as an active member of the IT leadership team and communicate cybersecurity risks, priorities, and recommendations clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.

What We’re Looking For

  • Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Cybersecurity, Computer Science, Business, or a related field; equivalent experience may be considered.
  • Eight or more years of experience in cybersecurity, IT risk, infrastructure, security operations, or related technology leadership roles.
  • Three or more years of experience leading cybersecurity programs, teams, vendors, or major security initiatives.
  • Strong knowledge of cybersecurity frameworks and practices, including NIST and CIS Controls.
  • Experience with enterprise systems such as SAP, Microsoft 365, cloud platforms, SaaS applications, data platforms, network infrastructure, and manufacturing or distribution technology environments.
  • Ability to communicate cybersecurity risks, business impacts, priorities, and recommendations to executives, business leaders, technical teams, and external partners.
  • Strong leadership, project management, vendor management, collaboration, analytical, and problem-solving skills.

Why Join Flexsteel

This is an opportunity to lead a business-critical cybersecurity function for an established, publicly traded company with a strong operational footprint and a continued focus on technology, resilience, and business transformation. The Director of Cyber Security will have meaningful visibility, executive partnership, and the ability to shape the company’s cybersecurity roadmap.

Flexsteel offers a competitive compensation and benefits package, including health, dental, vision, retirement benefits, paid time off, and additional company-sponsored benefits.

Work Environment

This role is primarily performed in a climate-controlled office environment. The position may occasionally enter operational areas where exposure to heat, humidity, fluctuating temperatures, dust, odors, oil, fumes, noise, powered industrial trucks, equipment, and moving mechanical parts may occur. Personal protective equipment may be required in designated areas.

title: Medication Adherence Technician (REMOTE)
description:
We’re unique. You should be, too.

We’re changing lives every day. For both our patients and our team members. Are you innovative and entrepreneurial minded? Is your work ethic and ambition off the charts? Do you inspire others with your kindness and joy?

We’re different than most primary care providers. We’re rapidly expanding and we need great people to join our team.

The Medication Adherence Technician applies knowledge and skills to engage in in-depth discussions with patients about medication adherence to identify and resolve patient adherence barriers. The incumbent in this role works with providers, clinical pharmacists and the pharmacy department to provide a coordinated adherence packaged product for patients requiring additional support establishing and maintaining compliance to their medication regimens. He/She is accountable for providing an unsurpassed patient experience by communicating to patients/providers on program specifics and arranging for prescription processing within the pharmacy; with the ultimate goal for patients to obtain an organized product they will understand allowing them to reduce or eliminate any adherence challenges. The Medication Adherence Technician focuses on providing consistent visibility and a presence to the target clients and patients.

ESSENTIAL JOB DUTIES/RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Makes outbound calls to patients and healthcare professionals regarding patient medications, adherence, and barrier removal.
  • Works diligently to remove barriers to ensure prescription regimens are provided to patients. This may involve analysis, research, and problem-solving to obtain resolution.
  • Interacts with healthcare professionals of all levels involving patient medications. Calls the pharmacy or provider to assist patient with medication refills, medication synchronization, or 90-day supply requests.
  • Captures and supports medication adherence patient prescription requests/needs.
  • Facilitates and/or coordinates the process whereby prescriptions are sent into the pharmacy pharmacy for patients, processed appropriately, adjudicated to third party insurance, error resolution completed, packaged and prepared for dispensing to the patient.
  • Follows established medication adherence workflows, including but not limited to: following up with patients requesting enrollment and patients currently enrolled to initiate or continue delivery of medication regimens.
  • Ensures assigned prescription processing tasks are accurate and reviewed by supervising personnel as required before dispensing to patients.
  • Motivated to meet set targets as established by leadership. Completes minimum daily goals for outreach (telephonic, email, mail) to patients and clinicians for Medication Adherence measures.
  • Provides feedback and/or solutions on how to improve the medication adherence patient/client experience.
  • Assists with training programs for clinical personnel involved in Part D HEDIS measures in the centers of ChenMed/JenCare/Dedicated.
  • Performs other duties as assigned and modified at manager’s discretion.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES:

  • Foundational knowledge and understanding of standard medication adherence practices, protocols, techniques, functions and processes
  • Excellent interpersonal skills, telephone communications skills and pharmaceutical calculation skills
  • Excellent written, verbal, listening and interpersonal communication skills
  • Good organizing and prioritizing skills
  • Strong time-management skills and keen eye to detail
  • Must possess a customer service mindset with the ability to remain patient, calm and empathetic is challenging situations
  • Ability to actively listen and understand patient questions and provide accurate answers or solutions.
  • Ability to make sound decisions and conduct follow ups for problematic situations that may arise during the established process
  • Ability to practice discretion and care on a regular basis when working with sensitive/confidential data pertaining to the patient, department, or company
  • Ability to interact with all levels of internal and external parties, to convey information correctly and always represent ChenMed and its entities in the most favorable manner
  • Capable of multi-tasking in a fast-paced, ever-changing healthcare environment
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite products including Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook, database, and presentation software
  • Ability and willingness to travel locally, regionally, divisionally or domestically up to 10% of the time
  • Spoken and written fluency in English

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE CRITERIA:

  • High School Diploma or equivalent required OR additional experience above the minimum may be considered in lieu of the required education on a year-for-year basis

  • Must meet at least one of the following requirements:
  • Certification as a Pharmacy Technician or Medication Assistant with a minimum 6 months of related work experience OR
  • A minimum of 2 years of work experience in a medication dispensing/pharmacy setting or call center

$14.3 - $20.42 Hourly

title: Operations Technician

Legends Global, the leader in privately managed public assembly facilities, has an excellent and immediate opening for an Operations Technician responsible for performing work as needed to efficiently clean, maintain, and prepare for events and other day to day needs in keeping with standards of a first-class facility. This includes, but is not limited to setting/striking tables, chairs, staging, air walls, barricades, pipe and drape, dance floor and other event related inventory as needed. Other responsibilities may include preventative maintenance, cleaning, upkeep, replenishing supplies and operating machinery including but not limited to utility vehicles, compactors, scrubbers, sweepers, snow machines, pallet jacks and other motorized material handling equipment as trained and authorized.

-Adhere to all Facility rules, regulations, safety programs, policies and procedures.

title: Product Security Engineer IV
description:
Product Security Engineer IV

College Board – Technology – Product Security

Location: 1) This is a fully remote role. Candidates who live near CB offices have the option of being fully remote or hybrid (Tuesday and Wednesday in office).

Type: This is a full-time position

About the Team

The College Board Product Security team is a close-knit and enthusiastic group of technologists with a thirst for knowledge in security and cloud. We collaborate closely to investigate and solve problems and have strong alignment with our product teams to be a step ahead in securing the organization’s suite of products. We are an agile organization, embracing AI and cloud-native systems, and are focused on improving speed and security of service delivery in support of our important mission. Our team comes from a wide variety of backgrounds as well as experience within the security space and we work to ensure everyone on the team has a voice.

Product Security Engineers work closely with Product teams as well as other organizational stakeholder groups to achieve product and security business objectives. They support threat modelling, architecture design, and implementation of secure development practices. In addition, they help define organizational security standards and organizational capability and tooling adoption decisions.

About the Opportunity

As a Product Security Engineer IV, you will work alongside other security engineers to support security across the development lifecycle for assigned College Board product teams. You will participate in threat modeling, vulnerability assessment, and design review—including for products that incorporate AI-powered features and use AI coding tools in development. You will build and apply your security knowledge on real work and document your findings clearly.

Day-to-day, you will conduct security code reviews, operate assigned security tooling, and support the remediation of identified vulnerabilities. You will also contribute to the Product Security Partners program, helping product engineers understand and apply secure development practices.

This is hands-on product security work with real stakes—your contributions help protect platforms that serve millions of students and educators worldwide.

In this role, you will:

Support Product Team Partnerships (55%)

  • Participate in planning, grooming, and design sessions for assigned product teams; contribute to security discussions.
  • Contribute to threat models and risk registers for assigned products; document findings clearly and escalate issues to leadership as needed.
  • Conduct vulnerability assessments on assigned products; apply exploitability frameworks to support accurate risk prioritization.
  • Apply CB's security policies, audit requirements (SOC 2, ISO 27002, PCI, PII), and GRC standards—with guidance—to support compliance activities.
  • Review code and security design documentation; identify security issues and contribute feedback in design reviews.
  • Support remediation of security gaps in assigned products; track and report progress against Product Security Framework requirements.

Support the Product Security Program (20%)

  • Participate in security training sessions; help product engineers apply secure coding practices, including responsible use of AI coding tools.
  • Support the Product Security Partners program by contributing to security champion activities in assigned product teams.
  • Document security learnings and patterns; contribute to the team's shared knowledge base.
  • Invest in developing your security expertise: learn from industry advancement, attend team learning events, apply new skills in your daily work, and contribute to Hackathons.

Contribute to Operational Improvement (25%)

  • Operate and monitor assigned security tooling across cloud environments; support the integration of security controls into CI/CD pipelines.
  • Contribute to security metrics tracking and reporting; collect and organize data that measures partner team security posture.
  • Participate in agile ceremonies; manage assigned stories and tasks with clear documentation and timely delivery.
  • Serve as on-call first responder for security tooling your team owns; support the Information Security team on incident response.

About you, you have

  • 4+ years of experience in product security, application security, cloud security, or software engineering with security responsibilities.
  • Deep application security knowledge, including common vulnerability classes (OWASP Top 10), secure coding practices, and security testing.
  • Solid experience with securing AWS Services, AWS Secure Architectures, Application Security and Cloud Applications, including Software Supply Chain and micro service architecture
  • Familiarity with cloud environments (AWS preferred) and CI/CD pipelines; developing knowledge of how security controls integrate into software delivery.
  • Familiarity with audit and compliance frameworks such as SOC 2, ISO 27002, PCI, and PII, and the ability to apply them with guidance to product teams.
  • Experience reading and reviewing code; proficiency or active development of skills in JavaScript/TypeScript or Python is a plus.
  • Clear, concise written and verbal communication; the ability to document findings and explain security concepts to technical peers.
  • A growth mindset: you seek feedback, apply it, and invest actively in developing your security expertise.
  • Ability to travel 2-3 times per year to College Board offices in New York or Reston, VA.

All roles at College Board require:

  • A passion for expanding educational and career opportunities and mission-driven work
  • Curiosity and enthusiasm for emerging technologies, with a willingness to experiment with and adopt new AI-driven solutions and comfort with learning and applying new digital tools independently and proactively.
  • Clear and concise communication skills, written and verbal
  • A learner's mindset and a commitment to growth: welcoming diverse perspectives, giving and receiving timely, respectful feedback, and continuously improving through iterative learning and user input.
  • A drive for impact and excellence: solving complex problems, making data-informed decisions, prioritizing what matters most, and continuously improving through learning, user input, and external benchmarking.
  • A collaborative and empathetic approach: working across differences, fostering trust, and contributing to a culture of shared success
  • Authorization to work in the United States

About Our Process

  • Application review will begin immediately and will continue until the position is filled. This role is expected to accept applications for a minimum of 5 business days.
  • While the hiring process may vary, it generally includes: resume and application submission, recruiter phone/video screen, hiring manager interview, performance exercise such as live coding, a panel interview, a conversation with leadership and reference checks.

What We Offer

At College Board, we offer more than a paycheck: we provide a meaningful career, a supportive team, and a comprehensive package designed to help you thrive. We’re a self-sustaining nonprofit that believes in fair and competitive compensation grounded in your qualifications, experience, impact, and the market.

A Thoughtful Approach to Compensation

  • The hiring range for this role is $140,000 to $151,000.
  • Your exact salary will depend on your location, experience, and how your background compares to others in similar roles at the College Board.
  • We aim to make our best offer upfront, rooted in fairness, transparency, and market data.
  • We adjust salaries by location to ensure fairness, no matter where you live.

You’ll have open, transparent conversations about compensation, benefits, and what it’s like to work at College Board throughout your hiring process. Check out our careers page for more.

title: Meat Lead Full Time
description:
A World-Class Team

BJ’s Wholesale Club is powered by more than 30,000 team members who make a real impact every day. Whether you're stocking shelves, solving problems or shaping strategy, your work helps families save on what matters most.

We’re a team built on purpose and opportunity. Join us and be part of something meaningful.

Why You’ll Love Working at BJ’s

At BJ’s Wholesale Club, our team members are at the heart of everything we do. That’s why we offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your health, well-being and future – both on and off the job. When you grow, we grow.

Here’s just some of what you can look forward to:

  • Weekly Pay: Get paid every week so that you can manage your money on your terms.
  • Free BJ’s Memberships: Enjoy a complimentary The Club Card Membership, plus a free Supplemental Membership for someone in your household.*
  • Generous Paid Time Off: Take the time you need with vacation, personal, sick days, holidays, bereavement, and jury duty leave.*
  • Flexible and Affordable Health Benefits: Choose from three medical plans, and access optional dental, vision, Health Savings Account (HSA), and flexible spending account options to fit your lifestyle.*
  • 401(k) Retirement Savings Plan: Build your financial future with a company match (available to team members 18 and older).*
  • Employee Stock Purchase Plan: Accumulate funds through after-tax payroll deductions that can be used to purchase shares of BJ’s common stock at a 15% discount.*

*Eligibility requirements vary by position.

Job Summary

The Meat Lead is responsible for overseeing meat department operations, ensuring compliance with food safety standards, maintaining inventory and merchandising excellence, and optimizing financial performance. This role supports operational execution and product quality while ensuring adherence to company policies and procedures. The Meat Lead does not have direct supervisory responsibilities but plays a critical role in supporting business performance and enhancing the Member experience.


A valid ServSafe Food Safety Certification is required and must be maintained in good standing. BJ’s covers any applicable cost associated and training.


Team Member Engagement

  • Live our values: Demonstrate inclusive behavior, make ethical choices, and approach your work with a positive and solution-oriented mindset.
  • Create a safe and collaborative environment: Foster open communication and trust.
  • Celebrate team members: Acknowledge others’ contributions, support team success, and help create a positive, encouraging work environment.

Member Experience

  • Guarantee service excellence: Ensure daily execution of GOLD Member Standards are met and are consistently reinforcing key service behaviors: Greet, Anticipate, Appreciate (GAA); Fast, Friendly, Full, Fresh, Clean; and Listen, Apologize, Solve, Thank (LAST) across all areas of the club.
  • Create a positive experience: Engage with Members in a friendly and helpful manner to contribute to a premium shopping experience.
  • Respond to Member needs: Address Member questions or concerns promptly and escalate unresolved issues to a supervisor when necessary.

Consistently Run Great Clubs with Great Standards

  • Maintain Club Standards: Consistently Delivering GOLD Standards in your club.
  • Contribute to club goals: Perform daily responsibilities with accuracy and consistency to support improvement in key performance areas and help the club meet or exceed targets.

Achieve Financial Performance

  • Cost Discipline: Use supplies responsibly and follow scheduling expectations to help the club stay within labor and supply goals.
  • Support Performance and Profitability: Complete tasks efficiently and accurately and follow best practices to help drive strong club results.
  • Understand the Business: Learn how your role impacts key club metrics and contribute to overall department performance through consistent execution.

Major Tasks, Responsibilities, and Key Accountabilities

  • Lead Meat Department Operations: Oversee the preparation, cutting, packaging, and merchandising of fresh meat products following company guidelines.
  • Oversee Production Process: Oversee meat production, including slicing, weighing, packaging, and labeling of meats, cheeses, and prepared foods while following food safety and sanitation guidelines.
  • Demonstrates Full Proficiency: Execute operational functions of the department, including the ability to cut, trim, and prepare meat to company standards.
  • Manage Inventory Proactively: Ensure proper product availability by monitoring inventory levels and executing timely replenishment to maintain in-stock conditions.
  • Accurate Item Labeling: Ensure all items are accurately priced, labeled, and in compliance with company policies.
  • Analyze Production and Sales: Track and analyze sales, waste, and shrink data to identify opportunities for process improvements and cost reduction.
  • Sanitation and Safety Compliance: Maintain compliance with all sanitation, safety, and food handling regulations, including ServSafe guidelines, while ensuring the cleanliness and proper maintenance of meat equipment such as slicers, ovens, and refrigeration units.
  • Report Operational Concerns: Escalate operational concerns, such as equipment malfunctions, stock shortages, or food safety risks, to management as necessary.
  • Execute proper product rotation: Apply FIFO (First In, First Out) rotation procedures to reduce waste and maintain optimal product quality.

description:
Why Join Rincon Research Corporation (RRC)?


At Rincon Research Corporation, our primary business is innovating, developing, and fielding digital signal processing (DSP) products and services for the United States Defense and Intelligence Communities in support of national security.

Rincon Research Corporation is seeking a Junior Orbit Determination Engineer to serve as a part of a dynamic team to build a new, end-to-end development program studying, designing, and deploying advanced orbit determination, maneuver planning and constellation management missions for United States Government space systems. RRC is looking for an exceptional experienced engineer to support this program through all phases of development—from early architecture and System Requirements Review (SRR) through Critical Design Review (CDR), integration, testing, and finally deployment into operational systems. In this role, you will work with other team members to engineer a complex space program. As a small business, RRC offers a unique opportunity to combine hands-on technical depth with senior-level leadership, allowing you to remain deeply engaged in detailed design and engineering decisions while helping to guide the overall program.

Come join the team that is creating cutting edge signal processing and geolocation systems for the future!

What are the primary responsibilities in the Orbit Determination Engineer position?

You will work in a highly collaborative, multidisciplinary environment alongside talented electrical engineers, mathematicians, aerospace engineers, and computer scientists/engineers. At RRC, all engineers are involved across the entire system lifecycle from architecture and development through deployment, operations, and sustainment—receiving direct feedback from customers and seeing their work make a tangible, real-world impact. Innovation is expected: team members are encouraged to propose improvements to system architectures, engineering processes, tools, and security posture.

Core responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

  • Astrodynamics analysis and problem solving
  • Researching, implementing, and updating custom astrodynamics algorithms
  • Implementing algorithms in software and testing with real-world data
  • Developing astrodynamics software tools.


What required background will make you successful?

  • Bachelor’s degree in Aerospace Engineering (preferred), Astronomy, Applied Physics, or other equivalent field of discipline
  • Demonstrated strength in scientific programming, especially C/C++ and Python
  • Ability to obtain and maintain TS/SCI security clearance

Preferred skills:

  • Master’s degree or PhD in Aerospace Engineering (preferred), Astronomy, Applied Physics, or equivalent field of discipline

Applicable Background:

  • Astrodynamics

  • Satellite maneuver planning, reconstruction, and characterization
  • Navigation via GPS and other GNSS
  • Experience with orbit software systems such as STK, ODTK, GMAT, or FreeFlyer
  • Scientific programming
  • Experience in both Windows and Linux environments

Where is the position located?

This position can be located at our Centennial, CO; Colorado Springs, CO; or Chantilly, VA locations.

Join us and become part of an elite team working on new disruptive system architectures. title: Principal Research Associate, Analytical Development
description:
The Role

In this role, you will support microbiology method development and lifecycle activities within Analytical Development for mRNA-based vaccines and therapeutics. You will apply hands-on expertise in microbiological methods including bioburden, endotoxin, sterility, and environmental monitoring to execute method development, optimization, characterization, qualification, and validation studies. You will work closely with Analytical Development scientists and cross-functional partners to evaluate method performance, troubleshoot technical challenges, support investigations and regulatory questions, and advance robust microbiological methods toward implementation in Quality Control. Success in this role requires strong laboratory execution, scientific problem-solving, attention to data quality and documentation, and effective collaboration across CMC Development and Quality.

Here’s What You’ll Do

  • Execute microbiological method development, optimization, characterization, qualification, and validation studies for bioburden, endotoxin, sterility, environmental monitoring, and related microbiological methods.
  • Independently plan and execute defined experimental studies; analyze and interpret data, identify sources of variability, troubleshoot technical issues, and recommend experimental next steps.
  • Evaluate method performance and suitability for intended use across relevant materials and sample types to support development, qualification, validation, and method lifecycle activities.
  • Author and execute study protocols and methods and contribute to technical reports, development summaries, validation documentation, and other analytical documentation.
  • Perform microbiological testing as part of method development, qualification/validation studies, investigations, troubleshooting, and other non-routine technical assessments.
  • Support microbiological investigations, deviations, method troubleshooting, and root-cause assessments in partnership with AD, AS&T, QC, Quality, Process Development, and other cross-functional teams.
  • Provide microbiology technical support for development programs, including technical assessments, risk evaluations, regulatory questions/RTQs, and preparation of supporting data and documentation.
  • Support method transfer and implementation in internal and external QC laboratories and provide technical support during method lifecycle activities.
  • Contribute to the evaluation and implementation of alternative or rapid microbiological methods, new technologies, and automation approaches that improve method performance, efficiency, or turnaround time.
  • Communicate experimental results, conclusions, risks, and recommendations to technical and cross-functional stakeholders while maintaining high standards for laboratory safety, data integrity, and documentation.

Here’s What You’ll Need (Basic Qualifications)

  • M.S. in Microbiology, Biology, Molecular Biology, Biochemistry, Biotechnology, or a related field with 4+ years of relevant experience; or B.S./B.A. with 6+ years of relevant industry experience. Hands-on experience with microbiological methods and analytical method development, qualification, validation, or troubleshooting is required.

Here’s What You’ll Bring to the Table (Preferred Qualifications)

  • Hands-on experience with microbiological methods including bioburden, bacterial endotoxin, and sterility; environmental monitoring experience is desirable.
  • Experience developing, optimizing, characterizing, qualifying, or validating microbiological methods in a biotechnology or pharmaceutical environment.
  • Understanding of microbiological method performance, suitability, controls, interference, recovery, variability, and fitness for intended use.
  • Experience in troubleshooting microbiological methods and supporting laboratory investigations, deviations, and root-cause assessments.
  • Familiarity with USP and other applicable compendial and regulatory expectations for microbiological methods.
  • Experience supporting method transfer and implementation in QC or external testing laboratories.
  • Experience with rapid or alternative microbiological methods, microbial identification, or related technologies is desirable.
  • Experience with mRNA, lipid nanoparticles, vaccines, biologics, or other advanced therapeutic modalities is preferred.
  • Strong data analysis, problem-solving, written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to clearly document and communicate experimental results.
  • Behaves like an owner, self-motivated and organized, with the ability to manage multiple laboratory priorities while maintaining scientific rigor, data integrity, and high-quality documentation.

Our Working Model

As we build our company, we have always believed that an in-person culture is critical to our success. This role is 100% onsite, reflecting the importance of being physically present to support the work, collaborate closely with colleagues, and contribute to our site-based operations.

Working onsite enables real-time collaboration, strong team connections, direct mentorship, and the hands-on partnership needed to deliver our mission. Join us in shaping a world where every interaction is an opportunity to learn, contribute, and make a meaningful impact.

Moderna is a smoke-free, alcohol-free, and drug-free work environment.

At Moderna, we believe that when you feel your best, you can do your best work. That’s why our benefits and well-being resources are designed to support you—at work, at home, and everywhere in between.

title: Director, AI & Technology Systems Foresight
description:
Director, AI & Technology Systems Foresight

Research & Policy Center


About the team


CFA Institute's Research & Policy Center has established a Macro Systems & Foresight function to help the investment profession navigate a future shaped by disruption and uncertainty.


Foresight is not forecasting. Rather than predicting a single outcome, the team examines material structural changes already reshaping finance while developing multiple plausible futures across 5-, 10-, and 20-plus-year horizons. It maps the mechanisms through which change may propagate and considers what alternative trajectories could mean for finance. That work helps frame RPC’s research, standards, advocacy, and thought leadership priorities and supports continued readiness as external conditions evolve.


About The Role


As the team’s Senior AI and technology specialist, you’ll assess how artificial intelligence and other material technologies could structurally reshape global finance, including market and institutional structures, investment practice, professional roles, and standards.


This is about AI as a force of disruption to the financial system, not technology for its own sake. You’ll bring technical realism to the team’s thinking, challenging hype-driven narratives as readily as assumptions that underestimate the pace or significance of change, and translate technological developments into clear structural questions, hypotheses, scenarios, and implications for RPC to investigate and test.


A core purpose of the role is internal enablement. You’ll partner with research, standards, advocacy, and other RPC teams to stress-test assumptions, assess the future relevance of existing work, and understand how AI and other technological developments may affect their areas. You’ll contribute specialist technical expertise while ownership of broader strategy and substantive work remains with the relevant functional leaders.

You’ll also translate the team’s technical analysis into high-quality external thought leadership and contribute to senior industry discussions on AI, technology, and finance. External publication and representation are extensions of the underlying foresight work, not standalone objectives.

This is a senior individual-contributor role reporting to the Head, Macro Systems & Foresight and working as part of a small, multidisciplinary team of specialists.


What You'll Do


  • Provide deep technical analysis of AI and other material technological developments, prioritizing changes already affecting finance while maintaining disciplined awareness of emerging capabilities and technologies.
  • Assess AI capability trajectories, architectures, model behavior, scaling dynamics, compute and data constraints, autonomy, control challenges, and institutional feasibility, distinguishing technically plausible developments from speculation or hype.
  • Map how technological change could transmit through investment workflows, portfolio construction, risk management, financial institutions, market structure, professional roles, and standards.
  • Translate technical developments into clear structural questions, hypotheses, critical uncertainties, and plausible future states that can inform shared foresight priorities and subsequent RPC research, standards, advocacy, and other work
  • Contribute technical expertise to scenario development and stress-testing, ensuring assumptions about AI capability, adoption, governance, and institutional response remain credible and appropriately conditional.
  • Identify relevant technical constraints, failure modes, governance challenges, and systemic risks, and assess what they may mean for finance, investment practice, and professional expectations.
  • Partner with RPC functional teams to stress-test existing research, standards, guidance, advocacy positions, and other assets where AI or technological change may affect their continued relevance or fitness for purpose.
  • Support RPC’s living-readiness discipline by identifying material changes in technology, capabilities, or adoption that should trigger reassessment of existing assumptions, positions, or assets
  • Produce clear technical landscape assessments, executive briefings, and contributions to broader foresight outputs, and develop external thought leadership that translates complex technological change into accessible, decision-relevant implications for finance and the investment profession.
  • Engage researchers, technologists, practitioners, governance experts, and institutional stakeholders to challenge assumptions, maintain current technical understanding, and strengthen the team’s analysis

What You'll Bring


  • Deep expertise in artificial intelligence, AI systems, architectures, and evolving capability dynamics, with sufficient breadth to assess adjacent technological developments where relevant.
  • Demonstrated ability to reason about AI as an evolving socio-technical system, connecting technical capability with adoption, institutions, governance, and real-world constraints.
  • Strong understanding of AI capability trajectories, scaling dynamics, compute and data constraints, model behavior, autonomy, failure modes, and governance architectures.
  • Familiarity with financial markets, investment management, or financial institutions, or demonstrated ability to apply deep technical expertise rapidly to unfamiliar domain contexts.
  • The ability to distinguish credible developments from speculative or deterministic narratives, while staying open to change that challenges prevailing assumptions.
  • The ability to explain complex technology clearly to non-technical and senior audiences, without jargon.
  • Strong systems thinking, including the ability to trace how technological change may transmit through financial markets, institutions, investment workflows, professional practice, roles, and standards, while maintaining a system-level perspective rather than becoming confined to narrow applications
  • Comfort operating across long time horizons and with incomplete evidence, together with disciplined judgment about what the available evidence supports and where technical trajectories remain uncertain.
  • Exceptional writing and communication skills, with a track record of substantive analysis or thought leadership for sophisticated audiences.
  • A collaborative style, strong stakeholder-management skills, and the ability to influence without authority, engage constructively with senior internal stakeholders and external technical experts, contribute specialist expertise to a multidisciplinary team, and publish in an institutional voice.
  • Strong intellectual independence, curiosity, and disciplined judgment, including a willingness to challenge prevailing assumptions where technical evidence warrants it. Strategic foresight experience is a plus but not required.

title: Records Management Specialist
description:
Job Function

The Records Management Specialist is responsible for maintaining the organization, accuracy, security, and accessibility of Compliance and Eligibility records. This position manages file storage, retrieval, tracking, and recordkeeping activities to ensure files are organized, compliant, and readily available. The role requires exceptional attention to detail, strong organizational skills, and a commitment to maintaining a highly structured and efficient file room environment.

Essential Functions

Records Management & File Administration

  • Maintain complete responsibility for the organization, upkeep, and daily operation of the file room.
  • Establish and maintain a highly organized filing system for active, inactive, vacated, terminated, transferred, withdrawn, and archived records.
  • Retrieve, track, and refile records in a timely and accurate manner.
  • Maintain file location logs and tracking systems to ensure all file movement can be monitored and accounted for.
  • Conduct routine audits of files and filing systems to identify missing documents, misfiled records, duplicate files, and organization issues.
  • Ensure all files are correctly labeled, indexed, and maintained according to agency standards.
  • Monitor file retention schedules and assist with records archiving and destruction processes in accordance with agency policies.
  • Prepare files for internal reviews, audits, compliance monitoring, hearings, and other agency needs.
  • Maintain orderly storage areas and ensure records are protected from damage, loss, or unauthorized access.
  • Identify opportunities to improve filing processes and records management practices.

File Room Operations

  • Serve as the primary point of contact for file requests from agency staff.
  • Pull, prepare, and distribute files requested for operational, compliance, or administrative purposes.
  • Monitor files checked out by staff and ensure timely return.
  • Research the location of missing or misplaced records and maintain documentation of recovery efforts.
  • Maintain inventory of file folders, labels, archive boxes, and other records management supplies.
  • Ensure file room shelving, storage areas, and workspaces remain orderly, accessible, and efficiently arranged.
  • Develop and maintain consistent file organization standards throughout the department.

Document Processing

  • Review incoming documents for proper filing and placement within participant, applicant, landlord, and program files.
  • Sort, label, organize, and file documentation according to established procedures.
  • Scan, copy, assemble, and prepare records as needed to support agency operations.
  • Ensure documents are filed promptly, accurately, and in the correct order.
  • Verify that required documents are present and properly organized within files.
  • Administrative Support
  • Assist staff with locating records, researching file histories, and obtaining archived documentation.
  • Maintain tracking logs, inventories, and records management reports.
  • Prepare records and documentation for transfer, storage, or review.
  • Assist with special records management projects and file room improvement initiatives.
  • Perform other related duties as assigned.
  • Maintain strict confidentiality of all applicant, participant, landlord, employee, and agency information.
  • Ensure records are maintained in accordance with HUD requirements, agency policies, retention standards, and records management procedures.
  • Protect files and confidential information from unauthorized access, removal, or disclosure.
  • Follow established procedures for document handling, storage, retention, and destruction.

Qualifications

  • High School diploma or equivalent required.
  • Minimum of two (2) years of clerical, records management, administrative support, or related office experience preferred.
  • Experience maintaining large volumes of records and documentation preferred.
  • Exceptional organizational skills and attention to detail.
  • Ability to establish and maintain highly structured filing systems.
  • Ability to work independently and manage competing priorities.
  • Strong problem-solving skills and ability to locate and reconcile discrepancies in records.
  • Proficiency with general office equipment and basic computer applications.
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality and handle sensitive information appropriately.

Working Conditions

  • Office environment with substantial responsibility for document and records management.
  • Frequent handling, sorting, filing, and retrieval of paper records.
  • Moderate physical activity associated with filing, organizing, and retrieving records.
  • Regular interaction with agency staff requesting records and documentation.
  • Moderate noise level with periodic interruptions.

Abilities

  • Ability to maintain consistent attention to detail for extended periods.
  • Ability to organize large quantities of records with a high degree of accuracy.
  • Ability to stand, walk, bend, stoop, reach, and file documents throughout the workday.
  • Ability to lift, carry, and move file boxes and records weighing up to twenty-five (25) pounds.
  • Ability to work efficiently in a paper-intensive environment.
  • Ability to maintain neat, orderly, and structured workspaces.

Equipment Operation

  • Scanner/Copier/Printer
  • Telephone
  • Label maker
  • Shredder

title: Part-Time Undergraduate Research Assistant
description:
APPLICATION INSTRUCTIONS:

  • CURRENT PENN STATE EMPLOYEE (faculty, staff, technical service, or student), please login to Workday to complete the internal application process. Please do not apply here, apply internally through Workday.

  • CURRENT PENN STATE STUDENT (not employed previously at the university) and seeking employment with Penn State, please login to Workday to complete the student application process. Please do not apply here, apply internally through Workday.

Approval of remote and hybrid work is not guaranteed regardless of work location. For additional information on remote work at Penn State, see Notice to Out of State Applicants.

JOB DESCRIPTION AND POSITION REQUIREMENTS

The Department of Agricultural Economics, Sociology, and Education is seeking an undergraduate research assistant to support a project to create a database cataloguing state immigration policies across the United States from 1989-2026. The RA will work directly with the study PI and a team of RAs to collect, clean, and code state legislative data. This position is for both the fall 2026 and spring 2027 semesters, with there being a possibility of extension into summer 2027.

This is a great opportunity for any student interested in topics surrounding immigration, sociology, public policy, political science, and/or data science, and will allow students to gain hands-on experience with real-world research data and contribute to an active research project. The RA’s tasks will include the following:

  • Collect state legislation pertaining to immigrants/immigration from state legislative websites and other public sources.
  • Systematically enter legislative data in a structured spreadsheet following an established coding protocol.
  • Assist in cleaning collected state policy data for accuracy and consistency.
  • Assist with basic data cleaning (e.g., spot-checking data entries, flagging discrepancies for PI review).
  • Communicate regularly with the PI on progress and participate in regular team meetings.

Required qualifications:

  • Interest in U.S. immigration, public policy, and/or law.
  • Interest in gaining familiarity with social science and/or legal/legislative research.
  • General familiarity with Excel and/or Google Sheets.
  • Excellent self-management skills.
  • Ability to work independently, meet deadlines, and stay organized with minimal day-to-day supervision.
  • Strong attention to detail and comfort with repetitive, careful data work.
  • Strong written and oral communication skills.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Prior research assistant experience.
  • Record of coursework in demography, sociology, political science, public policy, Latin American studies, and/or economics.
  • Experience with social science and/or legal/legislative research.
  • Experience using statistical software (e.g., R, Stata, SAS, SPSS, Python).

How to Apply

Please include a current resume/CV, and one or two paragraphs detailing your interest in the position and any relevant experience.

Candidates who advance to the next stage in the hiring process will be contacted to schedule a 30-45 minute interview and will be asked complete a sample data coding exercise.

Continuous Improvement & AI Enablement

  • Train and develop team members on responsible AI usage and validation practices.

Key Measurables

  • Year-End Close completed accurately and on schedule.

  • 100% completion of assigned balance sheet reconciliations.
  • No significant control, compliance, or documentation deficiencies.

Qualifications

  • 7+ years of progressive accounting experience with leadership responsibility.
  • Experience in manufacturing environments required.
  • Experience with software, SaaS, subscription, or ASC 606 revenue recognition preferred.
  • Strong knowledge of U.S. GAAP, internal controls, and audit requirements.
  • Demonstrated success leading close processes, process improvement initiatives, and accounting teams.
  • Advanced Excel, ERP, reporting, and financial systems proficiency.
  • Curiosity and willingness to leverage AI and emerging technologies to enhance accounting operations.

At TAPCO, we aim to enhance transportation and personal safety in our communities through innovative solutions and products. We are driven to save lives! title: Debt Strategy and Performance Analyst
description:
Join us, be part of more.

We’re so much more than an energy company. We’re a family of brands revolutionising how we power the planet. We're energisers. One team of 21,000 colleagues that's energising a greener, fairer future by creating an energy system that doesn’t rely on fossil fuels whilst living our powerful commitment to igniting positive change in our communities. Here, you can find more purpose, more passion, and more potential. That’s why working here is #MoreThanACareer. We do energy differently - we do it all. We make it, store it, move it, sell it, and mend it.

About your team:

At British Gas, our mission is to sell it and mend it.

We’ve been powering the UK’s homes and businesses for over 200 years – but supplying energy is just part of what we do. We’re making the UK greener and more energy efficient, getting closer to Net Zero. By using clever tech like thermostats, heat pumps, solar panels and EV chargers, we’re making it cheaper and easier for our customers to reduce their carbon-footprint.

Working as part of the End-to-End Debt Strategy & Performance team you will play a key role in shaping debt performance across British Gas Business. Using data-driven insight, you'll help monitor, analyse and optimise debt outcomes, supporting everything from debt prevention and cash collection to operational efficiency and commercial performance.


As a Debt Strategy and Performance Analyst, you'll turn complex data into actionable recommendations, identifying trends, risks and opportunities that drive better business decisions and deliver sustainable reductions in the cost of debt. You'll measure the impact of strategic initiatives, track recovery performance, and help improve customer payment behaviours and bad debt outcomes.


This is a varied role with opportunities to develop expertise across areas such as Direct Debit performance, debt prevention, operational and third-party recovery performance, workflow management and debt operations, depending on business priorities and demand. If you're passionate about turning data into meaningful business outcomes, we'd love to hear from you.

Key Accountabilities

Performance Insights and Analytical Investigations


  • Monitor end-to-end debt performance across assigned areas of responsibility; identifying trends, risks and opportunities across debt, recoveries & business initiatives
  • Produce and maintain regular reporting and management information packs
  • Track performance against goals, forecasts and business cases
  • Analyse operational and commercial performance drivers to identify root causes and improvement opportunities
  • Identify opportunities to increase operational efficiency and customer outcomes.
  • Translate complex data into meaningful insights with actionable recommendations.

Strategy and Optimisation

  • Support the development and impact assessment of debt strategies, business cases and treatment approaches
  • Provide evidence-based recommendations to support strategic decision making.
  • Model potential performance impacts of proposed changes and initiatives
  • Support the implementation of initiatives, defining processes, testing and tangible KPIs to monitor success
  • Assess the effectiveness of Business Initiatives deployed, measuring performance and ensuring expected outcomes & benefits are achieved
  • Identify opportunities for process simplification and efficiency improvement

Insight, Governance and Reporting

  • Develop and maintain reporting suites, dashboards and KPIs frameworks to monitor performance.
  • Produce meaningful management information that supports decision making and prioritisation.
  • Present findings and recommendations to stakeholders in a clear and actionable manner
  • Assist in ensuring recovery activities are delivered in line with business policies and governance requirements.
  • Maintain documentation relating to initiatives, assumptions, methodologies and benefits tracking
  • Identify risks, control weaknesses and compliance concerns, escalating where appropriate.


Work Experience and Skills

  • Strong analytical experience within debt management, collections, finance, commercial performance or operational performance environments.
  • Experience analysing large data sets and translating insight into actionable recommendations.
  • Experience identifying and delivering performance improvement opportunities
  • Strong numerical, problem solving and detailed root cause analysis - identify opportunities for performance improvement.
  • Experience supporting business change and benefits realisation activities.
  • Experience developing reporting, dashboards and KPI frameworks.
  • Commercial awareness with the ability to balance customer outcomes and business performance.
  • Advanced analytical capability using SQL, Power BI, Fabric, Databricks, SAS or similar tools.
  • Strong problem-solving and root-cause analysis skills.
  • Excellent stakeholder engagement and communication skills.

Why should you apply?

We’re not a perfect place – but we’re a people place. Our priority is supporting all of the different realities our people face. Life is about so much more than work. We get it. That’s why we’ve designed our total rewards to give you the flexibility to choose what you need, when you need it, making sure that you and your family are supported not only financially, but physically and emotionally too. Visit the link below to discover why we’re a great place to work and what being part of more means for you.

If you're full of energy, fired up about sustainability, and ready to craft not only a better tomorrow, but a better you, then come and find your purpose in a team where your voice matters, your growth is non-negotiable, and your ambitions are our priority.

title: Heavy Duty Equipment Journeyperson
description:

West St. Paul, Manitoba

We are looking for a skilled, reliable, and safety-focused Heavy Duty Equipment Journeyperson to join our team in Manitoba. In this hands-on role, you will inspect, diagnose, maintain, and repair a variety of specialized municipal and public works equipment, including vacuum trucks, hydro-vac units, street sweepers, refuse and recycling trucks, and other heavy-duty vehicles.   • Diagnose and troubleshoot hydraulic, electrical, pneumatic, and mechanical systems.
  • Repair and maintain vacuum trucks, hydro-vac units, street sweepers, refuse and recycling trucks, sewer inspection equipment, and other specialty vehicles.
  • Complete work orders accurately and efficiently while maintaining service documentation.
  • Collaborate with the Service Writer, Parts Department, and fellow technicians to maximize equipment uptime and customer satisfaction.
  • Maintain a clean, organized, and safe work environment in accordance with company and regulatory safety standards.

Total Rewards:

  • $2,500 Signing Bonus for fully licensed Journeypersons, payable in accordance with the Company's signing bonus program terms and conditions.
  • Quarterly Profit-Sharing Bonus Program (up to $1,500)

  • Competitive hourly wage based on experience and qualifications

  • 100% Employer-Paid Extended Health Benefits
  • Vacation Entitlement plus Paid Personal Days
  • Tool Allowance
  • Safety Footwear and Eyewear Allowance
  • Employer-Matching Retirement Savings Program

Position Details:

Location: West St. Paul, Manitoba

Compensation Type: Hourly (overtime paid in accordance with applicable employment legislation)

Schedule: Monday to Friday; occasional extended hours may be required based on operational needs

Travel: Minimal travel (approximately 0–2%)

Vacancy Type: Existing Position

What You Bring:

  • Strong troubleshooting and diagnostic skills.

  • Ability to perform the essential duties of the position, with or without reasonable accommodation.

Who We Are:

Joe Johnson Equipment (JJE) is a leading distributor of public works equipment across Canada and the U.S. We support municipalities and contractors with equipment such as vacuum trucks, refuse and recycling vehicles, street sweepers, and sewer inspection systems.

Our Core Values: Leadership, Customer Excellence, Integrity, Inspiration, Teamwork, Innovation, and Ambition

title: Cyber Threat Intelligence Analyst
description:
Cyber Threat Intelligence Analyst

Work as a member of a threat intelligence team responsible for understanding how emerging cyber threats impact the client organization while conducting highly detail-oriented security threat analysis and working with clients to validate and characterize threats. Support incident detection, response operations, and signature development, and provide input on new detection strategies and remediation guidance. You Have:

  • Experience with Splunk

  • Experience with the technical capabilities and limitations of the internet and online technologies, including collaborative internet tools such as social networking sites, blogs, and microblogs, and internet mapping tools

description:
About AVMAC LLC:

AVMAC was founded by two former Naval Aviation Maintenance Officers, Bert Ortiz and Don Buzard, who collectively have more than eight decades of experience assigned to, or directly supporting, both carrier and amphibious aviation.

AVMAC’s corporate staff and leadership team employ many with similar backgrounds and experience, which makes it a highly knowledgeable force multiplier to their customer base. The company prides itself on hiring, recruiting and training veterans as it continues to serve the Department of Defense and the Department of Transportation Homeland Security and commercial customers nationwide.

Position Summary:

The F/A-18 Aircraft Worker performs a variety of tasks related to the servicing, inspection, maintenance, and support of F/A-18 aircraft. Under the supervision of higher-level technicians or supervisors, this role involves assisting in the maintenance and repair of aircraft systems, components, and structures to ensure airworthiness and mission readiness.

This position is Fulltime, hourly position and the job duties are performed onsite on Marine Corps Air Station Miramar, San, Diego, California.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Make repairs to F/A-18 aircraft following orders of more senior technicians.
  • Work may include, but is not limited to, replacing or repairing worn or damaged components, such as carburetors, alternators, magnetos, fuel controls, fuel pumps, oil pumps, and engine mounted gearboxes, and compressor bleed valves using hand tools, gauges, and testing equipment; removing engine from aircraft, using hoist or forklift truck, disassembling and inspecting parts for wear, cracks, security, or other defects, and repairing or replacing defective engine parts and reassembles and installs engine in F/A-18 aircraft.
  • Performs preflight, thru-flight, and post-flight maintenance inspections,
  • Performs miscellaneous duties to service aircraft, including flushing crankcase, cleaning screens and filters, greasing moving parts, and checking brakes.
  • Enters in the maintenance records description of the work performed and verify the work was performed satisfactorily, may service engines and airframe components at line station making repairs, short of overhaul, required to keep aircraft in safe operating condition,
  • May specialize in work, repair and modification of structural, precision, and functional spare parts and assemblies, and may specialize in engine repair.
  • Perform other qualified duties as assigned.

Qualifications, Knowledge and Skills Required:

  • High school diploma or equivalent.
  • Must be able to obtain and maintain access to the base and all necessary facilities.
  • Minimum four (4) years’ experience with USN/USMC F/A-18 Aircraft preferable.
  • Must be able to obtain Plane Captain qualification within 90 days.
  • Knowledge and use of special tools/equipment required to perform assigned maintenance tasks is mandatory.
  • Must be physically able to perform all assigned duties. Must have a valid driver license.
  • Ability to read and interpret technical publications, safety rules, operating and maintenance instructions and procedure manuals.
  • Should be a self-motivated and be able to perform work with minimum supervision.
  • Must be able to meet physical requirements associated with and/or pass any medical examination requirements related to performing daily assigned tasks.
  • US Citizenship required due to the nature of the work.

Physical and Environmental Requirements:

  • This position requires normal physical functions.
  • Work may require frequent bending, reaching and climbing.
  • Frequently lift and carry items weighing up to fifty pounds and occasionally lifting heavier items with the assistance of other workers.
  • Work may be performed on top or under equipment in cramped or awkward positions.

What We Offer: (benefits vary based on FT, PT, or On-Call status)

  • Benefits offered include Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance
  • Employer-paid Life insurance, long-term disability and short-term disability
  • Paid time off -including 11 Holidays (8 hours per holiday)
  • Participation in the AVMAC LLC 401(k) plan

The hourly rate for this position is $46.13 (this pay rate does not include health and welfare).

title: Director of Risk Management and Safety
description:
Job Title: Director of Risk Management and Safety

Location: Honolulu, HI

Position Summary

The Director of Risk Management & Safety is responsible for the strategic oversight and day-to-day administration of the company’s risk management, insurance, workplace safety, and workers’ compensation programs for a diverse workforce of approximately 5,000 employees of the company and affiliated entities supported by the company. This role ensures compliance with Hawaii-specific regulatory requirements, minimizes financial and operational risk, reduces workplace injuries, and supports a safe work environment across retail stores, distribution, offices, and support operations. This is a hands-on role and partners closely with Operations, HR, Legal, Finance, and third-party vendors to proactively manage claims, safety programs, and loss prevention initiatives.

Key Responsibilities

Risk Management & Insurance

  • Develop and manage the enterprise risk management strategy across all business entities.
  • Oversee insurance programs, including:
    • Workers’ compensation
    • General liability
    • Auto liability
    • Property
    • Umbrella/excess coverage
  • Serve as primary liaison with insurance brokers, carriers, TPAs, and legal counsel.
  • Assist with annual insurance renewals, exposure data, and loss runs.
  • Partner with Finance/VP of HR on premiums, reserves, claims forecasting, and budgeting.
  • Oversee claims trends at a macro & micro level and cost-of-risk modeling.
  • Report risk exposure and trends to CEO, VP of HR, and senior leadership.
  • Support business continuity, incident response, and crisis management planning.

Workers’ Compensation (WC) Administration

  • Oversee the full lifecycle of workers’ compensation claims under Hawaii WC laws, including:
    • First report of injury
    • Claims investigation and documentation
    • Coordination with TPAs and medical providers
    • Return-to-work and transitional duty programs
  • Train managers in injury reporting, documentation, and employee communications.
  • Ensure timely reporting and compliance with the Hawaii Department of Labor & Industrial Relations (DLIR).
  • Monitor WC costs, experience modification rates (EMR), and claim performance.
  • Coordinate with defense counsel on litigated claims
  • Assist with all types of insurance settlement negotiations, including worker’s compensation within authority
  • Prepare documentation and summaries for hearings, mediations, and appeals
  • Analyze claims trends and implement loss reduction strategies.
  • Partner with HR and Legal on claim disputes, litigation, and settlements.

Financial Oversight & Cost Control

  • Oversee the total cost of workers’ compensation (indemnity, medical, expenses)
  • Oversee WC budgets, reserves, and forecasts
  • Works with CEO, VP of HR, and senior leadership to set key performance indicators (KPI’s) or metrics to meet overall cost cutting initiatives.
  • Analyze loss trends and drive long-term cost reduction initiatives.
  • Evaluate deductible levels, self-insurance structures, or captives (with Risk/Finance)

Third-Party Administrator (TPA) & Vendor Oversight

  • Manage, and hold TPAs accountable
  • Set service standards, KPIs, and audit expectations
  • Oversee relationships with:
    • Medical provider networks
    • Utilization review vendors
    • Nurse case management
    • IME providers
    • Defense counsel
  • Escalate and resolve systemic performance issues

Safety & Loss Prevention

  • Lead the company-wide safety, security, and emergency planning program across all business entity operations.
    • Develop and conduct proactive safety training, increase engagement, training, and accountability
    • Collaborate development and implementation of preventive security training and programs with director of security
  • Ensure director of security perform security audits related performance and conduct physical surveys of premise security, including security equipment condition.
    • Develop and conduct emergency training plans
  • Develop, implement, and maintain safety policies and procedures aligned with:
    • Hawaii OSHA (HIOSH)
    • Federal OSHA standards
    • Grocery/retail best practices
  • Conduct safety audits, inspections, and hazard assessments at store and facility levels, including audits of food safety.
  • Investigate serious incidents and near misses; implement corrective action plans.
  • Partner with Operations to address ergonomic risks, material handling, slips/trips/falls, and equipment safety.
  • Oversee safety training programs for managers and employees.

Compliance & Regulatory Oversight

  • Ensure compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local safety and workers’ compensation regulations.
  • Maintain OSHA logs, injury records, and required postings.
  • Support regulatory audits, inspections, and inquiries.
  • Maintain documentation and reporting across all business entities.
  • Partner with Legal on:
    • Litigation strategy and risk exposure
    • Regulatory compliance and audits
    • Contractual risk transfer (indemnification, insurance requirements)
  • Monitor changes in laws affecting risk exposure (labor, safety, construction, etc.)
  • Oversight of ensuring workplace is free of hazardous materials.

Cross-Functional Partnership

  • Partner with:
    • Operations on store-level safety execution
    • HR on employee relations, accommodations, and return-to-work
    • Legal regarding claims, litigation, and labor-related risks
    • Finance on cost control and insurance strategy
  • Serve as a trusted advisor to leadership on risk exposure and mitigation strategies.
  • Support labor relations matters where safety or WC issues intersect with union activity.

Leadership & Program Management

  • Develop safety, security, and risk management standards across all business entities.
  • Influence and guide leaders.
  • Lead vendor relationships and ensure service-level accountability.
  • Prepare reports and presentations for VP of HR as needed.
  • Set department goals, metrics, and budgets
  • Develop policies and standards for risk management practices
  • Mentor and develop risk manager
  • Influence executive decision-making through risk-based insights

Qualifications

Required

  • Bachelor’s degree in risk management, Safety, Human Resources, Business, or related field.
  • 7+ years of progressive experience in:
    • Workers’ compensation
    • Risk management
    • Workplace safety
  • Strong knowledge of Hawaii workers’ compensation laws and HIOSH requirements.
  • Experience working with insurance carriers, TPAs, brokers, and legal counsel.
  • Strong analytical, communication, and critical thinking skills.

Preferred

  • Experience supporting large, multi-site retail or grocery operations.
  • Experience supporting unionized workforces.
  • Experience in grocery, retail, distribution, or hospitality environments.
  • Experience managing programs across multiple legal entities.

Physical & Work Environment

  • Regular travel to stores and facilities across Hawaii.
  • Ability to conduct onsite safety inspections.
  • Hybrid office role.

description:

Responsible for terminating and testing aerial and underground fiber optic systems, updating, and maintaining project tracking information such as production sheets, time sheets and customer required paperwork.   • Construct proper splice cases pressurized and non-pressurized, using all types and sizes of cable, including but not limited to grounding, bonding, isolation, slack storage, and sealing.

Additional Responsibilities (Secondary Functions)

  • Customer Service ‐ Interaction with project owners, engineers and coordinating with customers and engineers for scope changes and communicating those changes to the Project Manager.
  • Team Leader – Ability to assist in supporting a group to successfully complete an assigned task, share knowledge and experience with the team, mentor junior technicians.

Qualifications

  • Minimum of 2 years of fiber splicing experience

  • FOA or ETA OSP Certification
  • Safety-minded and follow safety regulations.
  • Valid Driver’s License, Commercial Driver’s License
  • Reliable transportation to travel when necessary.
  • Willing to submit to pre-employment, random and for-cause drug testing.
  • Ability to effectively and regularly converse and comprehend in English.

Physical and Mental Demands

  • Lift, push, pull up to 50 pounds regularly.
  • Grasp and manipulate various hand tools.
  • Twist, bend, pull, push, reach, and stoop regularly.

At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight!

This role supports the development and operations of New Glenn, a single-configuration, heavy-lift orbital launch vehicle capable of routinely carrying people and payloads to low-Earth orbit, geostationary transfer orbit, cislunar, and beyond. Its first stage is fully reusable, and the vehicle was designed from the beginning to be human-capable.

We are a dynamic team of collaborators, doers, and problem-solvers who are relentlessly committed to a culture of safety. As a part of a small, cross-functional team responsible for launch IT and communications infrastructure, you'll be instrumental in manufacturing integration and launch pad operations efforts for Blue Origin's first orbital class rocket.
