title: Rigger - Turbine Outages & Precision Equipment Handler (Saudi Arabia)
description:
Job Description

The Turbine & Precision Equipment Rigger is responsible for executing highly critical, heavy, and precision lifting operations during power plant turbine outages and industrial maintenance shutdowns. This role demands exceptional technical expertise to safely handle multi-million dollar rotating equipment, gas/steam turbine components, and delicate machinery within tightly restricted spaces. The successful candidate must strictly adhere to engineered lifting plans, maintain zero-compromise safety standards, and display flawless precision under fast-paced outage timelines.

Key Responsibilities

  • Rigging Execution: Safely attach, lift, guide, and position heavy turbine components and associated mechanical equipment in strict compliance with approved, engineered lifting plans.
  • Pre-Lift Assessment: Thoroughly review critical technical parameters prior to every lift, including total load weight, exact center of gravity, designated lifting points, travel path clearances, and final landing arrangements.
  • Equipment Management: Select, calculate, and inspect specialized rigging hardware such as synthetic/wire-rope slings, shackles, spreader beams, chain blocks, and specialized lifting accessories.
  • Compliance & Safety Verification: Audit all lifting tackle before use to verify valid identification tags, current inspection status, and Working Load Limits (WLL).
  • Precision Maneuvering: Expertly guide immense structural loads through highly restricted areas and congested plant environments utilizing controlled mechanical methods and precise signaling.

Requirements

  • Experience: Minimum of 3 to 5 years of proven experience as an industrial rigger, with a strong preference for candidates who have completed major turbine outages, power plant shutdowns, or heavy mechanical maintenance.
  • Technical Skills: Comprehensive knowledge of rigging mathematics, center-of-gravity calculations, crane signals, and rigging hardware capacities.
  • Certifications: Valid third-party rigging certifications (such as TUV, Bureau Veritas, Aramco, or equivalents) are highly preferred.
  • Physical Capability: Ability to work in confined spaces, at heights, and handle the physical demands of 12-hour shifts typical during emergency or scheduled outages.
  • Soft Skills: Strong teamwork orientation, high attention to detail, and a strict commitment to safety protocols.

Position Overview:


The Vice President of Corporate Services is an enterprise leader responsible for developing and executing Freddie Mac’s corporate real estate, property development, workplace and Corporate Services strategy. The role also provides executive oversight of facilities management, physical security, transportation, event and audio-visual support, food, fitness, mail, and reprographic business services, as well as the corporate information resource center. Freddie Mac was established by Congress in 1970 to provide liquidity, stability, and affordability to the nation's residential mortgage markets. Freddie Mac supports communities across the nation by providing mortgage capital to lenders. Today Freddie Mac is making home possible for one in four home borrowers and is one of the largest sources of financing for multifamily housing.


Your Impact:


The Vice President will shape the long-term direction of the corporate real estate portfolio and workplace environment while ensuring Corporate Services deliver resilient, efficient and high-quality services. Key Responsibilities:

Qualifications:

  • Strong communication, project management, organizational and negotiation skills required.

The successful candidate will have the ability to establish credibility at all levels of the organization, a strong leadership profile, exceptional communication skills, and an effective adaptive style across multiple internal and external stakeholder groups, including the board of directors, other senior leaders, and FHFA, our conservator and regulator.

The ideal candidate will balance strategic vision with disciplined execution while fostering an engaged, high-performing team and a culture of continuous improvement, innovation, safety, and service excellence.

title: Hardware Debug Engineer
description:
Extreme Engineering Solutions (X-ES) is looking for a hands-on Hardware Debug Engineer to diagnose, troubleshoot, and recover rugged embedded computing hardware. This role supports Production by investigating failures on complex single board computers and system assemblies, often requiring troubleshooting down to the component level.

The Hardware Debug Engineer will use electrical test equipment, product schematics, assembly documentation, software tools, and structured troubleshooting techniques to identify root causes of hardware failures. This position works closely with Production, Manufacturing Engineering, and Design Engineering to resolve individual failures and identify opportunities to improve product quality, manufacturing processes, and product designs.

Duties and Responsibilities

  • Diagnose and troubleshoot complex electronic assemblies and single board computers down to the component level.
  • Perform hands-on electrical and functional testing using laboratory test equipment such as multimeters, oscilloscopes, and logic analyzers.
  • Read and interpret electrical schematics, assembly documentation, and test procedures to support troubleshooting.
  • Document troubleshooting activities, findings, and corrective actions.
  • Analyze failure data to identify recurring or systemic issues and provide recommendations for Production, Manufacturing Engineering, and Design Engineering.
  • Develop and improve troubleshooting methods, test procedures, and diagnostic tools.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a similar field. Relevant work experience may be considered in lieu of a required degree.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with an interest in hands-on hardware troubleshooting.
  • Ability to work efficiently and independently while managing multiple priorities.
  • Strong written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills.
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
  • Computer proficiency and ability to learn new hardware and software tools.
  • Ability to work onsite from our facility located at 9901 Silicon Prairie Parkway in Verona, WI.

Desired Qualifications

  • Experience troubleshooting and debugging electronic hardware to the component level.
  • Experience with laboratory test equipment such as multimeters, oscilloscopes, or logic analyzers.
  • Ability to read and interpret electrical schematics and assembly documentation.
  • Experience with surface-mount soldering or component-level electronic repair.
  • Experience with embedded systems, single board computers, or other complex electronic assemblies.

Compensation and Benefits

Extreme Engineering Solutions offers a competitive compensation package with excellent benefits, including:

  • No-deductible, low-copay group health and dental insurance (90% employer paid)
  • Life insurance, short and long-term disability insurance (100% employer paid)
  • Eligibility for health, dental, vision, life/AD&D, and disability insurance benefits on the first day of the month following date of hire
  • Paid time off, plus eight paid holidays a year
  • 401(k) employer match up to 4%. Roth option is available
  • Participation in the employee stock ownership plan (ESOP) at no cost to employees

X-ES also takes a casual, small-business approach to company culture. At our state-of-the-art office and manufacturing facility located in Madison’s growing tech corridor, there’s no formal dress code, flexible day shift scheduling, and dedicated personal workspaces. Our employees kick back at regular company events and enjoy lunches from local pizza places and food carts. At X-ES, we strive to offer a comfortable, relaxed environment for our employees to do their best work.

About X-ES

When “rugged enough” isn’t rugged enough for embedded computing systems, industry leaders in the military, aerospace, industrial, and commercial sectors turn to Extreme Engineering Solutions (X-ES). Because we strive to be the premier provider of mission-critical embedded products while delivering exceptional levels of customer and employee satisfaction, we hire strong contributors and give them space to thrive. As a 100% employee-owned company, our employees both drive and directly benefit from our success. Together, we meticulously design and build products that stand up to some of the most extreme conditions on the planet.

X-ES is located on the far west side of Madison, WI. The company designs and manufactures rugged embedded computing solutions for a variety of applications. For more information, visit .

X-ES is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, or any other category protected by law.

All X-ES job postings and application procedures are posted in compliance with Section 39.08 of the Madison General Ordinances.

We enable growth through the effective and efficient movement of over 45 million shipments annually, supporting the flow of materials and products between suppliers, manufacturers, and customers.

You will lead a team which collaborates cross-functionally with Legal, Finance, Supply Chain Planning, Sales, and transportation carriers to challenge network constraints and ensure alignment with business requirements.   • Optimize routing and location strategies using advanced modeling software.
  • Design, implement, and maintain routing solutions that drive measurable cost savings.
  • Conduct cost-to-serve and fleet equipment analysis to support strategic decisions.
  • Apply statistical analysis, regression modeling, and optimization techniques to enhance supply chain processes.

  • Build and maintain strong relationships across the enterprise to inform decisions and gather feedback.
  • Collaborate extensively with cross-functional teams including Legal, Finance, Supply Chain Planning, Sales, and 3PL carriers to ensure alignment and successful execution of transportation initiatives.
  • Translate complex transportation analytics and network modeling outputs into clear, concise, and actionable insights for both technical and non-technical audiences, influencing key stakeholders and executive leadership.

Job Description Summary

Educate the future of the Early Childhood industry as an Early Childhood Education instructor at Fox Valley Technical College. You will be part of a high performing, goal oriented team. This position is responsible for the delivery of instruction, facilitation of student learning, and the on-going development of curriculum and learning strategies that meet the needs of students and employers.

46-Week Contract

Job Description


Essential Functions and Responsibilities

The following duties are primarily performed and are essential for this position. Employees are expected to be able to perform each of these job duties satisfactorily and successfully to be qualified for the position. Other duties may be required and assigned.


  • Learning Facilitation – Foster student learning by developing appropriate instructional strategies to meet diverse student needs and support student engagement. Create learning experiences that integrate instructional technologies to maximize student success and multiple delivery methodologies such as hybrid, in-person, virtual, and on-line course delivery.
  • Assessment - Assess student learning and provide regular feedback to help students be successful. Use data to measure quality outcomes related to student persistence, retention, completion rate, course success, and learning and to design improvement strategies based on the evidence.
  • Curriculum Development - Develop and continually revise curriculum and instructional materials that are competency-based, current, consistent with employer expectations, and aligned with the college policy on level of required documentation to successfully prepare graduates for their chosen career fields.
  • Classroom Management – Fulfill assigned schedule, maintain accurate student attendance and grade records, maintain instructional environment with emphasis on safety, housekeeping, and equipment security, and ensure opportunities for student/engagement evaluation. Ensure course materials (including textbooks) are available to students.
  • Team Participation – Support the college by engaging in division, department and team activities, and meetings including planning, development, and budgeting, and staying current with internal and external changes and initiatives.
  • Business & Community Engagement - Build and maintain ongoing relationships with community, industry, and clinical partners by participating in advisory committees, external meetings, business visits, and community groups Collaborate with staff to recruit students, participate in recruitment events, and proactively promote the College and our programs.
  • Student Success & Support – Serve as an advocate for students and engage in activities that help students reach their goals by collaborating with Student Services staff to retain students, close achievement gaps, and help all students be successful. Advise students regarding class schedules, career information, internships, and other program-related information.
  • Professional Development - Continually improve knowledge and skills in emerging trends, current occupational practices, and teaching through professional development activities, networking with regional industry leaders, and the integration of new techniques and technology. Maintain Faculty Quality Assurance System requirements and licensure required to maintain individual and program accreditation.

Minimum Qualifications

Education and/or Experience Requirements:


  • Bachelor’s degree in Early Childhood Education or in a related and appropriate field; Master’s Degree preferred, OR
  • Possess a degree at the level in which they are teaching AND additional experience beyond what is required AND a plan to obtain bachelor's degree (with approval by the Vice President – Learning and Chief Academic Officer.) AND
  • Minimum of two (2) years full-time (or 4,000 total hours if part-time) of occupational experience in a target job for the program or programs being taught.
    • One year (or 2,000 hours) shall be within five (5) years prior to the date of appointment.
    • One year (or 2,000 hours) may be waived for occupational instructors with at least two (2) years of post-secondary teaching experience in the appropriate occupational field within five (5) years prior to the date of appointment.

In evaluating candidates for this position, Fox Valley Technical College may consider an exception to the education and experience requirements in the event of emergency staffing situations, pending credentials, specialized expertise or renowned qualifications of candidate, emerging fields, or lack of candidate availability. Exceptions must be approved by the Vice President of Learning/Chief Academic Officer.



Licenses, Certifications, and Other Requirements

  • Satisfactory background check and fingerprint-based criminal background check as required by the Wisconsin Administrative Code for Child Care Center Licensing.
  • Valid Driver's License.
  • Subject to FVTC's Motor Vehicle Records Check.
  • Proficiency utilizing learning management system.
  • Strong verbal communication skills.
  • Adapt quickly to changing demands, assignments, and circumstances to meet student needs.
  • Communicate effectively and professionally with various audiences.
  • Engage in continuous improvement in the quality of instruction by embracing innovative methodologies, techniques, and delivery methods.

Work Environment


  • Work will be completed in a hybrid environment, both in person and virtually.



Work environment may change based upon college needs.


Physical Requirements


  • Sitting: This role requires extended periods of sitting while performing tasks and utilizing computer systems.
  • Mobility: While much of the work is desk-based, occasional mobility may be necessary for attending meetings, office tours, or events within the workplace.
  • Fine Motor Skills: This role requires precise hand movements or manual dexterity for activities such as writing on a whiteboard, demonstrating experiments, or using instructional technology like computers.
  • Repetitive Motions: Capacity to perform repetitive motions, such as typing, without discomfort or injury.
  • Communication: Clear verbal and written communication skills are essential for interacting with employees, candidates, and stakeholders, both in-person and through electronic means.
  • Travel: Instructor position may require off-site teaching, fieldwork, or travel for professional development.
  • Lifting and Carrying: The role requires occasional/continuous lifting and carrying of light to moderate items up to 20 pounds.
  • Driving: Ability to operate a vehicle.

Pay is based on a multitude of factors, including experience, qualifications, education, relevant certifications, internal equity, and market data.

title: Full Stack Software Engineer
description:
The Company

Marigold is a fast-growing marketing technology company helping growing businesses build stronger customer relationships through its three core platforms: Emma, Campaign Monitor, and Vuture. We deliver powerful tools for email, SMS, and marketing automation that elevate engagement and drive real results. Marigold is headquartered in Nashville, Tennessee with offices in Sydney and London.


The Role


Senior Full Stack Engineers are an integral part of our autonomous, multi-disciplinary product teams, working closely with UX designers, Product Managers, and other software engineers to deliver quality, rock-solid customer experiences and scale our systems for ever-increasing growth. We work in small teams with clear objectives, which allows for accountability and transparency, and an expectation to support and maintain the software we create, including participation in an on-call rotation.

Note: The majority of the interview process will take place remotely, with one stage conducted in person.


This role is on the Campaign Monitor product, where the technology stack is mainly C#, JavaScript, SQL, and Java. Some of our frontend is still on Backbone.js as we continue migrating toward React, so you'll be working across both as part of that transition. We're looking to fill roles across a variety of projects, including:

  • Event-driven microservices and APIs in a distributed architecture
  • Dynamic web applications (ReactJS, Node.js, Backbone.js)
  • Infrastructure development on AWS (EC2, ECS, SNS/SQS, RDS, Elasticache, Elasticsearch)
  • Event streaming & big data solutions (Kafka, Spark)
  • Extending and growing our existing feature set

As a senior member of the team, you'll be expected to help shape architecture decisions, raise the bar on code quality through review and mentorship, and take ownership of problems end to end — not just implementation, but scoping, tradeoffs, and long-term maintainability.


About You

Essential

  • 10+ years of experience as a software developer.
  • BA/BS degree in Computer Science or a related field (in lieu of a degree, 3+ years of additional relevant industry experience).
  • Fluency in at least two programming languages, preferably including C#, Java, or JavaScript/TypeScript.
  • Comfortable using AI-augmented development tools (e.g., Copilot, Claude Code, Cursor) to write, review, and refactor code faster — with the judgment to know when to lean on them and when not to, and without outsourcing critical thinking about design, correctness, or security.
  • Familiarity with a range of storage engines (SQL, Elasticsearch, Cassandra, RDS offerings) and know when each is the right fit.
  • Data-driven decision making and familiarity with instrumentation techniques.
  • Effective communication skills, via interactive mediums and documentation.
  • You value teamwork and have solid collaboration skills, which are fundamental to how we work at Campaign Monitor.

Desirable

  • Experience in event streaming architecture and stream processing (Kafka, Spark).
  • Solid IaC experience with Terraform; comfortable picking up other provisioning/config tools as needed.

Haven't mastered everything on that list? That's okay. We heavily weigh potential, a desire for learning, and passion for contributing.


Why You'll Love It Here

  • Ultimate Flexibility: Unlimited time off, flexible hours, fully remote work and your birthday off.
  • Parental Leave: Generous parental leave for both parents.
  • Home Office: Setup allowance for new starters.
  • Genuine Connections: Optional fortnightly team gatherings at WeWork offices (lunch on us), culture clubs, an annual DevCamp to meet the wider team in person, Change Days and Innovation Sprints.
  • Professional Growth: Work at scale with cutting-edge technologies, keep learning, and see a real path forward.
  • Support & Benefits: Employee Assistance Program, wellbeing app, flu vaccinations, salary continuance and life insurance.

title: Director I, AP United States History Curriculum and Assessment
description:
Director I, AP US History Curriculum & Assessment

College Board - AP & Instruction

Location:

  • This is a remote role. Candidates who live near CB offices have the option of being fully remote or hybrid (Tuesday and Wednesday in office). All CB employees are required to occasionally travel to meet in person for business purposes.

Role Type:

This is a full-time position.

About the Team

The AP Curriculum and Assessment Team at College Board (125+ staff) collaborates with colleagues across all aspects of the AP Program to develop, manage, and deliver AP’s 43 courses in a wide variety of subject areas. AP® is a rigorous academic program built on the commitment, passion, and hard work of students and educators from secondary schools and higher education. AP provides willing and academically prepared high school students with the opportunity to study and learn at the college level. AP’s course teams comprised of educators and disciplinary experts ensure that course curricula are aligned to higher education expectations and reflect the state of the art in the discipline, contribute to instructional resources and tools for teachers, and develop assessments that allow students in these courses to demonstrate their mastery of course content and skills. AP leads in strategic use of AI to expand student access, strengthen instructional design and professional support, and enhance assessment creation and exam analysis. The English, World Languages, and Arts department, which includes English Literature, English Language, Spanish Language, Italian Language, French Language, German Language, Chinese Language, Japanese Language, Latin, Music Theory, Spanish Literature, and Art and Design is currently comprised of approximately 35 people supporting 14 courses in the AP portfolio. The Science department, which includes biology, chemistry, physics, psychology, environmental science, and Research, is currently comprised of approximately 25 people supporting 10 courses in the AP portfolio. The History and Social Science department, which includes history, art history, human geography, government and politics, economics, business, African American studies, and Seminar, is currently comprised of approximately 35 people supporting 12 courses in the AP portfolio. The Math, Computer Science, and Cybersecurity department, which includes precalculus, calculus, statistics, computer science, cybersecurity, and networking is currently comprised of approximately 22 people supporting 6 courses in the AP portfolio.

About the Opportunity

As the Director I, AP US History you will be responsible for preserving and improving the quality and validity of the AP Program’s core deliverables within the subject domain: the exam, the course curriculum, and the professional development content. You are also responsible for item development and management from authoring to administration; training and collaborating with subject-matter experts (SMEs), typically college professors and secondary school teachers. You will ethically and effectively integrate AI technologies in assessment creation and review. This includes judiciously using AI assisted tools to support fairness, validity, and innovation in AP assessments. You will train SMEs on assessment development protocols, translate between academics and technical experts (psychometricians), and collaborate to develop formative assessment materials and resources to support AP US History teachers worldwide. You will serve as a point of contact in AP for committees and communities of subject-matter experts and will be responsible for the curriculum and assessment for AP US History, and, in partnership with other AP teams, further the strategic growth of AP US History across the globe. Additionally, you may have the opportunity to present, speak, and moderate dialogue with academic and membership audiences to ensure that ongoing change and improvement within AP courses and exams is understood, accepted, and supported in secondary and post-secondary educational communities.

In this role, you will:

Assessment Development and Scoring (45-75%)

  • Serve as an assessment leader for AP US History, with primary responsibility for assessment development for AP US History. Your work in developing and revising test content is of the quality that requires only minimal adjustments based on feedback from your manager and other program leaders.
  • Independently lead processes for authoring and revising assessment content, including training educator constituents and leveraging generative AI to author and/or review assessment content, improving and/or making more efficient assessment processes and outputs.
  • Independently lead the development and management of assessment content (formative and summative) and scoring materials for AP US History through iterative review stages with multiple internal and external stakeholders, including the AP US History Team, Assessment Production team, Test Development Committee, and the Chief Reader, as appropriate.
  • Independently lead the development of assessment forms for AP US History, ensuring the AP Exam development aligns with approved curricula and test specifications.
  • Lead multiple face-to-face, weekend meetings, and virtual meetings (during work week, evenings, or weekends) annually with the AP US History Test Development Committee. You strategize and develop an agenda and approach to ensure the committee’s meeting time is of the highest productivity; you successfully adapt and pivot during the meeting as needed; and you successfully resolve all post-meeting item content edits.
  • Train and directly supervise Test Development Committee members in AP US History as content development contributors and reviewers. Recruit educators for the AP US History Development Committee and other opportunities to support AP Program.
  • Lead the successful scoring of student responses for AP US History Exams at the annual scoring event in person and online—the “AP Reading”—and produce AP Reading publications materials for teacher and student use. You plan all year, with increasing intensity in the months leading up to the Reading, ensuring all workflow steps for this incredibly complex event, as well as all post-Reading activities, are accounted for and successfully executed.

Assessment Quality and Process (10-15%)

  • Contribute to current research and best practices in assessment, and engage regularly with AP Curriculum & Assessment colleagues to align on standards and shared principles guiding AP’s assessment directions
  • Support assessment workstreams within the AP History and Social Science Department.
  • Contribute to processes for efficient, high-quality assessment development.
  • Contribute to initiatives to refine and improve question task models as well as exam design in collaboration with AP Curriculum & Assessment leaders and aligned to other College Board initiatives to achieve psychometric and disciplinary best practices on AP US History exams.
  • Monitor exam validity, security, reliability, fairness, and quality, as well as reader reliability in accordance with established Program thresholds for AP US History exam, identifying areas for improvement and executing on targeted improvement initiatives.
  • Collaborate with psychometrics and AP Curriculum & Assessment staff to establish fair, reliable, and valid cut scores for AP US History exam.

Course Development, Program Support, and Stakeholder Engagement (5-25%)

  • Refine and improve AP US History Course Framework to ensure clear and explicit learning outcomes that align with strategic priorities, including ensuring college/disciplinary standards as well as expanding the scope of reaching a broader audience of AP students.
  • Collaborate with AP teams to support the development of new products for AP US History designed to address unmet teacher instructional needs, potentially including developing prototypes, participating in small-scale market-testing, and creating models for subsequent development in conjunction with other AP workstreams.
  • Recruit educators for the AP US History Development Committee and other opportunities to support AP Program.
  • Serve as a recognized and trusted resource within the educator community by collaboration and engagement with the community to drive teacher satisfaction with AP US History and its exam.
  • Collaborate with the AP Professional learning team to support AP US History consultants and teachers.
  • Work with the AP Higher Education team to co-develop and implement plans to raise college and university awareness of AP US History courses and exams, including recruiting college faculty to participate in the AP Reading, co-leading the planning and execution of discipline-specific AP Faculty Colloquia events, and supporting Visiting and Virtual Fellows Programs.

About You

You (have):

  • A Master’s degree in US History or a directly related discipline, and knowledge of current trends in the discipline (required), although a doctorate in the discipline is strongly preferred
  • Expertise in US History with at least 5 years of experience in standardized assessment development or related work; experience with digital assessment and teaching preferred
  • Strong oral and written communication skills, with solid technical proficiency and a customer-focused mindset
  • Excellent organizational and planning skills, with the ability to manage multiple tasks and maintain close attention to detail, including proofreading
  • Demonstrated ability to implement processes and procedures, manage project plans and schedules, and maintain tracking documentation
  • Strong interpersonal and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively across all levels, and engage in giving and receiving constructive feedback
  • Ability to travel 6-8 times per year, plus up to two additional weeks for the AP Reading; must be eligible to work in the United States

All roles at College Board require:

  • A passion for expanding educational and career opportunities and mission-driven work
  • Curiosity and enthusiasm for emerging technologies, with a willingness to experiment with and adopt new AI-driven solutions and comfort with learning and applying new digital tools independently and proactively.
  • Clear and concise communication skills, written and verbal
  • A learner's mindset and a commitment to growth: welcoming diverse perspectives, giving and receiving timely, respectful feedback, and continuously improving through iterative learning and user input.
  • A drive for impact and excellence: solving complex problems, making data-informed decisions, prioritizing what matters most, and continuously improving through learning, user input, and external benchmarking.
  • A collaborative and empathetic approach: working across differences, fostering trust, and contributing to a culture of shared success
  • Authorization to work in the United States

About Our Process

  • Application review will begin immediately and will continue until the position is filled. This role is expected to accept applications for a minimum of 5 business days.
  • While the hiring process may vary, it generally includes: resume and application submission, recruiter phone/video screen, hiring manager interview, performance exercise such as item review and analysis, live coding, a panel interview, a conversation with leadership and reference checks.

What We Offer

At College Board, we offer more than a paycheck- we provide a meaningful career, a supportive team, and a comprehensive package designed to help you thrive. We’re a self-sustaining nonprofit that believes in fair and competitive compensation grounded in your qualifications, experience, impact, and the market.

A Thoughtful Approach to Compensation

  • The hiring range for this role is $96,000 – 135,000.
  • Your exact salary will depend on your location, experience, and how your background compares to others in similar roles at the College Board.
  • We aim to make our best offer upfront, rooted in fairness, transparency, and market data.
  • We adjust salaries by location to ensure fairness, no matter where you live.

You’ll have open, transparent conversations about compensation, benefits, and what it’s like to work at College Board throughout your hiring process. Check out our careers page for more.

title: Director of Residence Life

title: Fiber Technician Apprentice
description:
Position Summary:

The Fiber Optic Technician Apprentice is an entry-level position responsible for assisting experienced Fiber Optic Technicians with the installation, preparation, splicing, testing, troubleshooting, and maintenance of aerial and underground fiber optic systems. Under the supervision and direction of experienced technicians and management, the Apprentice will receive hands-on training in fiber optic cable preparation, splicing procedures, testing equipment, splice closures, troubleshooting techniques, and proper documentation.

The Apprentice will also assist with maintaining project tracking information, including production sheets, time sheets, and customer-required paperwork. All work must be performed in accordance with OSHA requirements, Expanse Core Values, company safety policies, and customer requirements.

This position is intended to develop the technical knowledge, field experience, and safety skills necessary to progress into a Fiber Optic Technician role.

Essential Functions:

  • Assist experienced Fiber Optic Technicians with preparing and splicing single-mode (SM) and multi-mode (MM) fiber optic cables in indoor and outdoor environments.
  • Learn proper fusion and mechanical splicing techniques under the supervision of qualified technicians.
  • Assist with the preparation and construction of fiber optic splice cases, including grounding, bonding, isolation, slack storage, and sealing.
  • Learn proper cable preparation techniques for loose tube buffer and ribbon fiber.
  • Assist with fiber testing and troubleshooting using equipment such as OTDRs, optical power meters, tone meters, fiber identifiers, and scopes.
  • Learn to read, understand, and document fiber optic test results.
  • Assist technicians with identifying and troubleshooting damaged or improperly functioning fiber.
  • Assist with reviewing and interpreting underground and aerial cable records, construction plans, maps, and field documentation.
  • Assist with preparing materials, tools, and equipment needed for assigned projects.
  • Maintain accurate production sheets, time sheets, field reports, and other customer-required documentation.
  • Communicate job progress, issues, concerns, and field conditions to the supervising technician or supervisor.
  • Follow established construction methods and instructions provided by experienced technicians, supervisors, engineers, and project management.
  • Participate in required safety meetings, training, and apprenticeship development activities.
  • Follow all applicable company and customer safety procedures and quality-control requirements.
  • Perform work in compliance with applicable OSHA, FCC, NESC, NEC, company safety manuals, technical procedures, and the Employee Handbook.
  • Properly use, clean, maintain, and secure company tools, vehicles, fiber optic equipment, and testing equipment.
  • Maintain assigned work areas and vehicles in a clean, safe, and organized condition.
  • Work flexible hours as required, which may include nights, weekends, overtime, and after-hours work.
  • Participate in emergency restoration activities and on-call assignments as training and experience allow and under appropriate supervision.
  • Travel to project locations as required.
  • Perform other duties as requested by the supervisor.

Additional Responsibilities (Secondary Functions)

Fiber Splicing & Testing – Develop knowledge and hands-on experience preparing various types of fiber optic cables for splicing. Learn the proper operation and care of fiber optic splicing and testing equipment and how to interpret test results for troubleshooting purposes.

Customer Service – Maintain professional interactions with project owners, customers, engineers, contractors, and other field personnel. Refer scope changes, customer concerns, or project issues to the supervising technician or Project Manager.

Teamwork – Work effectively as part of a crew and follow instructions from experienced technicians, crew leaders, supervisors, and management. Demonstrate a willingness to learn, ask questions, accept feedback, and develop technical skills.

Reporting – Provide timely and accurate information regarding assigned tasks, work completed, project status, issues, safety concerns, and results.

Training & Development – Successfully participate in company-provided training and hands-on instruction. Demonstrate continued progress toward performing fiber optic installation, splicing, testing, and troubleshooting tasks independently.

Other – Assist other positions and departments as directed by management and perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

  • No previous fiber optic splicing experience required; must have a willingness and ability to learn fiber optic installation, splicing, testing, and troubleshooting techniques.
  • Basic mechanical aptitude and ability to safely use hand and power tools.
  • Ability to follow verbal and written instructions.
  • Ability to learn how to read construction plans, maps, cable records, and technical documentation.
  • Safety-minded and committed to following company, customer, and regulatory safety requirements.
  • Basic computer skills, including the ability to learn and use Microsoft Outlook, Teams, Word, and Excel.
  • Ability to work effectively as part of a team.
  • Dependable, punctual, and willing to learn from experienced technicians.
  • Willingness to complete required company training and obtain applicable fiber optic certifications as required for advancement.
  • Ability to effectively and regularly converse and comprehend in English as required to understand safety instructions, training, work assignments, and job-site communications.

Physical and Work Requirements

  • Ability to work indoors and outdoors in varying weather and environmental conditions.
  • Ability to work at construction sites and around underground and aerial fiber infrastructure.
  • Ability to lift, push, and pull up to 50 pounds.
  • Ability to grasp and manipulate fiber optic tools, hand tools, and testing equipment.
  • Ability to regularly twist, bend, pull, push, reach, climb, kneel, and stoop.
  • Ability to stand and perform physical work for extended periods.
  • Ability to perform detailed work involving small fiber components.
  • Ability to work extended or non-standard hours when required by project conditions.

Minimum Education Requirements:

  • High school diploma or equivalent (GED)

Minimum Experience:

  • The Fiber Optic Technician Apprentice position is designed for a developmental role. Apprentices are expected to progressively demonstrate competency in fiber preparation, splicing, testing, troubleshooting, documentation, safety, and field operations.

Other:

This position is safety sensitive. It is subject to pre-employment and/or periodic background checks, motor vehicle records (MVR) and drug testing.

Driving Requirements:

Must possess a valid driver's license, must be at least 21 years of age. Must maintain a satisfactory driving record to safely operate company vehicles.

*This position description is a general guideline for work behavior and is not intended to be a comprehensive listing of all job duties. Therefore, it is also not, nor can it be implied to be, a contract of employment. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential tasks. Must be able to successfully complete an intense background investigation.*

Job Description:

Seize your opportunity to make a personal impact supporting the Case Management Modernization (CMM) Program. The CMM program is an initiative to support the Administrative Office of the US Courts (AO) in developing a modern, cloud-based solution to support all 204+ federal courts across the United States.


GDIT is your place to make meaningful contributions to challenging projects and grow a rewarding career. The Business Intelligence (BI) Developer will be part of the CMM Data Modernization and Governance team responsible for delivering an integrated data governance, engineering, data platform, reporting, analytics, and Artificial Intelligence (AI)/Machine Learning (ML) capabilities that support operational decision-making and fulfill AO's data and analytics objectives in support of the CMM program.


The successful candidate will be responsible for delivering advanced reporting, analytics, visualizations, statistical modeling, and AI/ML capabilities that provide data-driven decision-support tools and actionable insights to users and stakeholders of the CMM application. This role oversees design, development, integration, and continuous enhancement of dashboards, reporting tools, predictive analytics, and AI/ML capabilities in alignment with strict federal compliance requirements.


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

The Business Intelligence (BI) Developer will execute the following responsibilities:


Reporting & Analytics

  • Develop and integrate configurable dashboards, self-service reporting capabilities, and predictive analytics within the CMM application.
  • Designs intuitive, interactive dashboards and visualizations that communicate business insights effectively.
  • Coordinate and implement data replication or feeds required to support downstream stakeholders and external systems.
  • Continuously monitor system performance to ensure 95% or greater of analytical queries meet defined Service Level Agreement (SLA) response times monthly, including dashboard load times of five seconds or less.
  • Drive user adoption of dashboards and reporting tools, with monthly usage across targets users.
  • Collaborate with product owners, data engineers, and UX designers to ensure seamless integration of analytics features into the CMM user experience.
  • Partner with business leaders, data engineers, analysts, and program leadership to translate business requirements and KPIs into actionable technical designs and insights.
  • Build and enhance dashboards and reports in approved BI tools, ensuring performance and usability at scale.
  • Implement and validate SQL logic, calculations, and metric definitions across reporting products.
  • Coordinate with Data Engineering to resolve upstream data issues and curate data for reporting.
  • Apply visualization standards and documentation so reports are consistent, interpretable, and support adoption.
  • Ensure reporting artifacts comply with privacy, access control, and data handling requirements.
  • Establish and enforce data governance frameworks, standards, and best practices ensuring data accuracy, consistency, classification, and security.
  • Drive continuous improvement of BI platforms through performance tuning, automation, metadata management, and advanced analytics (predictive and self-service BI).
  • Support delivery of architecture design documents, governance artifacts, data lineage, and metadata catalog processes.

AI/ML Capabilities

  • Support and consume AI/ML solutions with adherence to government compliance standards.
  • Establish, maintain, and oversee a master AI/ML Capability Register documenting all proposed, in-review, approved, and rejected capabilities, including status tracking, submission dates, and authorization history.
  • Implement responsible AI/ML practices aligned with federal requirements, ensuring transparency, risk mitigation, fairness, and compliance.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • MA/MS degree with 5+ years or BS/BA degree with 7+ years of general experience in information systems and 5+ years of specialized experience.
  • Experience may be considered in lieu of degree.
  • Expertise in python, SQL & data transformations supporting large-scale analytical data systems.
  • Strong hands-on experience with BI tools such as Qlik (preferred), AWS QuickSight (preferred), Power BI, or Tableau.
  • Advanced SQL skills and experience working with analytical data models and semantic layers.
  • Experience delivering reporting in regulated or high-sensitivity data environment.
  • Experience assisting with testing, by writing acceptance criteria & confirming test cases results.
  • Experience with producing relevant and current requirements, sizing user stories correctly, and removing roadblocks prior to sprints start.


REQUIRED COMMUNICATION & ORGANIZATIONAL SKILLS

  • Excellent presentation and communication (oral and written) skills.
  • Consultant mindset with the ability to work with high level customer stakeholders and build excellent customer relationships.
  • Experience identifying and applying industry tools, solutions, methods best practices, and emerging technologies.
  • Strong analytical skills and problem-solving skills with the ability to formulate and communicate recommendations for improvement.
  • Demonstrated ability to work effectively, independently, and as part of a team.

PREFERRED CERTIFICATIONS

One or more of the following certifications is preferred:

  • Data Visualization and Data Story Telling certifications
  • Qlik Sense Business Analyst

title: Law and/or Graduate Student - Part-Time Research Assistant
description:
APPLICATION INSTRUCTIONS:

  • CURRENT PENN STATE EMPLOYEE (faculty, staff, technical service, or student), please login to Workday to complete the internal application process. Please do not apply here, apply internally through Workday.

  • CURRENT PENN STATE STUDENT (not employed previously at the university) and seeking employment with Penn State, please login to Workday to complete the student application process. Please do not apply here, apply internally through Workday.

  • If you are NOT a current employee or student, please click “Apply” and complete the application process for external applicants.

Approval of remote and hybrid work is not guaranteed regardless of work location. For additional information on remote work at Penn State, see Notice to Out of State Applicants.

JOB DESCRIPTION AND POSITION REQUIREMENTS

The Department of Agricultural Economics, Sociology, and Education is seeking a law and/or graduate student research assistant to support a project to create a database cataloguing state immigration policies across the United States from 1989-2026. The RA will work directly with the study PI and a team of RAs to clean and code state legislative data. The RA will specifically work with the PI to read through and code state bills pertaining to immigrants and immigration. This position is for both the fall 2026 and spring 2027 semesters, with the possibility of extension into summer 2027. The RA’s tasks will include the following:

  • Read state legislation on immigrants/immigration.
  • Systematically code legislation for a series of indicators following an established coding protocol.
  • Enter the coded information into a structured spreadsheet
  • Assist in cleaning collected state legislative data, checking for accuracy and consistency.
  • Communicate regularly with the PI on progress and participate in regular team meetings.

Required qualifications:

  • Interest and/or formal specialization in U.S. immigration law, social/public policy.
  • Interest in gaining familiarity with social science and/or legal/legislative research.
  • General familiarity with Excel and/or Google Sheets.
  • Excellent self-management skills.
  • Ability to work independently, meet deadlines, and stay organized with minimal day-to-day supervision.
  • Strong attention to detail and comfort with repetitive, careful data work.
  • Strong written and oral communication skills.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Prior research assistant experience involving data entry/management.
  • Experience with social science and/or legal/legislative research.

How to apply

Please include a current resume/CV, and one or two paragraphs detailing your interest in the position and any relevant experience.

Candidates who advance to the next stage in the hiring process will be contacted to schedule a 30-45 minute interview and will be asked to complete a sample data coding exercise.

BACKGROUND CHECKS/CLEARANCES

Employment with the University will require successful completion of background check(s) in accordance with University policies.

Pursuant to the Jeanne Clery Disclosure of Campus Security Policy and Campus Crime Statistics Act and the Pennsylvania Act of 1988, Penn State publishes a combined Annual Security and Annual Fire Safety Report (ASR). The ASR includes crime statistics and institutional policies concerning campus security, such as those concerning alcohol and drug use, crime prevention, the reporting of crimes, sexual assault, and other matters. The ASR is available for review here.

title: Exec. Director, Biostatistics
description:
COMPANY:

At BioCryst, we share a deep commitment to improving the lives of people living with hereditary angioedema (HAE) and other rare diseases. We leverage our expertise in structure-guided drug design to develop first-in-class or best-in-class oral small-molecule and injectable protein therapeutics. Our global headquarters is in Durham, North Carolina, we have a regional office in Boston, Massachusetts, and our employees span the globe across sites in multiple countries. We are proud of our culture of engagement and accountability that rewards people for innovative thinking and achievement of key objectives. For more information, please visit our website at or follow us on LinkedIn and Instagram.


JOB SUMMARY:


As Exec. Director, Biostatistics, this individual leads the conduct and analysis of all BioCryst-sponsored clinical studies from Phase I to Phase IV as well as selected non-clinical studies. The role requires technical expertise as well as vendor management capabilities. The individual in this role is responsible for the appropriate use of statistical thinking and methods and conformance to principles of GCP, as applicable to biostatistics and programming. S/he is also responsible for the identification, evaluation, and implementation of new processes and technologies related to biostatistics and programming as well as outsourcing strategy, in alignment with the goals of Biostatistics & Data Science.


S/he may act as project statistician for an individual project. Performance in this role relies on an extensive experience base in study design, regulatory strategy and programming, sound judgment to plan and accomplish goals, and an ability to lead and direct the work of others. A wide scope of creativity and latitude is expected. and direct the work of others. A wide scope of creativity and latitude is expected.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:


• Responsible for Biostatistics support of BioCryst-sponsored clinical studies as well as selected non-clinical studies and Biostatistics support of Medical Affairs.

• Ensures the relevance and adequacy of statistical methods employed in BioCryst-sponsored clinical development activities and selected nonclinical studies.

• Ensures conformance to relevant regulatory guidelines and Good Clinical Practice.

• Ensures that Biostatistics effectively contributes to the formulation of clinical development strategies as regards optimal development program and study design.

• Responsible for Biostatistics oversight of CRO/contract staff for performance of outsourced operational activities. Reviews and approves contracts, work orders, and invoices within grant of authority.

• Act as project statistician for an individual project.

• Participation in FDA and other regulatory agency meetings as the Company’s spokesperson for biostatistical topics.

• Thinks outside of the regulatory biostatistics box (e.g. maximum learning from phase 2 experiments regardless of pre-specified SAP, experience in Phase 3b/4 design and analysis to maximize a product’s life cycle).

• Participation in organization-wide process definition, creation, and implementation with a continuous focus on efficiency and productivity enhancement.

• Definition, monitoring, and evaluation of relevant performance metrics.

• Author/ reviewer of relevant sections of all critical documents required to support development of Company’s products including clinical study protocols, statistical analysis plans, data management plans, regulatory briefing documents, regulatory dossiers such as NDAs and MAAs, responses to regulatory questions, scientific abstracts and manuscripts.

• Responsible for accuracy of data included in public corporate communications of BioCryst clinical trial results, including press releases, slide presentations, SEC filings, scientific meeting abstracts, and published manuscripts. Responsible for monitoring quality audit process for those communications.

• Ability to communicate technical concepts to technical or regulatory audiences, and to broader audiences in a nontechnical manner without loss of rigor.

• All other duties as assigned.

EXPERIENCE & QUALIFICATIONS:


• Ph.D. in Biostatistics (or related field) with at least 12 years’ experience in the pharmaceutical industry, 10 or more years’ experience in the design, analysis and interpretation of clinical trials or an equivalent combination of education and experience. Deep understanding of SAS programming is sufficient to provide oversight of statistical programming and ability to program as needed. Management experience preferred.

• Strong leadership and interpersonal skills.

• NDA filing experience: key contributor to one or more successful product approvals.

• Proven expertise with the disciplines, practices and procedures that pertain to biostatistics, programming, and clinical data management, including development and accountability for relevant quality management systems.

• Demonstrated knowledge of the clinical development process and relevant regulatory guidelines and requirements.

• Experience with Data Monitoring Committees and\or study steering committees.

• Takes a hands-on approach (e.g. will do analyses him/herself when necessary).

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

• Proven team player with ability to work well in a collegial environment: willing to challenge the status quo.

• Experience with European and Japanese regulatory agencies.

• Formal expertise and experience in Bayesian statistics as well as frequentist statistics.

• Experience supporting medical affairs and post-marketing studies is an added benefit.

• Flexible scheduling and ability to travel internationally.

• “Small-company attitude” that embraces change within a high-risk environment.

• Responsiveness and ability to prioritize effectively.

The statements in this position description are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by people assigned to this classification. They are not intended to be construed as an exhaustive list of responsibilities, duties, and skills required of personnel so classified. The manager may assign additional responsibilities and assignments from time to time.

title: UX Technical Designer III
description:
Application close date:

Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the requisition is closed.

At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight!

This role supports the development and operations of New Glenn, a single-configuration, heavy-lift orbital launch vehicle capable of routinely carrying people and payloads to low-Earth orbit, geostationary transfer orbit, cislunar, and beyond. Its first stage is fully reusable, and the vehicle was designed from the beginning to be human-capable.

As a UX Technical Designer on the Integrated Ground Systems (IGS) team, you will design the mission critical software that monitors and controls our launch vehicles and ground support systems. As part of a passionate, and highly collaborative team, you will shape the user experience for the mission operators and engineers who make spaceflight possible.

Our team operates on the core belief: Human-Centered Design is essential to building safe, reliable, and efficient systems. This is a unique opportunity to see your work have a tangible impact on the future of spaceflight.

Responsibilities

  • Frame the Problem, Not Just the Solution: Don’t just execute on feature requests. You own the critical "discovery" phase, using research, data, and deep collaboration to define the right problems to solve on behalf of the mission.
  • Own the End-to-End Design Process: Move from ambiguity to clarity by designing the complete user experience. You will drive the process from initial user flows and wireframes to deliver pixel-perfect visual designs and interactive prototypes in Figma.
  • Be the Voice of the User: Embody a deep sense of empathy for our operators. You will engage them directly to understand their world, workflows, and pain points, translating that insight into artifacts including user journeys, scenarios, and task analyses to serve as the team's guide.
  • Build a Stronger Foundation: A primary mission of this role is to improve the quality, consistency, and accessibility of our software. A key part of this effort is actively working to resolve design debt, strengthen and improve our design system and create scalable foundation for future work.
  • Partner with Engineering: Act as a dedicated design partner for developers. You will be responsible for translating user needs into clear design specifications, understanding technical constraints, and ensuring the final product is implemented with exceptional attention to detail.
  • Cultivate a Culture of Humility: Ability to earn trust, maintain positive and professional relationships, and contribute to a culture of inclusion. You will know how to give and receive sharp, kind feedback to make the entire team better.

Qualifications (Minimum Requirements)

  • A strong portfolio is required. Your portfolio reflects shipped products, not just concept work.
  • Bachelor’s degree in HCI, Interaction Design, or a related field, or equivalent years (5+ years) of hands-on experience as a Product Designer.
  • Proven ability to deliver high-quality work in a fast-moving, highly collaborative team environment.
  • High proficiency with modern design and prototyping tools (Figma, Adobe Creative Suite).
  • Exceptional communication skills with the ability to articulate the rationale behind your design decisions.
  • Must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

Desired Qualifications

  • Experience designing for complex, technical, or data-dense applications (e.g., desktop, enterprise).
  • Experience with safety-critical or mission-critical applications (e.g., aerospace, automotive, medical).
  • Experience building or contributing to a robust design system.
  • Knowledge of and experience upholding accessibility standards (WCAG).
  • Familiarity with Agile Scrum practices.
  • Experience with Git, Qt/QML or code authoring test and integration purposes is a strong plus.


Base Pay Range for:

WA applicants is $141,162.00 - $197,626.80

Other site ranges may differ


Culture Statement

Don’t meet all desired requirements? Studies have shown that some people are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single desired qualification. At Blue Origin, we are dedicated to building an authentic workplace, so if you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every desired qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

title: Staff Consultant (Human Factors/Safety)
description:
About ESi

Engineering Systems Inc. (ESi) is an engineering and scientific investigation and failure analysis firm. We are frequently retained by law firms, insurance companies, and manufacturers to answer complex technical questions on projects ranging from small, focused investigations to large-scale, high-profile losses.

Our work spans a wide range of challenges, including major transportation accidents, equipment and product failures, personal injury claims, and damage to residential, commercial, and industrial structures. The variety, complexity, and real-world impact of our projects create deeply fulfilling and intellectually engaging careers for our consultants.

At ESi, you’ll have the opportunity to shape your own path while being supported by a collaborative culture, national expertise, and industry-leading resources.

Why ESi

ESi’s Biomechanics & Safety team conducts multidisciplinary analyses to investigate incidents, determine root causes, and support litigation, while proactively identifying hazards and assessing risk. The team evaluates human factors and safety across products and environments, ensuring compliance with applicable standards in a collaborative, growth-focused setting.

Key Responsibilities

  • Reviews project proposals or plans to determine time frame, funding limitations, procedures for accomplishing project, staffing requirements, and allotment of available resources to various phases of project.
  • Evaluates root causes in industrial, transportation, and consumer product accidents.
  • Confers with project personnel to provide technical advice and to resolve problems.
  • Identifies and reviews existing media (e.g., photographs, video, witness statements, depositions, police and OSHA reports, drawings, etc.) to develop preliminary conclusions and plan further investigation.
  • Conducts inspections of accident scenes and of involved or exemplar vehicles, machines, safety equipment, consumer products, and other items as needed.
  • Locates, assesses pertinence of, and applies consensus safety standards, scientific literature, existing test data, and governmental regulations.
  • Designs and conducts testing and/or develops models to obtain and evaluate human factors data.
  • As part of a team, conducts risk assessments or job safety analyses for a variety of products and industrial machines.
  • Prepares written reports and verbal presentations of findings and conclusions in clear, concise, and easy-to-understand terms.
  • Prepares exhibits with visualization group to clearly communicate complex engineering concepts.
  • Manage projects from initiation to completion. Prepare technical, project-related reports on a timely basis for clients as required.
  • Performs other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

Education / Certifications / Licenses

  • Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Psychology, or related field required.
  • Master’s degree or Ph.D. in Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Psychology, or related field preferred.

Experience

  • 2-5 years’ of work experience in the forensic field with experimental design, human factors consulting, statistical analysis, and/or evidence examination desired. Related educational experience will also be considered.
  • Must have completed academic coursework or received comparable certification in the following topics: engineering, neuropsychology, human-computer interaction, human factors and product design, occupation biomechanics, cognitive engineering and/or work physiology.

Other Technical & Non-Technical Skills

  • Experience in MATLAB, psychopy, and R and the ability to design and write original computational models of human performance and statistical analysis code is desirable.

What We Can Offer You

  • Medical, Dental & Vision

  • 401k with employer match

  • 10 paid holidays (9 standard holidays and 1 floating holiday)
  • Work/Life Balance in a collaborative working environment

  • Career Growth & Continuing education opportunities

The pay range listed reflects a good-faith estimate of the compensation we expect to offer most candidates for this role. Total compensation includes a competitive base salary and bonus opportunity, with final pay determined by job-related factors such as experience, qualifications, individual performance, and overall company performance.

After internal discussions and market research, the current pay band for this opportunity is $110,000 to $180,000.

Physical Demands:

This role requires frequently sitting or standing for extended periods of time and occasionally lifting and/or moving items weighing up to 50 pounds, with infrequent lifting up to 75 pounds. The work regularly requires bending, twisting, kneeling, crouching, and maintaining balance. This position frequently requires handling and operating specialized tools and equipment and working in a variety of physical positions, including occasionally accessing tight or confined spaces. title: Research Intern (PhD), AI-Scale Protocols & Simulation
description:
About Marvell

Marvell’s semiconductor solutions are the essential building blocks of the data infrastructure that connects our world. Across enterprise, cloud and AI, and carrier architectures, our innovative technology is enabling new possibilities.

Your Team, Your Impact

Marvell is a global leader in high-performance silicon and AI infrastructure, powering the world's most advanced datacenters, cloud platforms, 5G networks, and AI/ML workloads. Our innovations drive next-generation computing, networking, and storage — enabling breakthrough performance, scalability, and efficiency for the most demanding applications.

Why This Internship

* Engage with open research problems at the frontier of AI systems — challenges that require access to real silicon, large-scale infrastructure, and production data
* Contribute to work intended for publication, with support for presenting results both internally and externally
* Translate research outcomes into real products and next-generation silicon, extending impact beyond publication
* Collaborate with and receive mentorship from senior architects and researchers who will help advance your ideas
* Gain access to advanced infrastructure, tools, and pre-release hardware rarely available in academic settings
* Pursue original, exploratory research directions — independent thinking is actively encouraged

What You Can Expect

Focus: Explore how tomorrow's AI networks will behave at scale — using simulation to study scale-up and scale-out protocols, congestion, and the interplay between workloads, fabrics, and hardware before they ever reach silicon.

Key Responsibilities

  • Investigate emerging scale-up and scale-out protocols and how they perform under real AI workloads
  • Explore and extend simulation platforms to model networking and congestion-control behavior at scale
  • Experiment with AI-scale and LLM-serving simulation, and workload/trace-driven modeling (e.g., Astra-Sim, Chakra, htsim)
  • Study and evaluate protocol performance, scalability, and resilience across topologies
  • Correlate simulation results with architectural and hardware behavior to uncover new insights

What We're Looking For

Eligibility: Enrolled in a PhD, MS by Research, or MTech by Research program in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, electronics or Electrical Engineering or a related field.

Requirements

  • Strong fundamentals in computer networks, transport protocols, and distributed systems
  • Curiosity about large-scale simulation and a desire to work with frameworks such as Astra-Sim, Chakra, htsim, ns-3, gem5, or SST
  • Understanding of scale-up/scale-out fabrics, RDMA, or congestion control — or eagerness to go deep
  • Programming in C++ and Python

Preferred: Interest in LLM-serving and AI-workload simulation, next-generation datacenter networking, protocol design, or large-scale performance analysis.

title: Security Operations Analyst II
description:
Do you enjoy getting hands-on with complex security investigations rather than simply triaging alerts? Are you confident working across Microsoft Defender, Sentinel and KQL to understand what is really happening behind an event? Do you know when to investigate independently and when an incident needs to be escalated?


CFA Institute is looking for a Security Operations Analyst II to join our Security Operations Center and strengthen our in-house cybersecurity capability. You will operate as a highly capable security analyst across monitoring, investigation, incident response and threat hunting, working between our managed security service and senior Security Operations specialists.


You will join at an important point for the team, taking meaningful ownership of day-to-day security operations while helping us continue to mature areas including proactive threat hunting and investigative capability.


What You’ll Do


  • Investigate security alerts and events across endpoints, identities, email, cloud services and network infrastructure, determining whether activity is malicious or legitimate.
  • Use Microsoft Defender XDR, Microsoft Sentinel and KQL to investigate suspicious activity, correlate telemetry and identify indicators of compromise and attacker behaviours.
  • Independently own routine and moderately complex investigations, determining scope, severity and potential business impact and escalating when specialist or senior support is required.
  • Review escalated security cases and work closely with our managed security service provider and senior analysts to ensure investigations are thorough and appropriately handled.
  • Support incident response across identification, investigation, containment and recovery, including collecting and analysing evidence to establish investigative timelines.
  • Investigate phishing, suspicious email activity, credential compromise and cloud or identity-related security events.
  • Contribute to the development of more proactive threat-hunting capability, using security telemetry and investigative queries to identify potential threats.
  • Recommend improvements to detection coverage, hunting queries, playbooks and investigation procedures based on what you uncover.
  • Translate technical findings into clear, useful information for technical and non-technical stakeholders, including contributing to executive-ready security briefings when required.
  • Participate in a rotational on-call schedule supporting significant or time-sensitive security incidents.

What We’re Looking For


  • Hands-on professional experience within a Security Operations Center, cybersecurity operations or a closely related technical security environment.
  • Practical experience with Microsoft Defender and/or Microsoft Sentinel, with the ability to use the Microsoft security environment as part of real investigations.
  • Hands-on experience using KQL to query security data, investigate suspicious activity or support threat hunting.
  • Strong understanding of SIEM and EDR/XDR technologies and how their telemetry is used during an investigation.
  • Demonstrable experience investigating security alerts and incidents across areas such as endpoints, identity, email and cloud environments.
  • Experience investigating phishing, suspicious email activity and potential credential compromise.
  • The technical judgment to work independently through complex or ambiguous situations while recognising when escalation is the right course of action.
  • Understanding of incident-response processes, security investigation methodologies and attacker tactics and techniques, including familiarity with MITRE ATT&CK.
  • Strong communication skills, including the ability to turn detailed technical findings into clear information for different audiences.
  • A curious, continuously learning approach to cybersecurity and a genuine interest in keeping pace with emerging threats, technologies and investigative techniques.

Why Join Us


  • Join an in-house Security Operations team where you will have meaningful ownership of investigations rather than operating solely within an initial alert queue.
  • Work across a broad security control environment, with significant hands-on exposure to Microsoft security technologies.
  • Help strengthen and mature CFA Institute’s proactive threat-hunting and broader Security Operations capability.
  • Work closely with experienced security specialists and contribute to investigations that have visibility across technology and senior leadership.
  • Gain exposure to evolving areas of the security portfolio, including threat intelligence, data protection and brand protection.
  • Join at a point where the Security Operations function is evolving, giving you the opportunity to contribute to how its capabilities, detections and investigative practices develop.

Center of Technical Excellence Vehicle Structures Process Integrator

We, at Aeronautics Systems, are reshaping our Engineering organization to drive stronger execution and faster decision making, while equipping our teams with the processes, tools, and technical training needed to succeed and grow. As a member of the Center of Technical Excellence (CoTE) team, you will be at the heart of this transformation, driving relentless improvement and ensuring that our technical capabilities stay ahead of emerging challenges and opportunities.

The Aeronautics Engineering organization is seeking an Engineer Aeronautical/ Principal Engineer Aeronautical – Vehicle Structures Integration to support the Vehicle Structures technical discipline within the newly established Vehicle Engineering (VE) CoTE. This role reports to the Aeronautics Systems (AS) Vehicle Integration Manager within the VE CoTE and is responsible for supporting the development of discipline-specific processes, technical manuals, and training to elevate technical excellence across the Vehicle Structures discipline.

The Engineer Aeronautical/ Principal Engineer Aeronautical – Vehicle Structures Integration candidate will work closely with all the Vehicle Structures Discipline Process Technical Owners (DPTO) to deliver Sector wide technical discipline capabilities for processes, tools, and training within the Design, Structural Analysis, Material & Process, Liaison and Standard Parts disciplines. As an integrator, you will leverage prior execution experience and subject matter expertise within the CoTE and across the Sector to support continued development of discipline products, ensuring process excellence and promote compliance in collaboration with program technical leaders.

The ideal Engineer Aeronautical/ Principal Engineer Aeronautical – Vehicle Structures Integration candidate combines an understanding and practical experience within the greater discipline with a passion for technical training and development, collaboration, and continuous improvement, a vision for digital solutions and integration within the ecosystem. This integrator will collaborate closely with other VE discipline leads and integrators within the CoTE.

Responsibilities will include, but are not limited to:

  • Support strategic vision, operations and technical priorities for Vehicle Structures, aligned to long-term Sector strategy.
  • Support projects with direction from the Design, Structural Analysis, Material & Process, Liaison and Standard Parts DPTOs, with a focus on process, tool, and training development, with a goal to strengthen technical excellence and workforce capabilities that result in improved business results.
  • Partner with NG Fellows within the Vehicle Structures disciplines to advance Sector- and Enterprise-wide emerging technologies and future workforce capabilities.
  • Supports the development and maintenance of Vehicle Structures Principles and Operating Practices (PrOP), Process Asset Library (PAL) manuals, and Nimbus Process Models, ensuring technical excellence and compliance in partnership with program execution teams

This requisition may be filled at an Engineer Aeronautical, Structural, Material Processing / Principal Engineer Aeronautical, Structural, Material Processing level based on the qualifications below.

  • Experience utilizing Vehicle Structures methods, tools, standards, and processes
  • Experience working with multi-disciplinary teams and geographically dispersed teams
  • Experience with or exposure to digital design initiatives and solutions
  • Must have an active DoD secret or higher clearance (with a background investigation completed within the last 6 years or currently enrolled into Continuous Evaluation) and eligibility for Top Secret/SCI
  • Must be able to attain and maintain Special Program Access (PAR)

Principal Engineer Aeronautical – Vehicle Structures Integration
