title: Technology Process Re-Engineering, Vice President
description:
Who we are looking for

We are seeking a Vice President, Technology Process Re-Engineering, to lead priority process mapping and re-engineering initiatives across State Street Global Technology Services. Reporting to the Managing Director, Head of Technology Process Re-Engineering, this role will execute the team’s standards and methodology, develop clear end-to-end process views, and deliver practical improvements that simplify execution, strengthen controls, and improve operational transparency.

The ideal candidate is an experienced technology transformation and process improvement leader with strong capabilities in process mapping, operating model analysis, and process re-engineering within a large, complex, and regulated organization. This individual must be able to translate fragmented knowledge into clear process maps, facilitate cross-functional decisions, and manage improvement work from analysis through implementation.

This is a hands-on GTS-facing leadership role that will partner with technology process owners, risk partners, platform teams, and global delivery organizations. The Vice President will apply the standards, tooling, and governance established by the Head of Technology Process Re-Engineering while leading assigned workstreams, coaching team members, and ensuring that redesigned processes are implemented and sustained.

What you will be responsible for

GTS Technology Process Mapping Delivery

  • Apply the GTS technology process mapping methodology, standards, taxonomy, and tools to assigned priority processes, and provide practical feedback to improve the team’s approach.
  • Develop and maintain clear end-to-end views of priority GTS processes, connecting activities, roles, systems, handoffs, controls, pain points, and performance indicators to improve transparency and accountability.
  • Lead assigned process mapping and re-engineering workstreams, coordinate contributions from team members and subject matter experts across global locations, and ensure consistent quality, timely delivery, and effective stakeholder engagement.

Process Re-engineering, Optimization & Control Improvement

  • Conduct structured process analysis to identify duplication, fragmentation, manual workarounds, unclear ownership, control gaps, and opportunities to simplify, standardize, or automate execution.
  • Facilitate working sessions with GTS process owners and transformation teams to design future-state processes, clarify roles and decision rights, document requirements, and develop practical implementation plans.
  • Define and track measurable outcomes for assigned re-engineering initiatives, including reduced complexity, improved cycle times, stronger control alignment, clearer accountability, and better management information.

Governance, Quality & Reporting

  • Execute governance routines that keep assigned process maps current, validated, owned, and aligned to GTS standards, control expectations, and management reporting needs.
  • Prepare concise, executive-ready reporting on process coverage, delivery progress, key risks, improvement opportunities, open decisions, and realized outcomes; escalate issues and recommendations to the Head of Technology Process Re-Engineering.

Stakeholder Engagement & Change Adoption

  • Build effective working relationships across GTS technology, risk, operations, and delivery teams to align on current-state findings, future-state design, priorities, dependencies, and adoption plans.
  • Facilitate fact-based discussions, resolve day-to-day ownership ambiguity, challenge inefficient ways of working constructively, and help teams move from process documentation to measurable and sustained improvement.

What we value

  • Technology Process Delivery: Proven ability to lead complex process mapping and re-engineering workstreams within a large, matrixed technology organization.

Correctional Segreant (SCI) Permanent opportunity for ODOC and OCE employees only

Oregon Department of Corrections

Are you ready to step into a leadership role and take on greater responsibility in maintaining safety, security, and professional development within the facility? We are seeking dedicated and experienced candidates for the position of Correctional Sergeant. This is an excellent opportunity for career advancement while playing a crucial role in maintaining security, overseeing staff, and guiding AICs toward rehabilitation.

Please note: If there are lateral applicant(s), they may be reviewed and interviewed prior to promotional applications.

About the Job – Your Role

As a Correctional Sergeant, you will be a senior security staff member responsible for overseeing custody, control, supervision, and daily care of adults in custody while upholding the mission of the Department. You will serve as a lead worker, ensuring facility operations run smoothly, safely, and efficiently. You will supervise AICs during movement assignments, monitor high-security areas, and conduct security operations such as transports, searches, and emergency response.

In this role, you will also play a key part in staff development, assisting in training and potentially mentoring subordinate staff as a Field Training Officer (FTO). You will lead by example, modeling professionalism, accountability, and behaviors that support rehabilitation efforts.

These positions are represented by American Federation of State, County, and Municipal Employees (AFSCME). This position may be eligible for Police & Fire (P&F) benefits through Public Employees Retirement System (PERS), as defined by statute.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Two (2) years of experience in a correctional security setting where your primary duties were the care and custody of AICs;
  • Be able to obtain, within two weeks, an Oregon Department of Public Safety Standards and Training (DPSST) Correctional Certificate OR a Correctional Certificate from another government agency;
  • Possess a High School Diploma or GED certificate;
  • Be 21 years of age or older;
  • United States Citizen.

Education will not be accepted as a substitute for the required experience.

Special Qualifications

  • Ability to obtain a valid Oregon motor vehicle operator's license.

Required

  • Must be a current for ODOC and OCE employee (temporary and contract workers excluded) to apply.

About the Department

The Oregon Department of Corrections is responsible for over 12,000 adults in custody in 12 state prisons throughout Oregon. It advises and evaluates counties regarding administration of probation and parole programs supervising more than 24,000 offenders in Oregon communities. The mission is to protect communities, promote accountability, and transform lives.

The Oregon Department of Corrections serves a diverse and changing population of people who are incarcerated and on supervision. We commit to creating an organization both reflecting the diversity of the population we serve and ensuring all employees thrive in a culture of safety, trust, and belonging. We strive to be an anti-racist corrections system. Welcoming, inclusive, and respectful of all people. Free of discrimination, harassment, and retaliation.

The Department offers a variety of programs and opportunity to create a safe and healthy environment to for our staff, volunteers, and adults in custody. Joining the Oregon Department of Corrections is joining a team working for the benefit of our communities through innovative and proven correctional practices.

Chickasaw Nation Industries, Inc. serves as a holding company with multiple subsidiaries engaged in several lines of business (Business Services, Health, Infrastructure and Engineering, Mission Optimization, Technology and Transportation) for the federal government and commercial enterprises. The ability to obtain, maintain and access classified information at the Top Secret/SCI level, which requires U.S. Citizenship

Involved in the performance of assessments of systems and networks within the networking environment or enclave and identifies where those systems/networks deviate from acceptable configurations, enclave policy, or local policy. title: AI Product Owner- GSM
description:
Rockwell Automation is a global technology leader focused on helping the world’s manufacturers be more productive, sustainable, and agile. With more than 28,000 employees who make the world better every day, we know we have something special. Behind our customers - amazing companies that help feed the world, provide life-saving medicine on a global scale, and focus on clean water and green mobility - our people are energized problem solvers that take pride in how the work we do changes the world for the better.

We welcome all makers, forward thinkers, and problem solvers who are looking for a place to do their best work. And if that’s you we would love to have you join us!

Job Description

The AI Product Owner serves as the primary business liaison between GSM (Global Sales and Marketing) functions and the GSM AI delivery team. You will identify business challenges and lead discovery. You will gather and clarify requirements, prioritize AI opportunities, and partner with experts. These experts include AI Developers, Enablement Specialists, Process Architects, and Project Managers. Together, you will deliver solutions that improve productivity, efficiency, and user experience.



You will translate needs into actionable work, own use cases through discovery and delivery, maintain priorities, coordinate stakeholder decisions, and confirm that solutions achieve intended outcomes. The AI Product Owner is not accountable for enterprise AI strategy or portfolio governance. Instead, you will drive execution of the GSM AI roadmap through business partnership, disciplined product ownership, and use-case leadership.



Your Responsibilities:


Discovery & Problem Definition


  • Partner with GSM stakeholders to identify business challenges, users, workflows, pain points, and desired outcomes.
  • Define current and future-state processes, scope, constraints, dependencies, and important partners.
  • Focus on the underlying business need rather than a predetermined solution.

Requirements & Backlog Management


  • Gather, validate, and document requirements, user stories, use cases, and acceptance criteria.
  • Manage and maintain the backlog, including enhancements, defects, priorities, dependencies, and decisions.
  • Ensure work is clearly defined and development ready before execution.

Prioritization & Governance


  • Assess requests based on business value, user impact, complexity, risk, readiness, and capacity.
  • Recommend priorities, tradeoffs, and sequencing to GSM AI leadership.
  • Escalate unresolved ownership, policy, funding, data, or capacity issues when needed.

Solution Delivery


  • Partner with Process Architects and AI Developers to translate business needs into effective solutions.
  • Support backlog refinement, design reviews, testing, demonstrations, and acceptance activities.
  • Manage scope changes and ensure partners understand impacts and dependencies.

Pilot & Adoption


  • Define pilot objectives, success criteria, participants, and feedback mechanisms.
  • Collect and translate user feedback into prioritized improvements and adoption actions.
  • Partner with enablement and business leaders to support communications, training, and change management.

Value Realization


  • Establish success measures and expected outcomes upfront.
  • Monitor adoption, usability, efficiency, and business impact metrics.
  • Identify opportunities for continuous improvement, reuse, and broader AI adoption.

Stakeholder Communication


  • Provide transparent updates on scope, priorities, decisions, risks, and outcomes.
  • Maintain alignment between business needs, delivered capabilities, user feedback, and measured results.
  • Ensure work is paused or closed when ownership, readiness, value, or priority is insufficient.

The Essentials - You Will Have:


  • Bachelor's Degree in Relevant Field
  • Legal authorization to work in the U.S. We will not sponsor individuals for employment visas, now or in the future, for this job opening.

title: Principal Technical Lead Engineer, Rocket Engine Avionics & Control Systems
description:
Application close date:

Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the requisition is closed.

At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight!

This role is part of the Blue Origin Engines business unit, where our focus is the design, development, manufacturing, and testing of engines and propulsion systems. Built for multiple uses, our family of engines is powering the next generation of rockets for commercial, civil, national security, and human spaceflight.

This position resides within the Avionics & Control Products (ACP) organization, part of the Engine Business Unit. As a Principal Technical Lead Engineer for Rocket Engine Avionics & Control Systems, you will serve as the primary technical authority for all avionics systems within a specific rocket engine program. In this role you will define and drive the technical architecture, own the avionics system technical baseline for your assigned engine, lead design reviews with full technical approval authority, and ensure all avionics and control system deliverables are executed to the highest standards of safety, performance, and reliability.

The successful candidate is a seasoned technical leader and recognized expert in avionics and control systems. Your effectiveness stems from four integrated competency areas: (1) Technical Expertise — deep domain knowledge in aerospace electronics, embedded software, controls algorithms, sensors, actuators, power systems, and data networks, combined with systems-level thinking that anticipates downstream impacts of design decisions; (2) Technical Leadership — sound judgment that balances innovation with reliability, fluency in design reviews, failure analysis acumen, and confident decision-making under uncertainty; (3) People & Team Dynamics — mentorship mindset, cross-functional influence, composure under pressure, and a collaborative style that fosters innovation and resilience; and (4) Strategic Vision & Organizational Impact — tying technical decisions to mission success and business goals, identifying organizational gaps before they escalate, and communicating a compelling technical vision across all levels. You hold yourself and your teams to the highest standards of engineering rigor.

There is no “standard day” for this role. You will lead a multi-disciplinary engineering team across all engineering development phases, from customer use case elicitation all the way to full-scale hot-fire test and flight operations. On any given day you may be architecting a new generation engine control system, leading a failure review board, reviewing a control algorithm for stability margins, driving interface negotiations with vehicle teams, or mentoring a group of engineers through a gnarly systems integration challenge. Your breadth of expertise and technical judgment are the constant that ties it all together.

Position requires up to 10% travel to rocket engine test sites.

Responsibilities:

  • Own the avionics and control system technical baseline for the assigned rocket engine program; define and drive the technical vision, architecture, and long-term engineering roadmap for that program’s avionics and control systems.
  • Lead decomposition and allocation of engine-specific avionics requirements; establish and maintain system-level requirements, interface control documents, and design standards for avionics and engine control subsystems.
  • Lead all design reviews for the assigned engine avionics systems with full technical approval authority; participate as a non-advocate reviewer for cross-program architectural decisions.
  • Identify, characterize, and drive resolution of complex system-level technical risks across multiple concurrent development programs.
  • Provide technical oversight and direction for the integration of avionics hardware, software, control algorithms, sensors, affectors, and harnessing into test facilities and onto rocket engines.
  • Develop and maintain model-based design frameworks, simulation environments, and hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) test strategies to accelerate verification and validation.
  • Collaborate with program leadership, chief engineers, and functional managers to align technical execution with cost, schedule, and mission objectives.
  • Champion engineering best practices, design criteria, and lessons learned across the ACP organization.
  • Lead identification, assessment, and mitigation of technical risks across the assigned engine avionics system; drive technology maturation and identify emerging technology opportunities within the engine avionics team.
  • Mentor and develop engineers at all levels; actively contribute to a culture of technical excellence, psychological safety, and continuous learning.
  • Support and provide technical oversight during critical test campaigns and flight operations, both on-site and remotely.
  • Partner with Enterprise functions (Operations, Supply Chain, Mission Assurance) to ensure producibility, reliability, and cost-effectiveness of avionics and control system designs.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Passion for our mission: Millions of people living and working in space!
  • Minimum of a B.S. degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Systems Engineering, or closely related technical field.
  • 10+ years of experience in avionics systems, control systems, or a closely related engineering field, with demonstrated progression to senior/lead technical roles.
  • Deep, hands-on expertise in avionics architecture, embedded systems design, and control system development for flight or propulsion applications.
  • Proven track record of leading complex, cross-functional technical programs or subsystems from concept through qualification and operational deployment.
  • Strong working knowledge of control theory, digital signal processing, and closed-loop system design for engine or propulsion applications.
  • Experience defining and managing system-level requirements, interfaces, and verification/validation strategies across hardware and software domains.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead and influence technical teams and stakeholders without direct authority.
  • Proficiency in model-based design and simulation tools (e.g., MATLAB/Simulink) and scripting languages (Python or equivalent).
  • Experience with data communication protocols (e.g., EtherCAT, CAN, SpaceWire, MIL-STD-1553, or similar).
  • Demonstrated ability to build trusting and effective working relationships that improve team performance, deliver results, and strengthen our culture of inclusivity.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to clearly convey complex technical topics to audiences including senior leadership.
  • Must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • M.S. or Ph.D. in a relevant engineering discipline.
  • Experience across multiple rocket engine or propulsion programs in varying stages of development (early development through flight operations).
  • Familiarity with safety-critical software development standards (e.g., DO-178C, IEC 61508, or equivalent).
  • Experience with fault detection, isolation, and recovery (FDIR) design for flight-critical avionics systems.
  • Proficiency in Rust, C, or C++ for embedded or real-time systems development.
  • Experience with physics-based modeling tools (e.g., AMESIM, Modelica, or similar) for propulsion system simulation.
  • Familiarity with configuration management, requirements management, and product lifecycle management tools (e.g., Windchill, DOORS, or similar).
  • Experience supporting or leading test campaigns at rocket engine test facilities.
  • Demonstrated ability to develop and maintain multi-year product and technology roadmaps.

title: Cyber All-Source Intelligence Analyst
description:
Cyber All-Source Intelligence Analyst

The Opportunity:

Our clients need skilled analysts to turn reams of data into actionable intelligence for our government and military every day. If you have strong analytical skills and a problem-solving mindset, are familiar with intelligence tradecraft standards, and are ready to help our nation's leaders understand the critical threats and opportunities facing our country, we have an opportunity for you. Join our team as a Cyber All-Source Analyst.

In this role, you’ll review reporting from classified and unclassified intelligence streams every day as you build assessments that reflect the priorities of your regional or topical portfolios. You'll develop specific products by request and propose your own, coordinate with analysts on our team and across the intelligence community (IC), and brief warfighters, senior policymakers, and IC members on our analytic lines. Thanks to our mentoring and training resources, you'll also be able to hone your skills and mature into a stronger analyst. Our world is shifting quickly, and our clients need analysts who can help them stay several steps ahead.

Join us. The world can’t wait.


You Have:

  • Experience with all-source intelligence analysis and production on foreign national cyber military capabilities and foreign use of cyberspace, including doctrine, intent, operations, supporting services and infrastructure, and vulnerabilities
  • Ability to develop high-quality deliverables tailored to senior policymakers or defense stakeholders, including complex written products and formal or informal briefings
  • Active TS/SCI clearance; willingness to take a polygraph exam
  • HS diploma or GED and 7+ years of experience with analysis or Bachelor’s degree and 3+ years of experience with analysis

Nice If You Have:

  • Experience authoring current DoD product lines and utilizing ICD 203 tradecraft standards
  • Experience producing vector map products and conducting network analysis using geo­-enabled processes
  • Experience with data analytics, analysis, and visualization
  • Knowledge of the North America AOR or Central America AOR
  • Knowledge of the intelligence cycle


Clearance:

Applicants selected will be subject to a security investigation and may need to meet eligibility requirements for access to classified information; TS/SCI clearance is required.

We encourage you to learn more about our total benefits by visiting the Resource page on our Careers site and reviewing Our Employee Benefits page.

Salary at Booz Allen is determined by various factors, including but not limited to location, the individual’s particular combination of education, knowledge, skills, competencies, and experience, as well as contract-specific affordability and organizational requirements. The projected compensation range for this position is $62,000.00 to $141,000.00 (annualized USD). The estimate displayed represents the typical salary range for this position and is just one component of Booz Allen’s total compensation package for employees. description:

About this role:

Wells Fargo is seeking a Senior Branch Premier Banker (SAFE) to play a pivotal role within our National Branch Network. This role grows, deepens, and manages relationships with affluent customers and those with more complex financial needs, serving as their primary point of contact for banking products and services through scheduled appointments, lobby engagement, and proactive outreach. This role is designed for growth oriented professionals who lead with advice to acquire and deepen relationships through meaningful discovery and translate customer goals into comprehensive financial strategies. You will own and actively grow a defined book of business, leveraging goals based planning, and prudent risk oversight to deliver integrated solutions across deposits, investments, credit, home lending, and business banking. In addition, you’ll help customers with everyday banking needs-opening accounts, handling service requests, and ensuring a seamless experience making it easier for them to manage their banking with confidence. Success in this role is driven by strong relationship acumen, proactive customer engagement, and seamless collaboration with internal partners across Wealth, Home Lending, and Business Banking to deliver a differentiated customer experience.


Wells Fargo rewards behaviors that consistently create long term customer value and support customers in making informed financial decisions. You’ll be supported with digital tools, industry leading training, ongoing coaching, and backed by one of the most recognized brands in banking. This role offers a clear platform for career growth for experienced professionals who excel at building trust, managing a portfolio, and delivering holistic, multi product solutions.


In this role you will:

Employees hired into the Senior Branch Premier Banker LP role who are not fully licensed will participate in the Branch Network Licensed Banker program.

title: Principal Human Factors Engineer
description:
RELOCATION ASSISTANCE: Relocation assistance may be available

CLEARANCE REQUIRED FOR START: Yes

CLEARANCE TYPE: Top Secret

TRAVEL: Yes, 10% of the Time

Description

At Northrop Grumman, our employees have incredible opportunities to work on revolutionary systems that impact people's lives around the world today, and for generations to come. Our pioneering and inventive spirit has enabled us to be at the forefront of many technological advancements in our nation's history - from the first flight across the Atlantic Ocean, to stealth bombers, to landing on the moon. We look for people who have bold new ideas, courage and a pioneering spirit to join forces to invent the future, and have fun along the way. Our culture thrives on intellectual curiosity, cognitive diversity and bringing your whole self to work — and we have an insatiable drive to do what others think is impossible. Our employees are not only part of history, they're making history.

Northrop Grumman Aeronautics Systems is looking to add a Principal Human Factors Engineer to join our team. The position is located on site in Rancho Bernardo, California. This position can also be supported from El Segundo, California or Palmdale, California. This position will be in our Systems Engineering organization.


In this role, your primary roles and responsibilities will include:

  • Support the planning, coordination, and execution of activities to verify user experience (UX) requirements, including conducting evaluations, tests, and demonstrations to ensure requirements are met.
  • Support the evaluation of requirements adhering to Human Factors best practices and specified sections of MIL-STD-1472.
  • Contributions to Human Factors Analyses (including but not limited to: Task Analyses and Predictive Workload Analyses, Usability studies, Workload, and Situation Awareness surveys).
  • Candidates must be able to plan, conduct, summarize and brief user centered design events including Design Thinking Workshops and Operator in the Loop evaluations of system impacts on mission performance.
  • Author/support the program documentation of the HFE processes and products in a format consistent with US Military Data Item Descriptions (e.g. Human Engineering Program Plan, Human Engineering Design Approach Document – Operator, Human Engineering Design Approach Document – Maintainer, Human Engineering Test Plan, Human Engineering Test Report, et. al).
  • Collaboration with Design Integrated Product Teams (IPTs) to ensure evolving design addresses program needs and adheres to Human Interface design requirements
  • Analyze proposed workarounds for system discrepancies to determine whether the workaround is acceptable from an operator perspective
  • Support Airworthiness analysis, artifact development, and compliance summaries.

Basic Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s of Science Degree and 5 years of experience in a Human Factors related field; OR a Master’s degree and 3 years of related experience; OR a PhD and 1 years of related engineering experience.
  • Experience with MIL-STD-1472, Human Factor survey development, test procedure development/execution, and/or test report writing.
  • Ability to work in a dynamic, fast paced environment, Action Oriented, Strong Attention to Detail, Communicates Effectively.
  • Active USG Top Secret clearance (with a background investigation within the past 5 years or enrolled into Continuous Evaluation).
  • Ability to obtain and maintain initial Special Access Program (SAP) access via a Program Access Request (PAR). This SAP/PAR must be obtained prior to commencement of employment and must be obtained within a reasonable amount of time as determined by the company to meet its business needs.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain subsequent SAP PARs following commencement of employment to be able to completely support statement of work

Preferred Qualifications

  • Current applicable Special Access Program (SAP) clearance.
  • Active USG Top Secret SCI clearance (with a background investigation within the past 5 years or enrolled into Continuous Evaluation).
  • Bachelor’s Degree in a STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering or Mathematics) discipline and 5 years of related engineering experience; OR a Master’s degree in a STEM discipline and 3 years of related engineering experience; OR a PhD in a STEM discipline and 1 years of related engineering experience.
  • Military Flight Experience

Primary Level Salary Range: $114,000.00 - $171,000.00

The above salary range represents a general guideline; however, Northrop Grumman considers a number of factors when determining base salary offers such as the scope and responsibilities of the position and the candidate's experience, education, skills and current market conditions.

Depending on the position, employees may be eligible for overtime, shift differential, and a discretionary bonus in addition to base pay. Annual bonuses are designed to reward individual contributions as well as allow employees to share in company results. Employees in Vice President or Director positions may be eligible for Long Term Incentives. In addition, Northrop Grumman provides a variety of benefits including health insurance coverage, life and disability insurance, savings plan, Company paid holidays and paid time off (PTO) for vacation and/or personal business.

The application period for the job is estimated to be 20 days from the job posting date. However, this timeline may be shortened or extended depending on business needs and the availability of qualified candidates.

title: Lead Solutions Specialist, Real Time
description:
FactSet creates flexible, open data and software solutions for over 200,000 investment professionals worldwide, providing instant access to financial data and analytics that investors use to make crucial decisions.


At FactSet, our values are the foundation of everything we do. They express how we act and operate, serve as a compass in our decision-making, and play a big role in how we treat each other, our clients, and our communities. We believe that the best ideas can come from anyone, anywhere, at any time, and that curiosity is the key to anticipating our clients’ needs and exceeding their expectations.


Your Team's Impact :

The Product (Data Solutions) group is responsible for the growth and support of FactSet’s DataFeed (off-platform) products. Our aim is to consult and organize our client’s data consumption processes with FactSet’s proprietary and industry-standard delivery solutions. You will gain exposure to the entire Real Time Data Solutions product suite and learn to design custom solutions tailored to each client using a combination of products.


The Lead Solution Specialist on FactSet’s Real-Time Client Engagement team is a strategic, client-facing role focused on ensuring our institutional clients maximize the performance, stability, and business value of FactSet’s real-time market data solutions. This role blends deep technical knowledge of real-time data architecture with strong client relationship skills to deliver tailored, scalable, and resilient solutions across complex financial workflows. This is a strategic, high-impact role responsible for supporting some of FactSet’s most sophisticated institutional clients.


As a Lead Solution Specialist, you are a trusted technical and strategic partner across onboarding, integration, service optimization, and long-term relationship management for clients leveraging FactSet’s real-time data and infrastructure offerings. Lead Solution Specialists are trusted advisors responsible for driving the long-term success of enterprise clients by ensuring optimal use, stability, and evolution of the products and services they rely on. This role combines technical depth, relationship management, and business acumen. While not always hands-on coding, Lead Solution Specialists must understand the underlying infrastructure, integrations, and client workflows well enough to guide architecture, troubleshoot issues, and influence strategic decisions.

What You'll Do:

Strategic Client Engagement:

  • Serve as the primary technical and strategic contact for key Real-Time clients, driving deployment support, and long-term technical alignment.
  • Develop a deep understanding of each client’s environment, including their use of FactSet’s real-time platforms, data integration strategies, and operational goals.
  • Guide clients through migrations, cloud adoption, entitlement compliance, and architectural changes.

Optimization & Support Escalation:

  • Proactively identify areas for enhancement and coordinate with internal teams to implement solutions.
  • Serve as the escalation point for critical client issues, providing technical leadership through incident response and resolution.
  • Monitor service metrics and usage patterns to proactively address risk, improve resiliency, and drive client satisfaction.

  • Internal Advocacy & Product Feedback:
  • Partner cross-functionally with Product, Engineering, Implementation, Support and Solution Specialists to deliver customized solutions, resolve issues, and influence roadmap enhancements.
  • Act as a voice of the client internally while contributing to the ongoing evolution of FactSet’s real-time offering and engagement model.
  • Provide feedback on product enhancements, documentation, and feature gaps specific to real-time market data delivery.

What Sets a Lead Solution Specialist Apart at FactSet

  • Real-Time Expertise: Strong understanding of real-time data feeds, low-latency architecture, entitlement systems, and cloud-based delivery models.
  • Client-Centric Approach: Proven ability to align technical solutions with business goals, regulatory requirements, and trading workflows.
  • Technical Depth: Experience with Refinitiv, Bloomberg feeds, and familiarity with multicast, entitlement APIs, and real-time distribution platforms.
  • Cross-Functional Leadership: Skilled in navigating internal and external stakeholders to resolve challenges, drive solutions, and influence product direction.
  • Strategic Ownership: Comfortable leading large-scale initiatives such as platform migrations, feed consolidations, or multi-site deployments.

Qualifications

  • 7+ years in a technical client-facing role within financial services, data technology, or capital markets—e.g., Technical Account Manager, Solutions Architect, Technical Consultant.
  • Strong understanding of real-time data delivery, client connectivity, entitlement frameworks, and data workflows across trading and analytics platforms.
  • Experience supporting enterprise clients in cloud or hybrid environments (AWS), with knowledge of APIs, feed handlers, and low-latency infrastructure.
  • Familiarity with market data technologies (e.g. Refinitiv, Bloomberg, proprietary systems).
  • Exceptional client management, communication, and problem-solving skills; confident engaging with both technical and business stakeholders.
  • Scripting or diagnostics skills (Python, SQL, etc.) are a plus.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Finance, Engineering, or a related field.



What's In It For You

At FactSet, our people are our greatest asset, and our culture is our biggest competitive advantage. Being a FactSetter means:

  • The opportunity to join an S&P 500 company with over 45 years of sustainable growth powered by the entrepreneurial spirit of a start-up.
  • Support for your total well-being. This includes health, life, and disability insurance, as well as retirement savings plans and a discounted employee stock purchase program, plus paid time off for holidays, family leave, and company-wide wellness days.
  • Flexible work accommodations. We value work/life harmony and offer our employees a range of accommodations to help them achieve success both at work and in their personal lives.
  • A global community dedicated to volunteerism and sustainability, where collaboration is always encouraged, and individuality drives solutions.
  • Career progression planning with dedicated time each month for learning and development.
  • Business Resource Groups open to all employees that serve as a catalyst for connection, growth, and belonging.

Learn more about our benefits here.


Salary is just one component of our compensation package and is based on several factors including but not limited to education, work experience, and certifications.


The budgeted salary range for this position in New York City is $120,000-$170,000.

Company Overview:

FactSet (NYSE:FDS | NASDAQ:FDS) helps the financial community to see more, think bigger, and work better. Our digital platform and enterprise solutions deliver financial data, analytics, and open technology to more than 8,200 global clients, including over 200,000 individual users. Clients across the buy-side and sell-side, as well as wealth managers, private equity firms, and corporations, achieve more every day with our comprehensive and connected content, flexible next-generation workflow solutions, and client-centric specialized support. As a member of the S&P 500, we are committed to sustainable growth and have been recognized among the Best Places to Work in 2023 by Glassdoor as a Glassdoor Employees’ Choice Award winner. Learn more at www.factset.com and follow us on X and LinkedIn.

title: COMPUTED TOMOGRAPHY (CT) TECHNOLOGIST
description:
CLOSING DATE: Open Until Filled (OUF)

HOURLY RANGE: $32.25 - $40.31

***APPLICANT MUST HAVE A VALID UNRESTRICTED INSURABLE DRIVERS LICENSE***

***RESUME AND REFERENCES ARE REQUIRED***

ESSENTIAL DUTIES, FUNCTIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Performs CT scanning of the human anatomy.
  • Produces ionizing radiation within a safe permissible range as to achieve quality images.
  • Provides proper patient protection in accordance with prescribed safety standards related to radiographic examination. Secures the confidence and cooperation of the patient during examination procedures.
  • Assists with the radiology functions of a patient care facility, including planning and development of departmental policies and procedures.
  • Ensure compliance will all applicable tribal, state, federal laws, policies and regulations.
  • Operate all fixed and portable radiographic systems.
  • Perform duties vital to Diagnostic Radiology and CT Services for Outpatient, Inpatient and Emergency Medicine Services.
  • Ensure all patient orders, lab work and consent forms are complete in a timely manner.
  • Reviews labs and patient history to perform correct exam.
  • Administers IV contrast and oral/rectal contrast when appropriate.
  • Familiarity recognition and responds to any adverse reactions or allergic reactions.
  • Administers IV contrast material by means of existing IV line or by performing venipuncture.
  • Identify and review each patient’s requisition, either with a hard copy or in the computer system, for consistency of examination ordered with clinical diagnosis.
  • Ensure accurate documentation on exams/requisitions (i.e., patient’s full name, chart number, date of birth and examinations performed, etc.).
  • Assess patient’s condition; ensure patient safety through proper use of table straps and other support devices.
  • Identify anatomical orientation on all required images and ensure proper film identification on all images.
  • Coordinate exams with other modalities in order to ensure patients are processed through the department as efficiently as possible.
  • When appropriate, case review with the Radiologist.
  • Screens the patient for possibility of pregnancy and performs pregnancy testing if applicable.
  • Responsible in reviewing radiology orders for completeness and accuracy.
  • Reviews patient history and supporting clinical data for medical necessity.
  • Takes steps to acquire additional information, if needed from the patient, ordering provider and/or Radiologist.
  • Demonstrates acceptable imaging quality standards by critiquing positioning, technical factors and alignment.
  • Review patient data for accuracy, quality and completeness.
  • Verify and transfer image data in PACS and provides necessary medical history and information for Radiologist interpretation.
  • Ensure patient, visitor and environmental safety.
  • Prevent excessive radiation doses to the patient and staff by utilizing A.L.A.R.A. and adhering to department policies.
  • Initiate applicable “incident reports” in the RLDatix system by the end-of-shift; and report incomplete and incorrect examinations to the oncoming shift and to the Radiology Manager.
  • Transport patients to other departments as needed.
  • Respond to on-call services in a timely manner.
  • Assist with quality and safety programs and ensure compliance with hospital accreditation requirements.
  • Participate in development and review program goals and objectives for the Radiology Department.
  • Assist with reviews on Radiology Services’ Quality Assurance program, which complies with CMS and conforms to FDIHB, Inc.’s Quality Assurance plan.
  • Maintain cooperative communication with other departments.
  • Communicate with Health Information Technology, when necessary to assure billing is timely and current.
  • Actively assist in supply inventory and ordering and maintain equipment assigned to the department.
  • Maintain accurate record on equipment preventive maintenance and quality control as necessary.
  • Maintain accurate Daily/Weekly/Monthly Quality Control (QC) reports.
  • Assist with invasive procedures and knowledge of these procedures.
  • Competent in sterile technique.
  • Attends/participates in all mandatory trainings.
  • Assists in the orientation, training, and documentation of the progress of radiologic technologists, contractors and/or students as assigned.
  • Responsible for maintaining imaging equipment and workplace environment including maintaining supply inventories and cleanliness/orderliness of work area.
  • Recognizes and reports malfunctions and services needed and reports service needs in a timely manner.
  • Performs other duties as assigned. Assists Physicians and Radiologists as needed.

MINIMUM MANDATORY QUALIFICATIONS

Experience:

  • Two (2) years of direct work experience. OR
  • Direct work experience through FDIHB, Inc.’s Computed Tomography (CT)
    Technologist training program.

Education:

  • Associate of Science (AS) degree in Radiologic Technology OR
  • Certificate of completion by an accredited radiology-training program and/or the U.S. Military Tri-Service Radiography Program.

Licensure/ Certifications:

  • Certified and Registered by the American Registry of Radiologic Technologists (ARRT) and must maintain ARRT credentials.
  • Active, unrestricted Computed Tomography (CT) Technologist Certification by the Arizona Department of Health Services (ADHS) and must maintain certification.
  • Active, unrestricted Computed Tomography (CT) Technologist Certification by the
    Arizona Department of Health Services (ADHS) and must maintain certification.
  • Valid American Heart Association (AHA) certification in Basic Life Support (BLS) and
    maintain certification.

Please email degree or transcripts to: vanessa.apachee@fdihb.org

NAVAJO/INDIAN PREFERENCE

FDIHB, Inc. is located within the Navajo Nation and, in accordance with Navajo Nation law, has implemented a Navajo/Indian Preference in Employment Policy. Pursuant to this Policy, applicants who meet the minimum qualifications for this position and who are enrolled members of the Navajo Nation will be given primary preference in hiring and employment for this position and members of other federally-recognized Indian tribes will be given secondary preference. Position Title:

Job Description:


This is a hybrid position offering significant work-from-home flexibility.



If this opportunity aligns with your strengths, background, and commitment to fostering inclusivity, we encourage you to apply! At Oregon Health Authority (OHA), we value diversity and encourage applicants from all backgrounds and experiences to help us build a stronger, more equitable future for all.


Opportunity Awaits, Apply Today! – Administrator for Program Integrity


The Oregon Health Authority (OHA) is seeking an experienced leader to serve as the Administrator for Program Integrity within the Office for Program Integrity (OPI). This highly visible position provides strategic leadership for OHA’s statewide program integrity, fraud, waste, and abuse (FWA), and Medicaid compliance operations. Reporting directly to the Chief Financial Officer, the Administrator is responsible for setting priorities, developing policies and performance objectives, and ensuring OPI operations support OHA’s mission, strategic goals, and federal and state requirements.


The Administrator leads a multidisciplinary team responsible for investigations, financial and compliance audits, data analytics, provider oversight, and Medicaid program integrity activities. This role serves as OHA’s leading authority on Medicaid FWA and is responsible for identifying emerging risks and trends, strengthening detection and investigation strategies, and using data and operational insights to improve program integrity. The Administrator also provides policy guidance to OHA leadership and ensures that program integrity activities promote responsible stewardship of Medicaid funds while supporting equitable access to health care.


A significant part of this role involves building and maintaining strong partnerships across Oregon and at the federal level. The Administrator serves as OHA’s primary liaison with organizations including the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), federal oversight agencies, the Oregon Department of Justice Medicaid Fraud Control Unit, the Secretary of State, other state agencies, contractors, health care providers, and community and industry partners. The position represents OHA in committees, task forces, and technical advisory groups and provides consultation, education, and technical assistance on Medicaid compliance and program integrity.


In addition to strategic and operational leadership, the Administrator oversees OPI’s budget, contracts, staffing, strategic planning, and performance management. The position manages a complex portfolio of program integrity activities within OHA’s approximately $21 billion annual operation and exercises significant independent decision-making authority. This is an opportunity for a collaborative and strategic leader to help protect public resources, strengthen the integrity of Oregon’s Medicaid system, and advance OHA’s commitment to health equity, transparency, accountability, and high-quality services for Oregonians.


For a full review of the position description, please Click Here

What We Are Looking For


Minimum Qualifications: These qualifications must be reflected in your application for consideration.


  • Five years of management experience; OR two years of management experience and a bachelor’s degree in a related field.


Desired Attributes: The following are desired attributes that we have identified as key to success for this role at OHA. These are the attributes we are looking for in our top candidate. If you have any of these, please let us know in your application.


  • Medicaid Program Integrity & Compliance: Demonstrated experience leading or managing Medicaid program integrity, regulatory compliance, fraud, waste, and abuse (FWA), audit, investigation, or oversight activities.
  • Strategic Leadership: Demonstrated experience providing strategic direction, establishing priorities, developing performance objectives, and leading complex programs or multidisciplinary teams toward organizational goals.
  • Fraud, Waste & Abuse Investigation: Experience overseeing or conducting complex investigations, audits, risk assessments, data analysis, or other activities designed to identify and address fraud, waste, abuse, overutilization, or program compliance concerns.
  • State & Federal Regulatory Collaboration: Demonstrated experience working with federal, state, or local regulatory, oversight, law enforcement, or government entities on compliance, program integrity, audit, or related matters.
  • Data-Driven Program Management: Experience using audits, research, analytics, performance measures, financial information, or other data to identify trends, assess risk, improve operations, and inform policy or management decisions.
  • Executive Communication & Stakeholder Engagement: Demonstrated ability to communicate complex regulatory, financial, operational, or compliance issues to executive leadership and build effective working relationships with diverse internal and external stakeholders.

Preference Statement: Preference may be given to candidates who possess the following job-related knowledge, skills, and abilities.


  • Preference may be given to candidates with seven (7) or more years of management experience
  • Bachelor's degree with a master's degree preferred
  • Preference may be given to candidates who possess demonstrated knowledge, skills, and abilities in fraud investigation, program integrity, regulatory compliance, and legal or administrative proceedings, including experience representing an organization in court or other formal proceedings, negotiating with defendants or involved parties, establishing and documenting credible allegations of fraud, and communicating complex investigative or compliance matters to legal counsel, executive leadership, regulatory agencies, and other stakeholders.

title: Fiber Lineman
description:
Position Summary:

Responsible for terminating and testing aerial and underground fiber optic systems, updating, and maintaining project tracking information such as production sheets, time sheets and customer required paperwork. Additional responsibilities include performing all aspects of the project in accordance with OSHA, Expanse Core Values, and customer requirements. The Fiber Technician will be responsible for prepping and splicing fiber optic cables. Deep knowledge of most fiber optic splice closures, OTDR testing, optical power meter and fiber identifier.

Essential Functions:

  • Prepping and fusion or mechanical splice SM and MM fiber optic cables, in both outdoor and indoor settings
  • Construct proper splice cases pressurized and non-pressurized, using all types and sizes of cable, including but not limited to grounding, bonding, isolation, slack storage, and sealing.
  • Able to perform a mid-sheath ring cut splice on both loose tube buffer and ribbon fiber.
  • Testing and troubleshooting fiber using an OTDR, optical power meter, tone meter, fiber identifier and scope.
  • Provide the OSP Engineers with detailed reports of field splicing activity.
  • Work flexible hours, after hours work which would include nights and weekends.
  • On call rotation responding and restoring services for emergency calls, responsible for being on the job at short notice to repair damaged cables until service is restored.
  • Review and interpret underground and aerial cable records in existing records, on maps or in the field.
  • Must be able to create materials list based on plans/scope of work, order, and compile materials for crew in advance of deployment.
  • Make precise recommendations for changes in running fiber optic cables or provide input into construction methodologies.
  • May be asked to participate in engineering, permit, and construction processes.
  • Perform all work as necessary to conform to quality control guidelines (includes compliance with requirements outlined in applicable regulations such as: OSHA, FCC, NESC and NEC, etc.; as well as following procedures as outlined in the Installation, Technical, Operations, and Safety Manuals, and Employee Handbook)
  • Clean, maintain, stock, and secure assigned vehicles and equipment.
  • Basic computer skills including working knowledge of Microsoft Outlook, Teams, Word, and Excel
  • Perform other duties as requested by supervisor.

Non-Essential Functions:

  • Other duties as assigned.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities (KSAs)

Knowledge

  • Developing knowledge of electrical distribution and transmission systems.
  • Basic understanding of overhead and underground electrical construction.
  • Knowledge of electrical line equipment and components appropriate to apprenticeship level.
  • Developing understanding of primary and secondary electrical systems.
  • Knowledge of safe work practices associated with electrical line construction and maintenance.
  • Understanding of Health, Safety, and Environmental (HSE) procedures and guidelines.
  • Developing understanding of mechanical and electrical systems.
  • Knowledge of company policies, practices, and procedures as applicable to assigned responsibilities.

Skills

  • Electrical and mechanical aptitude.
  • Basic troubleshooting and diagnostic skills appropriate to apprenticeship level.
  • Ability to safely use hand tools, power tools, climbing equipment, and linework equipment.
  • Developing pole and structure climbing skills.
  • Basic math skills.
  • Clear verbal and written communication.
  • Organizational and time-management skills.
  • Attention to detail and quality.
  • Ability to follow instructions and established work procedures.
  • Ability to work effectively as part of a crew.

Abilities

  • Practice and promote safe work methods.
  • Identify workplace hazards and apply appropriate controls and PPE.
  • Work safely around energized and de-energized electrical systems within the employee's level of training and qualification.
  • Climb and work from wood, steel, and other applicable structures.
  • Establish and maintain effective working relationships with coworkers, supervisors, customers, and other personnel.
  • Accept instruction, coaching, and feedback from experienced personnel.
  • Learn and progressively perform more complex linework as apprenticeship training advances.
  • Handle multiple assigned tasks and priorities.
  • Find solutions to basic problems and appropriately escalate more complex issues.
  • Work a flexible schedule, including evenings, weekends, holidays, overtime, and emergency situations.
  • Respond to emergency restoration needs.
  • Read and interpret basic electrical drawings, schematics, maps, and technical information appropriate to apprenticeship level.
  • Maintain regular and timely attendance.
  • Travel for extended periods as required.

Physical Demands

  • Stand and walk for extended periods.
  • Push, lift, and carry up to 50 pounds.
  • Bend, stoop, kneel, reach, climb, and move throughout the workday.
  • Climb poles and structures and perform work at elevated heights.
  • Use fall-protection, climbing, and other required safety equipment.
  • Grasp and manipulate hand tools and linework equipment.
  • Perform physically demanding work for extended periods.
  • Work outdoors in extreme weather conditions, including heat, cold, rain, snow, and ice.
  • Work around fumes, odors, dust, moving mechanical equipment, vehicles, and other construction-related conditions.
  • Work in potentially hazardous electrical and industrial environments.
  • Ability to respond to emergency and storm-restoration conditions.

Minimum Education Requirements:

  • High school diploma or equivalent (GED)

Minimum Experience:

  • Must have completed all licensing requirements set by the State Regulations.
  • Must be able to obtain and maintain valid CDL Class A License

Other:

This position is safety sensitive. It is subject to pre-employment and/or periodic background checks, motor vehicle records (MVR) and drug testing.

Driving Requirements:

Must possess a valid driver's license, must be at least 21 years of age. Must maintain a satisfactory driving record to safely operate company vehicles.

Therefore, it is also not, nor can it be implied to be, a contract of employment. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential tasks. Must be able to successfully complete an intense background investigation.*

title: Profesional Sn. de Analítica de Compras / Remote / Bilingual
description:
At Iron Mountain we know that work, when done well, makes a positive impact for our customers, our employees, and our planet. That’s why we need smart, committed people to join us. Whether you’re looking to start your career or make a change, talk to us and see how you can elevate the power of your work at Iron Mountain.

We provide expert, sustainable solutions in records and information management, digital transformation services, data centers, asset lifecycle management, and fine art storage, handling, and logistics. We proudly partner every day with our 225,000 customers around the world to preserve their invaluable artifacts, extract more from their inventory, and protect their data privacy in innovative and socially responsible ways.

Are you curious about being part of our growth stor​y while evolving your skills in a culture that will welcome your unique contributions? If so, let's start the conversation.

Iron Mountain is seeking an analytical Senior Analyst: Procurement Analytics & Insights – GLOBAL to join our Global Procurement COE team.

As a key member of our Global Procurement Center of Excellence, you’ll have the opportunity to transform complex enterprise data into strategic insights that drive impactful business decisions. In this role, you’ll partner closely with Category Managers and Corporate Finance to optimize spend, validate P&L and EBITDA-level savings, and craft executive narratives for C-suite decision-makers. Here, your expertise will help build modern visual analytics and unleash hidden value across our global procurement ecosystem.


What You’ll Do (Responsibilities) In this role, you will:

  • Harmonize and structure spend data: Cleanse, model, and consolidate raw transactional data across ERPs (SAP, Oracle) and P2P platforms (Coupa, Ariba, ServiceNow) into a single source of truth.
  • Automate dashboards and advanced analytics: Design and manage intuitive BI dashboards, leveraging emerging AI tools and data pipelines to track core KPIs, cycle times, and predictive modeling.
  • Identify savings and category opportunities: Conduct deep-dive spend analyses to uncover tail-spend consolidation, volume leverage, and actionable sourcing pipeline priorities.
  • Validate EBITDA savings with Finance: Partner hand-in-hand with Corporate Finance and FP&A to audit, reconcile, and align realized cost reductions with business unit budgets.

What You’ll Bring

The ideal candidate will have:

  • 7 to 10 years of experience in procurement analytics, financial analysis, management consulting, or business intelligence.
  • Strong knowledge of SQL, BI platforms (Power BI, Tableau, Qlik), and data manipulation tools (Python, R, or advanced Excel/VBA).
  • Direct experience working with enterprise ERP/P2P data structures (Oracle, SAP S/4HANA, Coupa, SAP Ariba).
  • Advanced written and verbal English communication skills with executive presentation experience.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Data Analytics, Finance, Computer Science, Supply Chain Management, Economics, or a related quantitative field (Master's preferred).

What We Offer (Benefits)

  • Location: Colombia (Bogota), or Mexico
  • Competitive compensation and benefits aligned with experience.
  • Flexible work options/alternative work options to support work–life balance.
  • Comprehensive health, wellness, and retirement plans.
  • Opportunities for continuous learning and professional growth.

If you are ready to explore your potential and turn complex data into strategic impact, apply today to join our team at Iron Mountain!

description:
Job Description

Kraft Heinz is home to some of the world's most iconic brands — and this role puts you at the center of elevating creative across 70+ North American brands. As a direct creative partner to brand teams across the portfolio, you'll help shape the work that millions of consumers experience every day, at a company that has staked its reputation on pushing creative boundaries and raising the bar for what great looks like.


Champion Creative Effectiveness (15%)

  • Drive visibility, adoption, and cultural momentum for Kraft Heinz’s ACE (Accelerating Creative Effectiveness) program in North America.

  • Advance creative effectiveness through tools, routines, inspiration, shared standards and governance, making it an expected outcome of how we work.
  • Upskilling brand teams through L&D, guidelines & frameworks

Embedded creative and comms support for BU brand teams (70%)

  • Establish, own and continuously refine a new embedded support model for BU brand teams, shaping how it's rolled out and embedded across the organization to scale creative effectiveness across 24+ brands.
  • Provide embedded support across key moments including brand foundations, brand tune-ups, IAT immersion sessions, briefing and creative development, driving stronger briefs, more effective agency partnership and stronger creative output.
  • Build the capability of BU brand teams by providing hands-on support, advice and troubleshooting, influencing outcomes without taking ownership away from the teams themselves.
  • Lead and develop a high-performing team, setting clear expectations and creating the coaching and development needed for individuals to grow in confidence, capability and impact.
  • Act as the brand communications specialist within the Creative function, serving as a subject matter expert and setting the standard for what great looks like across brand communications work.
  • Report directly to the VP, Creative, and work as part of the Creative leadership team, aligning closely to the function's priorities, ways of working and ambitions to support the success of the team.

Build creative community and reputation (15%)

  • Foster a creative culture rooted in bravery, inclusivity, and consumer connection.
  • Celebrate the impact of great creative; Raise the profile and visibility of creative work across the org.
  • Partner with Corporate Comms and PR teams to shape our creative reputation and storytelling externally.
  • Inspire through thought leadership, learning moments, and partnerships with external creative leaders.

Expected skills & qualifications

  • Curious, courageous, collaborative and strategic leader passionate about the power of brand, communications & consumer experience to impact strategic direction of business.
  • Minimum of 10 years of hands-on experience, including client and/or agency side positions.
  • Proven track record of driving creative excellence, innovation, effectiveness and impact.

  • Exceptional strategic thinking and problem-solving abilities. Ability to create and execute practical plans to achieve strategic objectives.

Otis is seeking a Cybersecurity Architect, Director to play a pivotal role in shaping the future of cybersecurity across our global organization. This is an opportunity to bring deep technical expertise and strategic thinking to a highly visible role, helping define how security is designed into the systems, products, applications, and technologies that support Otis today and into the future.

As Otis continues to accelerate the digitization of its products and systems, you will help develop innovative security architectures that protect critical systems and data across cloud, hybrid-cloud, and enterprise environments. You will work at the intersection of Enterprise Security and Product Security, helping translate evolving cybersecurity challenges into scalable, forward-looking solutions.

In this role, you will have the opportunity to influence Otis’ global security vision and architecture, partner with key stakeholders across the organization, and help ensure security remains foundational to how Otis designs and delivers technology.

This Director-level position is primarily a strategic individual contributor role, ideal for an accomplished cybersecurity architect who wants to remain close to the technology while having the scope and influence to drive meaningful change across a global enterprise. The role reports to the Sr. Director, Cyber Product and Architecture.



On a typical day you will:


  • Design and develop security architectures for enterprise systems, cloud- and hybrid-based systems across all types including Infrastructure, Platform and Software as a Service (IaaS/PaaS/SaaS)
  • Review enterprise security solution architectures at the nexus between Enterprise security and Product Security
  • Design and implement secure architectures and designs (based on business requirements) that will allow those requirements to be met with a minimal degree of risk to the organization and with appropriate security controls present

  • Develop security standards while working in partnership with Engineering, Infrastructure Services and Application Development organizations to choose appropriate technology solutions, and facilitates complete integration into the company environments
  • Identify, recommend, coordinate and deliver timely knowledge to support teams regarding security technologies, processes or tools
  • Partner with other leaders across the business to identify opportunities and risks and deliver solutions that support business strategies while protecting intellectual property globally
  • Develop and execute strategies to increase security knowledge throughout the enterprise
  • Consult with other Otis Digital Technology teams and functional departments to identify and remediate risk and legacy systems, and improves processes and procedures which support the transition efforts

  • Bachelor’s or advanced degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, or a related field, or equivalent relevant professional experience
  • One relevant cybersecurity certification, such as CISSP, CISA, CISM, CCSK, or an equivalent credential, is preferred

  • 10+ years of experience in IT architecture and/or engineering, with a strong focus on cybersecurity

  • Demonstrated ability to influence and build consensus across business and technology stakeholders, translating complex security considerations into practical solutions and successful outcomes
  • Proven ability to deliver results, navigate complex challenges, and drive progress against ambitious business and technology objectives
  • Experience partnering directly with designers, developers, and Quality Assurance (QA) teams to design, build, and continuously improve digital products and services
  • Strong understanding of the full software development lifecycle (SDLC), including application architecture and deployment
  • Demonstrated ability to effectively manage quality, priorities, timelines, and scope within complex technology environments
  • Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills, with the ability to communicate complex technical concepts effectively across all levels of an organization
  • Strong planning, organizational, and prioritization skills, with the ability to adapt and manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment
  • Experience leading or managing small- and large-scale technical projects or programs
  • A highly accountable, disciplined, and quality-focused approach to delivering work
  • Ability to work independently and effectively in a remote environment
  • Ability to travel up to 10% as business needs require

  • A strong desire to learn and a proactive, problem-solving attitude.

Big West Oil's summer internship program provides full-time students with the opportunity to gain hands-on experience and develop real-world skills. From May to August, you'll work alongside seasoned professionals who will mentor you, providing the guidance and practical training you need to become an effective, well-rounded professional.

Position Overview:
Big West Oil is seeking applicants to join our Summer 2026 Internship Program. This internship offers the opportunity to work on value-added engineering projects that support continuous improvement, operational reliability, and process safety across our facility. The intern may work in one or more of the following engineering disciplines:

  • Process Engineering - Focuses on optimizing the day-to-day operation of chemical process units to maximize production, improve efficiency, and ensure product quality.
  • Process Controls Engineering- Involves designing, implementing, and day-to-day management of automated systems that use sensors and control loops to manage the stability and performance of plant operations in real-time.
  • Process Safety Engineering- Using engineering principles to prevent and control catastrophic incidents like fires, explosions, and toxic releases in industrial facilities, using the 14 elements of PSM
  • Economics and Planning- Forecasting market demands, analyzing process profitability, and optimizing long-term production plans to maximize the refinery's financial performance.

As an intern, you’ll collaborate with experienced engineers, gain exposure to real-world refining operations, and contribute to projects that enhance refinery performance and sustainability.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Support engineering teams with data collection, performance monitoring, and root cause analysis.
  • Contribute to projects focused on improving safety, energy efficiency, and unit optimization.
  • Assist in updating and reviewing PFDs, P&IDs, and control logic diagrams.
  • Participate in unit troubleshooting, safety reviews, and economic evaluations.
  • Prepare and deliver a final presentation summarizing your internship experience and project contributions.
  • Follow all safety procedures and participate in safety meetings and audits.

Qualifications:

  • Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s degree in Chemical Engineering (Junior or Senior standing preferred, all others welcome).
  • Strong academic background in core engineering principles and problem-solving.
  • Interest in refining, process systems, or energy-related industries.
  • Effective communication and teamwork skills.
  • Self-motivated, detail-oriented, and able to work independently.

What You'll Gain:

  • Hands-on experience in a dynamic, real-world refinery environment.
  • Exposure to refinery operations, project engineering, and technical analysis.
  • Mentorship from experienced engineers and professionals.
  • Networking opportunities with our sister companies.
  • Development of technical, professional, and leadership skills.
  • A deep understanding of how engineering supports safe and efficient fuel production.

About Big West Oil LLC.:

Owned and operated by FJ Management, Big West Oil believes employees are the key to success. The facility currently employs about 270 people, with an average employee tenure of 12 years. Employees at Big West Oil LLC take pride in creating lasting value. Big West Oil is one of five Utah refineries that produce gasoline, diesel, and other chemicals. We take pride in being industry leaders in environmental compliance, and we are passionate about fostering a family-oriented culture that supports employee fulfillment and career growth.

description:
Job Description

As a core member of the Intelligence Operations Center (IOC) within the broader Resiliency Center, the Intelligence Analyst applies analytical tradecraft to identify, assess, and forecast security risks that could impact our Company’s people, assets, and operations.


While intelligence analysis is the foundational function of this role, the successful candidate will be assigned to diverse, rotating portfolios based on dynamic business needs. These portfolios encompass analyzing complex geopolitical developments (such as political instability and regional conflicts), protective intelligence, insider risk, and a wide-range of issues impacting the safety of our employees, facilities, and other assets.


By transforming raw data from various threat streams into clear, actionable insights, this agile analyst empowers business leaders to make informed decisions and ensure our Company operates safely across the globe.

  • Provide dedicated analytical support to the Resiliency Center’s 24/7 watch desk and incident management teams during emerging global crises or targeted threat escalations.

  • Experience producing analytical reports and briefings for stakeholders.
  • Experience conducting OSINT investigations and analysis.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience working within a global enterprise environment.
  • Specific experience in one or more intelligence disciplines (e.g., geopolitical risk, insider risk, counterintelligence, protective intelligence).
  • Foreign language proficiency.

Skills & Competencies:

  • Foundational mastery of intelligence tradecraft, structured analytical techniques, and objective reporting standards.
  • Adaptability and intellectual curiosity, with the ability to rapidly learn and pivot across distinct subject matter portfolios.
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills.
